title: Saudi Arabia flight cancellations: Which airlines are suspending services and until when?
description: UAE and other international services remain suspended despite airport reopening
content: Flight cancellations across Saudi Arabia continue as airlines extend suspensions amid continuing regional tension and attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels . Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has partially reopened following its closure earlier this month, but international services remain disrupted. The airport is operating terminals 1 and 2 from October 25. Terminal 1 is designated for domestic flights, with Terminal 2 operating international flights. Etihad Airways has extended cancellations on routes to Riyadh and Dammam into November, while flydubai and Emirates has suspended several Saudi services until October 29. Here is how major airlines have adjusted their operations and when flights are expected to resume. Etihad Airways Etihad Airways has cancelled flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until November 5 owing to the regional disruption. All services to and from Riyadh and Dammam are affected, along with four Jeddah services – EY601, EY602, EY603 and EY604. Emirates Emirates has updated its online flight schedules for routes operating to Saudi airports. The airline will resume flights between Dubai and Jeddah on October 30, with EK801, EK805 and EK803 scheduled to fly to King Abdulaziz International Airport, and EK802, EK806 and EK804 due to operate the return legs to Dubai. Flights to both King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are due to resume on November 8. Flights EK815, EK819 and EK817 are all due to operate from Dubai to Riyadh daily, with EK816, EK820 and EK818 returning. To Damman, the airline will fly EK823, EK827 and EK821 and EK824, EK828 and EK822 returning. The airline's services to Medina Prince Mohammad Bin Abdulaziz Airport continue to operate. Flydubai The airline has cancelled flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Abha up to October 29. From October 30, it will operate two daily flights to Riyadh: FZ847 and FZ855, with FZ848 and FZ856 returning. Four daily flights will resume to Damman: FZ883, FZ869, FZ863 and FZ867, with FZ884, FZ870, FZ864 and FZ868 returning. One route will operate to Abha: FZ813 and FZ814. Air Arabia Air Arabia has cancelled services between Sharjah and several Saudi destinations including Riyadh, Abha, Dammam and Taif. No resumption date has been announced. Qatar Airways The airline has temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh up to and including October 25. Meanwhile, its services to Jeddah have been reduced from seven daily flights to four. Flights to Damman remain suspended. Oman Air Oman Air has announced that all flights to and from Riyadh are suspended until October 31. SalamAir The Omani low-cost airline has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam until October 31, citing regional security developments. Air France The French airline has extended its suspension of flights to and from Riyadh up to and including November 14. British Airways British Airways is scheduled to return with a limited service to Riyadh on November 3, operating one flight daily, according to previously announced plans. The airline discontinued flights to Jeddah in April as part of wider changes to its Middle East operations. Air India and Air India Express Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam until November 7. Akasa Air The Indian low-cost airline has suspended flights to and from Riyadh until November 30 and Jeddah until November 10. Cathay Pacific The Hong Kong airline has extended its suspension of flights to Riyadh up to January 31, 2027. Pakistan International Airlines The airline announced a temporary suspension of flights to Riyadh on October 9, without setting out a resumption date. The Pakistan Airports Authority said at the time that its other Saudi services were continuing as usual. Delta Air Lines The US airline has postponed the launch of flights between Atlanta and Riyadh until March 2027. Services had been scheduled to begin on October 23. IndiGo The Indian airline has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah up to October 31. Lufthansa The German airline has suspended flights to Riyadh until November 18, extending its previously announced October 16 deadline. The Lufthansa Group’s advisory also lists Dammam services as suspended through November 30. Eurowings, part of the group, is scheduled to resume flights to Jeddah on November 12. KLM The Dutch airline has extended cancellations of all flights to Riyadh and Dammam up to October 31. Philippine Airlines The Philippine flag carrier has suspended Riyadh flights PR654 and PR655 until November 29, citing the security situation at King Khalid International Airport. Scoot The Singapore Airlines-owned low-cost carrier has cancelled flights between Singapore and Jeddah until December 2.

title: ‘Israel needs a dramatic change’: Northern voters turn against Netanyahu
description: Soldiers and residents in northern Israel want a new direction after years of conflict, economic damage and security failures
content: A “dramatic change” is needed in Israeli politics , which includes removing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from government, people living in northern Israel have told The National days before the country goes to the polls. Those who spoke included senior officers and soldiers who have been on active duty in Lebanon, who are angry over the damage caused by Hezbollah to the ecomomy and to Israeli communities. They called on Mr Netanyahu to take responsibility for the security failures of the October 7, 2023 attacks. After nearly 20 years in office his time was over, critics said, especially in view of the right-wing coalition that had, in their eyes, caused the country great harm. “For me, this is one of the worst coalitions that we have ever had in Israel,” said Eyal Dror, a lieutenant-colonel reservist in the army who just returned from a tour of Lebanon. “I pray and hope that there is a new government which makes this a very important election,” he said, speaking in Kibbutz Dafna, near the northern town of Kiryat Shmona. He believes a new government is needed to rebuild the country’s economy, especially in the north where nearly 70,000 people were evacuated for almost two years after a war with Hezbollah that followed the Hamas-led attacks on Israel. Opposition leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett were “very professional people who might lead us to that road”, Lt Col Dror said. A voter for the left-wing Democrats Party, Barry Praag, also from Kibbutz Dafna, said a coalition government was inevitable but it was vital for the new government to work with the Israeli-Arab parties to address the Palestinian question. “I have no problem with the Democrats sitting with the Arab parties. It is a very complex problem but it must be tackled. We must face the idea of a two-state solution with the support of the surrounding Arab countries otherwise, it won’t work.” He added that Mr Netanyahu had "a lot to answer” for and that the “buck stops with him”. Lior Shelef, speaking at Kibbutz Snir, which is only about a kilometre from the Lebanese border, was on military operations in the north for much of the last three years. He was still unsure who he would vote for – a position he believed was shared by many Israelis – but said the country certainly needed a new government. “Israel needs a change, and I think this change should be very dramatic. There are quite a lot of things in the country now, the economy, the religious people not going into the army, that need to change dramatically.” Anyone who was part of government on October 7, 2023 should “be honest enough to say it’s time for change and understand it”, he added. Hezbollah threat To many in the north, the Hezbollah threat has not disappeared, and they fear that the Iran-backed group across the border in Lebanon is biding its time to attack again. Lt Col Dror stated that for the Lebanese government to “get their own country back they need to do some more against Hezbollah” but it was only Israel that “can make them weaker”. But like many in the north, he said he wants to live in peace so that tourism can return, the economy can be revived, and his children can be educated. “As long as I have to send my son to the school, which is 600 metres from Lebanon and Hezbollah have the ability to fly a drone across the school I'm not feeling safe,” he said. While he hoped that the politics and diplomacy of a new Israeli government might achieve that, he did not dismiss the possibility of further military action. Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday night as part of the latest anti-government demonstration, with protesters calling for an inquiry into the failures surrounding the October 7 attack. Mr Eisenkot, the main rival to Mr Netanyahu, was greeted with cheers and chants from the crowd at the rally. Mr Netanyahu has refused to set up a commission of inquiry into the attack, arguing that it would be biased against his government.

title: El Clasico: Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid look to spring a surprise at Camp Nou
description: Los Blancos head into the game as underdogs as Catalan side look to make it 10 wins out of 10 in La Liga
content: Jose Mourinho returns to El Clasico on Sunday as his Real Madrid side take on Barcelona at Camp Nou, looking to close the gap on their fierce rivals at the top of La Liga. Barca have enjoyed a sensational start to the season, winning nine out of nine in the Spanish top-flight – scoring 39 goals in the process – including a 5-2 win at Real Betis last weekend. Madrid, meanwhile, hammered Sevilla 4-1 at the Bernabeu, which saw Kylian Mbappe score twice, lifting Mourinho's side to within a point of second-place Atletico Madrid, but still seven behind Barca. Mourinho, who will manage in his first Clasico since returning for a second spell as Los Blancos manager during the summer, will be without suspended attacker Vinicius Junior for a match in which his team are undoubtedly the underdogs. “The people who thought a week ago that Barca could thrash us still think the same now,” said the Portuguese, whose team defeated RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday to maintain their 100 per cent start in the Uefa Champions League. “I don't think that view will change. The fact that people speak highly of Barca doesn't affect me. To be honest, there are matches in which they obviously deserve plenty of praise because they do some very good things. “In our case, we're viewed as a finished product. Finished products are difficult to achieve in football. If you talk about us at an advanced stage of the process, we've been working for three months. If you exclude preseason and the international break, we've been working for a month and a half. Far from being a finished product, we're at the very beginning of the process. “Our manager is still getting to know the team, analysing things and establishing his approach. The players are still getting to know me, too. I don't think it's fair to compare a team like ours with one that has been together for longer.” Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the campaign on Tuesday when they lost to Champions League holders Paris Saint Germain 4-2 in a breathless clash at the Parc des Princes. “It was a fantastic game from both teams,” said manager Hansi Flick in Paris. “We made a few too many mistakes in possession. We have to analyse the game, but I also saw a lot great things. It was a great test for us today. We've seen what things we need to do better, and that's what we'll do. “What we've done over the last few weeks has been incredible. The attitude, the quality. We tried to play how we want to play, we pressed them very high. There were a lot of fantastic things on show today.” And now Flick's attention will be turned to Madrid and their wily coach, Mourinho, who will almost certainly relish being the villain of the piece for Barca fans. “I have a lot of respect for him,” said the German. “When you’ve managed for so many years and had so much success, it’s a testament to his talent. “When I was [Joachim] Low’s assistant, I met with him in Madrid. Every player who played under him speaks of him with great respect. He’s a colleague, and a very successful one at that. “They have players with great quality in the final third,” he added when asked about the threats his team will face from Mourinho's side. “They’ve shown that in recent matches. We have to be careful and prepared. “For us, the important thing is our positioning, with and without the ball. We need to maintain good distance between the lines and be compact. “This is important when playing with a high defensive line. [defenders Pau] Cubarsi and Gerard [Martin] are having a great season and they complement each other well; they are growing together.” While Barcelona's array of attacking talent in the likes of Lamine Yamal (eight goals and six assists), La Liga top-scorer Raphinha (12 goals and three assists) and summer signing Anthony Gordon (one goal and four assists) have been hogging the headlines, it was another recent arrival – midfielder Rodri from Manchester City – who has provided a bedrock for those forwards to blossom. “We always look at ourselves and the impact he has on Barca,” said Flick. “When the opportunity arose to sign him, we were all convinced he would improve us. He was a piece to take the next step,” he said. “We’ve seen that in the first few matches. I’m very happy he’s here. Alongside Pedri, there’s great quality in midfield. We’re all happy with him.”

title: iPhone Duo buyers complain of cracks and display failures after just days of use
description: Some users report lines and dead pixels on the foldable display
content: Apple is facing complaints of damaged screens on its newly launched iPhone Duo , with some early buyers reporting cracks and display failures only hours after using the company’s first foldable smartphone. Images shared on Reddit appear to show damage concentrated around the hinge of the device’s inner display, with vertical cracks running down the centre and bright lines extending across the right side of the screen. Some affected devices also reportedly have dead pixels, raising concerns about the durability of the foldable display, which is one of the phone’s biggest selling points. The complaints come as the iPhone Duo officially goes on sale, following strong pre-order demand that saw initial stocks sell out rapidly and delivery dates for some customers pushed into next year. The Duo's prices in the UAE range from Dh8,499 to Dh13,599, and there are extended shipping times due to overwhelming demand. Dang these iPhone Duo screens can't be fixed til January! 😂💀💀💀 pic.twitter.com/ZsZX5l42mp — TexasTSLA (@TexasTSLA) October 24, 2026 Apple has reportedly been providing replacement devices to some affected customers despite limited retail inventory. However, a customer who received a broken Duo in the US said in a post on X that T-Mobile said it couldn’t replace any parts for the Duo until January. The iPhone maker is also reportedly planning to send damaged units to its engineering teams in California for examination to determine what caused the failures and whether changes are needed in future models. However, the extent of the problem remains unclear, and it is not known whether reports of broken Duo screens indicate a widespread manufacturing or design defect. The complaints add to the challenges Apple faces as it enters a foldable smartphone market already occupied by Samsung and Google, both of which have several years' experience developing devices with flexible displays.

title: UFC 333: Volkanovski weighs up options as he and Yan retain titles after night of Abu Dhabi brilliance
description: Australian beats Evloev to cement status as greatest featherweight champion while Yan wins Dvalishvili trilogy epic
content: Two champions walked into Abu Dhabi on Saturday. By Sunday morning, both had left with their title belts still wrapped firmly around their waists. Alexander Volkanovski cemented his place as the greatest featherweight in history with a TKO victory over Movsar Evloev at UFC 333, while Petr Yan retained his bantamweight belt with a unanimous decision over Merab Dvalishvili. Volkanovski had promised his wife he would not make her suffer on the sidelines at Etihad Arena, and the Australian was as good as his word with a second-round stoppage of Evloev. “It feels good to get a finish. I actually promised the missus – it was our wedding anniversary on Wednesday – I promised her a quick one so she wasn't stressing on the sidelines, so there you go.” Evloev looked way out of his league as he suffered the first defeat of his 21-fight career. Volkanovski looked better than ever. “He’s a great fighter. He was undefeated for a reason, but I just said I’m the right guy for that job,” Volkanovski said. Evloev conceded it was a “terrible fight” but that he was grateful to have shared a cage with the champion. “He’s a good one. Older, stronger, better, he’s truly a legend. I’m grateful for this opportunity to be here. Alex … great champion.” It was billed as striker against grappler. Volkanovski had encouraged Evloev to stick to his wrestling, saying no one could take him down, let alone keep him there. The Russian put that to the test three times in the opening round. The champion was up to the task every time. Evloev went to the well again in the second. Volkanovski showed the cunning of a fox in reversing it, proving he is no slouch on the ground either. It didn’t take long for Volkanovski to find his rhythm on his feet. He sliced Evloev open with a sledgehammer left hand that dropped the Russian. Volkanovski smelt blood, and after some vicious ground-and-pound that rendered Evloev helpless, the fight was waved off. COOKED HIM 😎 @AlexVolkanovski closes out #UFC333 with a RD2 finish! [ LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/noP5sd8ISz — UFC (@ufc) October 24, 2026 “I knew the ref would have to stop it when he covered up like that,” Volkanovski said, adding that he had no plans to retire after extending his record to 29 wins against four losses. “I’m choosing to do this. I said if I didn’t take too much damage, we probably keep going, so maybe we keep going.” Victory meant Volkanovski, 38, surpassed the great Jose Aldo for the most title wins in the featherweight division, with nine. “I don't really care about this,” he said, pointing to his belt, one that he has now defended six times across his two title reigns. “I really don't. “I just care about overcoming challenges. A guy that was undefeated in front of me, to overcome that and beat him, and again, getting through camps, means so much more to me.” The question now turns to who is next. Volkanovski says he has no plans to retire while also suggesting he could step up a division to fight lightweight champion Justin Gaethje, with the loser calling time on their career. Jean Silva or the winner of the bout between Aljamian Sterling and Kevin Vallejos is also a potential opponent at 145 pounds. “I guess we've just got to weigh the options. I’m in a pretty good position when you’ve got the president [ Dana White ] saying that you could pretty much do whatever you want.” Yan and Dvalishvili's epic third fight If the main event was a mismatch, the co-main event was an epic. Yan-Dvalishvili 3 lived up to its billing, with two of the greatest bantamweights delivering a fight for the ages. The head-to-head record read one win apiece, with the previous encounter seeing Yan dethrone Dvalishvili as bantamweight champion. The Russian took his time to get going, forced to fend off the relentless Georgian’s takedown attempts for the first two rounds. When he did let his hands go midway through the third round, they found their mark. Dvalishvili was slowed by punishing combinations and body shots that took the wind out of his sails. All three judges gave it to Yan, much to the delight of the crowd, who clearly backed the Russian. Debate's over 🫳 @PetrYanUFC puts on an instant classic to retain his belt! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/wFfqFYrsCS — UFC (@ufc) October 24, 2026 “I’m really happy about the way the fight went, about getting the victory, about being able to do it in front of all of these fans that came out to support me,” Yan said. “It's an incredible feeling. I feel great.” Dvalishvili’s game plan was clear from the outset: to continually shoot at the champion. He scored a few towards the end of the first round, with Yan unable to set himself or fire anything in return. The second round followed much the same pattern, with Dvalishvili shooting at every opportunity. He took Yan down several times, although the champion was quickly back to his feet. Dvalishvili began the third energetically, but was left wincing from a punishing kick to the liver. It was a tactic that served Yan well in their second fight in December. Dvalishvili backed off and attempted to shake it off, but it gave Yan confidence, and his punches started to find their target more frequently. Round four saw the pendulum swing in Yan’s favour. Dvalishvili’s takedown attempts lacked conviction, with Yan easily able to fend them off. His striking accuracy proved decisive, with his left hand, in particular, finding the mark at will. Yan closed out the fight strongly, landing pummeling combinations punctuated by one flying knee that busted open Dvalishvili's forehead. On weathering Dvalishvili’s early storm, Yan said: “Diamonds are made under extreme pressure. I could have just given up, but I had to go through it. This is what I do.” For Dvalishvili, it was a second successive defeat to Yan. “The Machine” never stopped coming forward but again had no answer to the champion’s superior striking. “I can do better,” he said. “Congratulations to Petr Yan. He beat me today; he’s the better man. Congratulations to him.”

title: Sultan Sooud Al Qassemi on art: How an Egyptian weaving village became a lesson in the power of giving
description: What we can learn from Garya Mahmoud's The Fields and the Village
content: A busy village scene in the Upper Egyptian Delta depicts a crowd of men harvesting corn and placing it on the backs of animals of burden, while women look after the children nearby. In the bottom-left corner, four men gather around a fire, possibly hinting that the scene is set in the autumn months, coinciding with the end of the corn harvest season in Egypt. The background is peppered with dome-topped houses, palm trees and birds. This scenic tapestry was created by Garya Mahmoud, one of the Ramses Wissa Wassef Art Centre’s first-generation weavers. The centre was founded by the prominent architect Ramses Wissa Wassef and his wife, Sophie Habib Gorgi, in 1951, and it initially employed 45 women and men in weaving, stoneware and batik painting. Ramses was behind several major projects, such as the Mahmoud Mokhtar Museum, opened in Cairo in 1962, and a string of churches and private residences across Egypt. Through the art centre, Ramses and Sophie envisioned a unique space that would give others opportunities that would allow them to earn a livelihood. In a 2018 interview with Masrawy , Sophie, recalling the conversation that prompted the creation of the centre, stated: “One day [Ramses] said to me, 'Why don’t we look for a simple village with quiet people and start a project that brings the place to life and helps the villagers learn something different?'” That village would be Harraniya, 15km south-west of central Cairo, not far from the Giza Pyramids. The couple could have simply opted for charity, but they chose to empower this “simple village” and “bring the place to life”, an act that embodies the proverb “give a person a fish and you feed them for a day; teach them how to fish and you feed them for a lifetime”. This spirit of generosity, selflessness and encouragement towards independence must be celebrated and commended whether it comes from an individual, a corporation or a country. The Arab Gulf states, too, have historically been among the most generous in terms of global aid. For instance, the Kuwait Fund for Development was founded in 1961 under Emir Sheikh Abdullah, as the world’s first development fund established by a developing country. Since its founding, it has extended loans to build schools and other infrastructure in more than 100 countries, continuing work even during Kuwait’s occupation in 1990-1991. Similarly, the UAE has been one of the world’s most generous countries relative to its size, contributing 0.61 per cent of its GDP, according to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, to developing and disaster-stricken nations. Last November, the UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs ranked the UAE as the third-largest donor of humanitarian aid globally for 2025, after the US and the EU. Since its founding in 1971, the UAE has delivered close to $100 billion in foreign aid, and today it is the world’s largest humanitarian donor to Gaza, providing $3.9 billion in aid, or close to half the global assistance, including the building of field hospitals and desalination plants. That said, not all acts of kindness are measured in billions or even millions of dollars. Often, small acts of generosity go a long way and lead to lifelong bonds. Mahmoud developed a close friendship with the founders, and when their daughter Suzanne, herself a stoneware ceramic designer, became engaged in 1972, the weaver created a tapestry to celebrate the occasion, depicting the couple and other family members. Since its establishment, scores of artisans and artists have benefitted from the Ramses Wissa Wassef Centre, and some, such as Mahmoud’s own daughter, Naglaa, have continued the legacies of their mothers and fathers long after they were gone. Today, tapestries from the centre are collected globally, and have appeared at auctions in Lebanon, the US, the UK and Sweden. The precedents set by Ramses and Sophie in 1951, Kuwait in 1961 and the UAE since 1971 are examples for us all. Giving back to our communities, whether it is at the state, corporate or individual level, should not merely be seen as an act of charity and kindness, but rather as a long-term investment in less-developed parts of our communities that can potentially bring the place to life.

title: What does luxury sound like? Inside the growing world of sonic branding
description: From the sounds inside Ferrari’s first electric car to a bespoke piano built for a Danish bank, brands are paying closer attention to what we hear
content: Those fortunate enough to own Ferrari’s new all-electric Luce may be preoccupied with whether the supercar can retain the Italian manufacturer’s famed engine sound. But listen more closely and it becomes clear that just as much thought has gone into the sounds inside the cabin, as Emmy-winning composer Nick Wood knows well. “From the engine start to indicators and warning tones, these are very simple noises. But they had to have a Ferrari feel to them, not sound generic like your open fridge door,” says Wood, who designed what he calls the Luce’s “sonic universe”. Every sound the car makes is the product of live recordings of organic sounds – from pianos and cellos to banging wood on pipework and the growl of vintage Ferraris – manipulated in the British composer’s Tokyo studio. “The importance of sound can come across as so nebulous that it can be hard to validate,” says Wood. “Brands are unsure about how to approach it. They’re all about cool video but have, until recently, no consistent identity for the way they sound. But, from product sounds – like those the Luce makes – to the music played at events, the idea of what’s called sonic branding is something more of them are waking up to.” Wood, one of the field’s pioneers, has worked with Chanel, Fiat, Uniqlo, Apple and the spa at Claridge’s hotel, and writes pieces of sound lasting anywhere from a second or two to several hours. Of course, the idea that brands should associate themselves with a sound is nothing new. Russell Boiarsky of Texas-based Stephen Arnold Music, which has worked on sonic identities for Airbnb, CNN and UPS, points out that the first radio jingle, for General Mills’ Wheaties cereal, was broadcast in Minneapolis a century ago this year. “But the difference is that jingles were meant to be earworms that you couldn’t forget whether you liked them or not, which is not always a positive thing. Sonic branding is about expressing the values of a brand through sound,” he explains. Think of Netflix’s start-up “ta-dum”, which suggests drama and a sense of occasion, or McDonald’s “I’m Lovin’ It” riff, designed to evoke fun and positivity. “The challenges,” Boiarsky adds, “are that it’s already a noisy world, so brands don’t want to bombard their customers with yet more.” There is already talk of a “sound-off economy”, in which more people keep their devices silent. “And audiences are already stretched thin for attention, so brands may have less than a couple of seconds to cut through.” When sonic branding succeeds, however, studies suggest it can be remarkably effective. Hearing is among the fastest senses our brain processes, while sound is closely connected to emotion and memory. As Wood points out, sounds can stay with us long after imagery has been forgotten – allowing a brand associated with them to resonate too. Repetition helps embed that association, but fewer iterations may be required than imagined: if a sound is well designed, as few as five exposures can be enough. And if the idea of a brand having a sound as much as a look still seems somewhat woolly, research is putting the effectiveness of this approach on a more scientific footing. “Brands are excited to hear that there is science behind this, that it’s not just witchcraft,” says Boiarsky with a laugh. Stephen Arnold Music works with UK-based SoundOut, a platform specialising in music testing and sonic brand analysis, to establish how closely a sonic logo or track matches a brand’s personality, its emotional impact and how distinctive it is. The company’s annual benchmark study tracks recognition and recall of sonic brands, while the company is now working with AI models to map particular kinds of sounds to certain feelings. “I don’t see that [insight] being used aggressively or to manipulate,” Boiarsky says – not, at least, in the way background “muzak” has been said to influence consumer choices or worker behaviour in shops and factories. Instead, he sees artificial intelligence as a starting point for a composer’s creativity, much as it can now generate a potential hit song that may lack the human element required for longevity. That is why, although sonic branding can be developed using synthesisers, Stephen Arnold Music often records with orchestras in pursuit of a more authentic sound. The human touch matters personally, too: both Wood and Boiarsky are recording artists in their own right. It is an approach shared by Unmute, a Copenhagen-based “creative sound agency”, which devised the sound logo for Imax cinemas globally. The team have spent the past year developing a new sonic identity for Danske Bank, which is now being rolled out. To create something that felt suitably Nordic for Denmark’s largest retail bank without sounding generic, Unmute even commissioned a bespoke piano using inherently intuitive audio cues. Built with two strings for every note, rather than the standard range of one to three, it produces what the agency describes as a “cleaner” sound. The instrument now stands in the lobby of the bank’s headquarters. “The work here is to translate a brand into meaningful sound, which will become part of that brand for years to come, so actually it’s a very big decision, rather like changing a logo,” explains Unmute co-founder and sonic director Simon Kringel. Sound may only have come to be regarded as a fundamental part of a brand’s ecosystem in the past five years or so, but Kringel believes its importance will continue to grow as our lives become increasingly digital. It is no coincidence that some of the most recognisable examples of sonic branding belong to technology companies such as Google and Nintendo, which have had a head start. “The move from print to digital platforms, and the fact that the way we interact with so many brands now is through websites and increasingly ‘gamified’ apps, means that the opportunity for sound is there, as well as the need for a sonic identity and user-friendliness,” says Kringel. “The questions for any brand to understand are: ‘How do we sound as a company?’, ‘How do we sound different from our competitors?’ and ‘How can people make a connection to us when they’re only listening?’”

title: UFC 333: Volkanovski makes history and keeps his promise with TKO win over Evloev
description: Australian retains featherweight title while Petr Yan beats Merab Dvalishvili in a fight-of-the-year contender at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi
content: Alexander Volkanovski made good on his promise of an early finish to beat Movsar Evloev inside two rounds in Abu Dhabi to cement his place as the greatest featherweight in UFC history. The Australian had promised his wife Emma that he would not make her suffer on the sidelines at UFC 333 by finishing Evloev early as a belated anniversary present, and he was as good as his word. Evloev, an elite wrestler, took Volkanovski down three times in the first round, but each time the champion was quickly back to his feet. An uppercut and a straight left rocked Evloev in the second. The Russian went to ground, and Volkanovski didn't waste the opportunity, pummeling his opponent with vicious ground-and-pound to finish the fight. The victory meant Volkanovski, 38, surpassed Jose Aldo for the most title wins in the featherweight division with nine wins. The legend lives on 🏆 @AlexVolkanovski defeats Movsar Evloev by TKO to remain as the featherweight champion of the world! [ #UFC333 | B2YB @ThorneHealth ] @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi pic.twitter.com/OgbVqgguLM — UFC (@ufc) October 24, 2026 Petr Yan settled his trilogy bout with Merab Dvalishvili with a unanimous victory at UFC 333 to retain the bantamweight title as Abu Dhabi witnesses a fight-of-the-year contender. The champion took his time to get going, constantly defending the relentless Georgian's takedown attempts through the first two rounds. A kick to the liver in Round 3 changed the momentum of the contest in the champion's favour. From there on, Yan picked off Dvalishvili at will, patted off ineffective takedowns and connected with combinations that had the challenger wincing. Dvalishvili simply had no answer to Yan's superior striking, and Yan settled their trilogy with his second win over the Georgian after dethroning him for the title back in December. Debate's over 🫳 @PetrYanUFC puts on an instant classic to retain his belt! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/wFfqFYrsCS — UFC (@ufc) October 24, 2026 Lone’er Kavanagh gave Ramazan Temirov a taste of his own medicine with a sensational first-round finish. The English flyweight caught the Uzbek with a beautiful left uppercut that sent Termirov reeling. Kavanagh waited for his opponent to get back to his feet before wading in with several crunching blows, after which the referee stepped in. PICTURE PERFECT 😍 Lone’er Kavanagh lands the flush uppercut as he leaves with the RD1 TKO win! @VisitAbuDhabi | @InAbuDhabi | #InAbuDhabi [ #UFC333 | LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/93NAPEZL1L — UFC (@ufc) October 24, 2026 Alexander Volkov picked up the 41 st win of his pro MMA career with a unanimous decision over Rizvan Kuniev. The giant Russian heavyweight, celebrating his 38 th birthday, controlled the distance and landed some punishing kicks throughout the three-round contest. Volkov, 38, repeated his request to Dana White for a title shot. It remains to be seen whether the UFC president grants his request after next month’s title fight between champion Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit. Aaron Pico kicked off the main card with a first-round stoppage of Losene Keita. The American featherweight had the Belgian in trouble with an early takedown before rocking him with a right hand that sent Keita to the canvas. Pico pounced, peppering his opponent with pot shots before the referee waved off the fight.

title: Arsenal go level at top of Premier League with Man City after easing to win over Everton
description: Gunners secure 2-0 victory in the pouring rain at the Emirates Stadium thanks to goals from Konsa and Gabriel
content: Arsenal moved to level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League after a comfortable 2-0 win over Everton in the pouring North London rain on Saturday. After table-toppers City fell to their first league defeat of the season earlier in the day, when Enzo Maresca's side lost 2-1 at Aston Villa , reigning champions Arsenal made no mistake a few hours later at the Emirates Stadium. A goal in each half from Ezri Konsa and then Gabriel earned the Gunners all three points against a tepid Everton attacking performance and Arsenal move alongside City – but behind on goal difference – on 21 points from eight games. Victory came on the back of Arsenal's draining Uefa Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Tuesday when a late goal from Declan Rice had earned Mikel Arteta's team a battling point in Germany, but saw Bukayo Saka limp off with a thigh injury that could rule him out for six to eight weeks. “It is a great feeling to get the three points, it always is. A clean sheet and a goal; it is a fantastic day overall,” said Konsa. Ezri Konsa opens his account for @Arsenal , putting the home side ahead from a corner! ⚽️ #ARSEVE pic.twitter.com/LPdTyxVRyq — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he said he had been waiting for it as well. It was only right I got it today. A goal from a set-piece has felt like it has been coming and today was the day. “I’m pleased for Gabriel. He is a top player and a top human. He has made my life easy since I joined the club and it is a pleasure to play along side him. “I've come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It's not surprising to me. We are champions and to be champions you've got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.” The opening goal came after an almighty scramble in the Everton's box following Martin Odegaard's in-swinging corner which was eventually bundled home virtually on the goalline by Konsa. It was the England defender's first goal for the club following his summer switch from Aston Villa and, surprisingly, Arsenal's first from a set-piece this season. The second did not arrive until the 68th minute and this time it was Konsa's defensive partner Gabriel – in his 200th Premier League game – who scored it. A nice Arsenal move saw an interchange of short passes ending with substitute Bruno Guimaraes slotting a ball down the flank to Ben White, who was played onside by the away defence, and his cross into the box was headed home at the far post by his Brazilian teammate. Another goal for @Arsenal ! ⚽️ Ben White puts it on a plate for Gabriel to extend the home side's lead! #ARSEVE pic.twitter.com/BcQKksq2DN — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 Next up for Arsenal will an away day at fourth-tier Fleetwood Town in the League Cup last-16 on Tuesday, followed by a trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool next weekend. Everton have now won just once in seven league matches but remain in the top half of the table, although that could change if results go against them on Sunday. They now face a double-header against Newcastle United, starting with Thursday's League Cup tie on Merseyside, followed b “Ultimately two set-pieces have cost us,” said Everton captain James Tarkowski. “I thought we did all right. We created a few chances ourselves but it feels disappointing – the second one especially was a suckerpunch. “The minimum is leaving everything out there. That is what the fans and the club expect of us. There was quality at times and we could have scored one. I’ve had much tougher games here but the three points doesn’t go our way.”

title: UFC 333: What time is Volkanovski v Evloev and rest of the main card in Abu Dhabi?
description: Etihad Arena to host two title fights including bantamweight championship between Yan and Dvalishvili
content: Abu Dhabi hosts its 24th UFC show on Saturday, October 24, when Alexander Volkanovski defends his featherweight title against Movsar Evloev in the headline bout of UFC 333. A stacked card also includes a trilogy bout between Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili, with Yan putting his bantamweight title on the line. Here is everything you need to know. What is it? UFC 333 is a mixed martial arts event from the UFC. The event will be headlined by the UFC featherweight champion Volkanovski putting his belt on the line against Evloev. The card will feature 14 fights. Where is it? Fight night will be held at Etihad Arena on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi . It will be the 12th UFC event staged at the venue. When is it? UFC 333 takes place on Saturday, October 24. The preliminary card is scheduled to begin around 6pm UAE time, with the main card expected to start around 10pm. Who are the headline fighters? Volkanovski is widely regarded as one of the best featherweights in history. The Australian won the vacant title with a dominant performance over Diego Lopes in April 2025 and backed that up with a similar display in their rematch in February, winning both by unanimous decision. This is Volkanovski's second run as UFC featherweight champion . In total, this will be his sixth title defence and his 11th straight title fight. Top-ranked Evloev earned his shot at gold after taking a contentious decision over Lerone Murphy in March. The Russian is undefeated in 20 pro- MMA bouts, while Volkanovski's record stands at 28 wins against four losses – twice to Islam Makhachev, once to Ilia Topuria and a defeat earlier in his career to Corey Nelson. Who is on the rest of the card? The co-main event will see Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili play out their trilogy in Abu Dhabi. Yan (20-5) arrives in the UAE as UFC bantamweight champion, having dethroned Dvalishvili when they last met in December 2025. The Russian's consummate boxing and takedown defence won out against Dvalishvili, who was defending his title for a fourth time in the calendar year. Dvalishvili (21-5) won their first meeting and has vowed to exact revenge on the Russian and settle their rivalry once and for all . Following Losene Keita's viral first-round knockout of Muhammas Naimov, the Belgian is a short-notice replacement for Arnold Allen and will face American featherweight Aaron Pico. English flyweight Lone'er Kavanagh will test his skills against Ramazan Temirov of Uzbekistan, and Alexander Volkov meets fellow Russian Rizvan Kuniev in a heavyweight clash to round out the main card. At the top of the prelims, Azamat Murzakanov will look to get back in the win column after his 12-fight win streak was halted by Paulo Costa in his last bout. The heavy-handed Russian takes on former light heavyweight title contender Dominick Reyes. What else is happening during fight week? There are two UFC Fan Experiences to attend throughout the week, one at Yas Mall (Monday-Saturday) and the other at Yas Bay Plaza (Wednesday-Sunday). The events are free and open to the public. Fans can get involved in immersive experiences and buy UFC merchandise at the stores. Timings: Yas Mall: Monday to Thursday, 10am to 10pm; Friday and Saturday from 10am to midnight. Yas Bay Plaza: Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, 4-10pm; Friday, 4pm to midnight; Saturday, 4pm to 2am. Fans can attend the public workout on Wednesday at Yas Mall's Town Centre (5-7pm), where the headline and co-main event fighters will go through their paces. The press conferences will be held on Thursday at Etihad Arena (4-5.30pm). Fans are also invited to attend for free. The weigh-ins will then take place on Friday, with the closed official weigh-ins scheduled for 8am before ceremonial weigh-ins in the evening at Etihad Arena (4-6.30pm), which are open to the public. Tickets Tickets can be purchased at www.ticketmaster.ae. How to watch UFC 333 on TV The event can be watched live in the UAE on Starzplay.

title: Aston Villa v Man City ratings: Manzambi 6; Jackson 8; Guehi 5, Ndiaye 8
description: Enzo Maresca's perfect start as manager is over after two goals from Senegalese striker earns Midlands side 2-1 Premier League win
content: Aston Villa ended Manchester City's 100 per cent winning start to the Premier League season when a Nicolas Jackson double earned them a 2-1 victory on Saturday. On the fourth anniversary of Unai Emery's appointment as manager , the Midlands club continued their impressive run against City as they secured a fourth successive win against them at Villa Park. Senegalese striker Jackson opened the scoring with just six minutes on the clock after Villa capitalised on a mistake by City defender Marc Guehi. The away side levelled just after half-time thanks to a towering header from Erling Haaland for his 13th goal in 11 matches across all competitions. But Villa would claim all three points when Jackson fired him from substitute Ibrahim Mbaye's ball into the middle on the hour mark. Victory temporarily lifts Villa up to sixth place with 11 points from eight matches, while City remain top although Arsenal could draw level with them on 21 points if the Gunners defeat Everton later on Saturday. 3 & 4 – Aston Villa are the first side to win three successive Premier League games against Manchester City since Liverpool in December 2016 and the first to win four successive home league matches since Spurs in February 2023. Heroes. pic.twitter.com/xFZzWPNaIP — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 24, 2026 What they said: Aston Villa defender Matty Cash: “The manager gives us tasks but you have to take responsibility too, I do a lot of work on wingers, I think as a full back you have to try to get aggressive and it makes them difficult for them. I thought I did my task well. Getting close to him is the biggest challenge. I was watching clips of him this morning. “We had a lot of change at the start of the season, it was going to take time to gel and get comfortable with each other. Unai Emery is brilliant, having him stay is the main priority for us.” Manchester City captain Ruben Dias: “It is frustrating for us. I felt everyone fought a lot for us. The first 15 minutes we took time to get into the game. They changed the way they set up a bit and it took us time to adjust. We then had chances and momentum and they ended up scoring two goals in two transitions. They were very efficient. There is room to improve and we need to do better. “I felt like we were dangerous in many occasions, even if we didn’t have the finish. I think we need a word of appreciation to all our boys because we kept fighting until the end.” Aston Villa ratings: Zion Suzuki – 8/10: Japanese keeper saved well from Ndiaye, Cherki and Khusanov inside opening 25 minutes. Beaten by Ndiaye effort that hit post and no chance with Haaland goal. A couple of good stops after break and has taken to English football with ease. Matty Cash – 7/10: Up against the threat of Doku and, like many a full-back, found it tough going. Booked for clumsy foul on Belgian early in second half which left him on knife edge for rest of game but stuck to task. Victor Lindelof – 8/10: Former Manchester United defender had helped keep Haaland very quiet only for Norwegian to score with his first attempt. But Swede still produced a fine performance at Villa Park Pau Torres – 8/10: Spanish centre-half played very well alongside defensive partner Lindelof as Villa maintained the form that has seen them lose only once in 10 matches across all competitions. Ian Maatsen – 6/10: Dutch full-back volleyed game's first attempt high and wide. Twice failed to stop Ndiaye cutting inside and firing off shots in first half. Vital header to deny Haaland second goal. Boubacar Kamara – 7/10: Quietly effective in the centre of Villa's midfield, dovetailing well with McGinn and does his job with minimum fuss but it vitally important to Emery's side Joao Gomes – 7/10: Midfielder who was sent off on his Villa debut in the opening game of the season, still looks like a booking waiting to happen but put in decent shift here. It's Jackson again! ⚽️ @AstonVilla are back in front! 🔥 #AVLMCI pic.twitter.com/Lcba6eIkVq — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 John McGinn – 7/10: Was captain's quick thinking after Guehi's mistake for City that set-up Jackson for striker's opening goal. His constant harrying of opponents delighted home fans. Johan Manzambi – 6/10: Curled free-kick from dangerous position well over bar. Worked hard defensively but too easily beaten by Ndiaye ahead of City's leveller, then booked for delaying the restart and hit in groin by ball in matter of minutes. Alysson – 7/10: Brazilian was full of running up and down pitch, making important challenges tracking back and made some dangerous runs forward helping Villa to fifth win in their past seven meetings against City. Nicolas Jackson – 8/10: Showed fine composure to skip past Anderson before thumping finish into roof of net for early Villa lead. Fired another low effort wide of target not long after. Second was first-time finish that keeper should have done better with. Substitutes: Ibrahim Mbaye (On for Alysson, 59') – 7/10: Set-up Jackson's second goal to earn quick-fire assist immediately after coming on. Ross Barkley (On for McGinn, 66') – 6/10: Brought to shore up midfield with City hunting for equaliser. Emi Buendia (On for Manzambi, 66') – 6/10: Argentine was full of energybut earned a late booking as Villa defender their lead. Brian Madjo (On for Jackson, 82') – N/A: Booked for shooting at goal after whistle had blown for foul. Leon Goretzka (On for Gomes, 82') – N/A . Man City ratings: Gianluigi Donnarumma – 5/10: Gave away early corner for taking too long with goal kick. Beaten at near post by rising Jackson finish minutes later. Made mess of shot from Senegalese striker that put Villa back in front in second half. Abdukodir Khusanov – 7/10: Started at right-back with Matheus Nunes again missing through injury, and looked solid. Shifted into centre for second half and the Uzbeki again looked comfortable. Ruben Dias – 6/10: Captain made vital sliding challenge on Alysson to stop Brazilian shooting on goal lat in first half. Had hands full dealing with in-form opponent in Jackson. Marc Guehi – 5/10: Coming on back of errors against Ipswich last weekend, was his awful touch that gifted Villa possession and led to early lead. Booked for pulling down Jackson on edge of box. Hooked at break. Josko Gvardiol – 7/10: Saw rising strike just after Haaland's leveller tipped over bar by Suzuki and had another effort blocked at close range by the Villa Keeper. Caught out of position giving Villa substitute Mbaye too much space to set-up Jackson's second goal. Elliot Anderson – 7/10: Usual relentless running in City engine room and didn't get grip of midfield like he has done at times this season. Booked for foul on Gomes. Enzo Fernandez – 6/10: Went down too theatrically looking for penalty after shove in back from Gomes and referee waved away claims. Far too quiet an afternoon from the £125 million midfielder . Iliman Ndiaye – 8/10: Showed lovely skill to drop shoulder, cut inside and fire off swerving shot that keeper saved well. Curled another effort off the post. Supplied cross for Haaland's goal.
