title: Lockerbie bombing suspect's trial to start in 2027
description: Jury selection for trial of alleged Pan Am bomb builder was scheduled to begin in August
content: Lockerbie bombing suspect Abu Agila Al Marimi 's trial will now probably begin in 2027, according to recently filed documents. The updated trial start date is the latest in a series of delays in the closely watched case that was supposed to begin several years ago. Judge Dabney Friedrich suggested that jury selection will begin at some point in January, reports from Monday's hearing said. Last month, court-appointed lawyers for Mr Al Marimi, the man accused of making the bomb that killed 270 people in the 1988 Lockerbie air disaster, were granted a delay to the start of the trial. During that August pre-trial hearing, Ms Friedrich granted Mr Al Marimi's court-appointed lawyer's request for more time to review evidence to be presented against his client. Jury selection for his trial was tentatively scheduled to begin on August 25, but as pre-trial hearings continued last week it was clear that deadline would not be met. In 1988, all 259 people on board Pan Am Flight 103 died in the terrorist attack. Eleven others were killed on the ground in Lockerbie , Scotland, by falling debris from the explosion. It occurred shortly after the Pan Am flight took off from London on December 21. Of the 270 victims, 190 were US citizens. About 150 pieces of crash evidence will be presented, along with accounts of witnesses from several countries. Evidence will also come in the form of passports, hotel records, receipts, telegrams, baggage tags and letters. Many of those documents come from Libya, the UK, the US, Malta, and what was then known as Czechoslovakia. Adding to the buzz around the case has been the release of a six-part series by Netflix titled The Bombing of Pan Am Flight 103. It portrays the events leading up to the incident and the investigation into it. The series ranks among Netflix’s top 10 TV shows in the US. Mr Al Marimi was first charged in 2020 and taken into US custody in 2022, but health issues, defence team problems and long pre-trial deliberations have delayed the trial. Only one person, former Libyan intelligence officer Abdelbaset Al Megrahi, has been convicted of the bombing. Al Megrahi died in 2012.

title: Iran war tests Trump's trade truce with China
description: Treasury chief pushes for 'quiet diplomacy' as Washington avoids provoking Beijing with secondary sanctions
content: The US left out a major player as Washington opened a new front in its maximum-pressure campaign against Iran's economy: China. When he unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast” at the Treasury Department on Monday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged other countries to cut their financial ties with Iran "and sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime". “It is now a time for world leaders to make a decision between prosperity and isolation, peace and terror, America and Iran,” Mr Bessent told reporters. With a naval blockade and military operation failing to force Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Washington is placing more pressure on global partners to further cripple an Iranian economy that has been weathering sanctions for decades. As part of this new campaign, the US announced it is broadening its scope of secondary sanctions to discourage foreign companies or countries from doing business with Iran. Those that continue to do so are at risk of being cut off from the dollar-based financial system. However, the US stopped short of imposing immediate penalties on China or indicating how far it is willing to go with it. China bought up to 90 per cent of Iran's shipped oil in 2025 and Mr Bessent said no country is above US sanctions. But he added that the best way to engage with countries is through “quiet diplomacy”. And although a US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz has dried up Iranian oil exports, China for decades has provided Iran with the materials to build missiles and drones, according to the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission. Bilateral trade between Tehran and Beijing was estimated to be worth almost $10 billion, according to the group, which was founded to examine the US's bilateral ties to China. The US has also placed sanctions against independent Chinese “teapot” refineries, although it has not yet gone after major Chinese banks or financial institutions. Little detail was also offered for Iran's other major trading partners including India, Pakistan and Turkey. Ali Wyne, senior researcher for China-US relations at the International Crisis Group, said it remained to be seen how willing Washington is to go after these major players. Mr Wyne questioned Mr Bessent's efforts to secure the sustained support of western allies, of which he said “many” had been alienated by the administration. “The announcement of ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ betrays anxiety, not confidence, about Washington's ability to induce Tehran's capitulation,” he said. Stephen Fallon, founder of DBM Consulting, compared the messaging with Mr Trump's first maximum-pressure campaign in 2018, after the US withdrew from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, which offered Iran sanctions relief in return for concessions on its nuclear programme. Those that would had already left the dollar-based financial system during Mr Trump’s 2018 sanctions campaign, he said, leaving few options for Washington. “We saw this in 2018, and it was powerful and it worked,” Mr Fallon said. Today's campaign comes amid a fragile trade truce that Washington and Beijing struck last year, placing a cap on tariffs and ensuring China's rare-earth minerals would continue to flow. While the US has been urgently seeking to secure its domestic critical minerals supply, experts say it is still years behind China, whose export restrictions are due to take effect only a few months after President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington. Reports suggest the Iran war is depleting the US's military stockpile, which could take years to rebuild. Mr Trump's administration is now engaging in diplomatic efforts and tapping into the private sector for projects linked to rare-earth minerals, scandium and other metals crucial to developing advanced defence systems. “Iran rather is … frustrating, humiliating and exhausting the US. Why would China interrupt that?” Mr Fallon said.

title: More than 50 UN member states urge Russia to accept full ceasefire in Ukraine
description: Group uses Kyiv's 35th anniversary of independence from the Soviet Union to push for return to peace talks
content: More than 50 UN member states on Monday urged Russia to accept a full and unconditional ceasefire in Ukraine and return to talks aimed at lasting peace. The call came as Kyiv marked 35 years since declaring independence from the Soviet Union. Dsnish Foreign Minister Lars Loekke Rasmussen delivered the joint statement at the UN on behalf of countries including the UK, France, Germany, Greece, Canada, North Macedonia, Japan and Ukraine, as well as the EU. “Ukraine wants peace. We want peace,” Mr Rasmussen said. “We strongly urge Russia to respond to the calls for a full, immediate and unconditional ceasefire and resume talks for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in Ukraine in accordance with international law, including the UN Charter.” The countries said Russia could end the war immediately by accepting the unconditional ceasefire sought by Ukraine and the international community for more than 18 months. The statement came on Ukraine's Independence Day, four and a half years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion. The group also called for prisoner-of-war exchanges to be completed, unlawfully detained people to be released and Ukrainians who were forcibly transferred or deported, including thousands of children, to be returned safely. It warned that the war's effects were spreading beyond Ukraine, with airspace breaches and drone incidents in Europe, and Russian attacks on Black Sea grain shipments and Ukrainian ports, which threatened global food security. The countries reaffirmed their support for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders, saying there was “no alternative to a just and lasting peace”. One of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s main aims in launching the 2022 invasion was to bring Ukraine back under Moscow’s influence. Ukraine declared independence from the Soviet Union on August 24, 1991, a decision later overwhelmingly backed in a nationwide referendum. With little movement on the front line and US-led peace efforts making no clear progress, Russia and Ukraine have increased bombings, killing civilians and damaging infrastructure. Civilian casualties have risen sharply as attacks intensify, the countries said, quoting UN figures that showed at least 437 civilians were killed in Ukraine in July, the highest monthly toll since March 2022. At least 68,000 civilians, including nearly 4,000 children, have been killed or wounded since Russia launched its full-scale invasion. Ukraine’s UN ambassador Andrii Melnyk said July was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians as the country was facing critical shortages of air defence interceptors. Mr Melnyk accused Russia of deliberately attacking civilians with ballistic missiles and urged Ukraine’s allies to release more air defence systems. “If we are to be completely frank, my fellow citizens find it difficult to understand why missiles capable of saving hundreds of lives every day are being kept in stowages instead of being used to shield Ukrainian civilians,” he said. Mr Melnyk acknowledged global production constraints and shortages of air defence systems but called on Ukraine’s allies “to provide Ukraine with all the available Patriot interceptor missiles currently held". Russia’s UN ambassador Vasily Nebenzya, meanwhile, accused Kyiv of deliberately targeting Russian civilians after failing to make gains on the battlefield. “Having failed to achieve the desired results on the battlefield, the Kiev regime has now definitively slipped into outright terror against Russia’s civilian population,” Mr Nebenzya told the Council. He accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of seeking more Western weapons that were then being used to strike Russian cities, residential areas and civilian infrastructure. “The calculation is obvious: to intimidate people, sow chaos and destabilize the situation inside Russia,” Mr Nebenzya said.

title: Trump threatens to double Canadian car tariffs
description: Car makers' shares fall amid fears the tariff would snarl the closely integrated supply chain between the US and Canada
content: US President Donald Trump has threatened to raise US tariffs on all cars, lorries and automotive ⁠parts from Canada to 50 per cent starting on January 1, intensifying a trade fight ​after negotiations collapsed last week. The trade deal would have cut the top-line tariff rate on Canadian cars and light-duty lorries from 25 per cent to 15 per cent, ⁠and the tariffs on aluminium and steel from 50 per cent to 25 per cent. But the deal fell apart on Friday over a number of points of contention, including whether the US tariff relief would have applied to medium or heavy-duty trucks. The escalation threatens to disrupt one of the world's most integrated car supply chains. US vehicle production is heavily reliant on ⁠Canadian-made parts and vehicles, and higher tariffs could raise costs for American car makers and consumers while deepening a trade stand-off that has already hit ​auto stocks. "Build in ⁠the US and there are zero tariffs. Canada ‌will be treated like a state no longer," Mr Trump wrote in a social media post. "On trade, and in other ways also, they are among the worst nations ​in the world to deal with. They feel entitled, and yet, we don't need Canada, they need us." But it is unclear if the new tariffs will be enacted. The January 1 introduction leaves room for potential negotiations, even as the Canadians see little chance of them resuming before the midterm elections in November. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is set to respond to the weekend tariffs with levies of his own on September 8 and the US has threatened to escalate further if he does. At a media conference in Quebec on Monday, Mr Carney said a "mutually beneficial deal" with the US was possible, but only if the Americans respect Canada's sovereignty. "When the Americans go to the negotiating table first with the right attitude toward our industry and a true partnership, of course we'll come to the negotiating table," he said at a briefing announcing an investment in six new Canadian icebreaker ships. Shares in car makers fell. Ford and Stellantis stocks were down 3.6 per cent and 4.2 per cent respectively, while shares of General Motors were down 1.6 per cent on Monday afternoon. Toyota stock was down 1.5 per cent in New York trading and Honda shares were down 2.1 per cent. "A threatened US tariff on Canadian auto parts ​will be paid by [the] US auto assembly. Without those specific parts, auto assembly throughout the US would halt," said Flavio Volpe, president of Canada's Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association.

title: UAE among 'most ambitious' AI markets, new report highlights
description: More than half of UAE organisations have introduced Agentic AI
content: The UAE's governance and investment in AI have created ripe conditions for businesses to make the most of the technology, a report says. ServiceNow , the enterprise software company, detailed its latest findings about how businesses, organisations and enterprises are using AI in its Enterprise AI Maturity Index. “The UAE remains one of the world’s most ambitious AI markets and the government’s long-term strategy and regulatory leadership have given organisations a genuine head start,” said Saif Mashat, vice president for the Middle East and Africa at ServiceNow. Mr Mashat, however, cautioned that it was not enough for entities to simply invest in AI. "The ones pulling ahead are moving from AI pilots to AI orchestration, connecting legacy systems, data, governance and AI agents in one control tower," he added. The ServiceNow analysis showed that the UAE made a 13-point improvement on its AI maturity score. "The research shows many organisations are still trying to layer AI on to fragmented technology environments, disconnected data and siloed workflows," a highlighted version of the analysis read. Agentic AI, often defined as AI tools that can act to help humans with repetitive tasks, continues to be the talk of the technology world, is still a work in progress for many businesses. "Currently, more than half, 57 per cent, of UAE organisations have implemented agentic AI, but only 7 per cent have used it to build autonomous workflows," the report continued. Mr Mashat said that because the UAE government "has already created many of the conditions for AI leadership", it was now largely up to companies to make sure they go beyond merely investing in the technology. "The challenge for enterprises now is to bring that same discipline and consistency into their own organisations," he said. In terms of investment, the ServiceNow survey showed that the UAE continues to be optimistic about AI. "UAE organisations expect AI to account for almost one fifth of total information technology budgets by 2027," the report read. For more than a decade, the UAE has pushed to be an AI leader as it diversifies its economy away from hydrocarbons. The country’s affinity for research into the technology has resulted in the establishment of start-ups, partnerships and investments from industry leaders including Microsoft , Nvidia and OpenAI. The UAE has also teamed up with the US to develop an AI campus, which will include 5GW of capacity for AI data centres, in Abu Dhabi. ServiceNow said that its 2026 Enterprise AI Maturity Index was compiled by ThoughtLab, and involved surveying about 4,500 executives and 2,000 employees around the world. Broadly, among the 19 countries where people were surveyed, there were recurring themes that emerged where many organisations were just starting to scratch the surface of how AI could affect day-to-day operations. Fifty-nine per cent of those organisations, according to ServiceNow, had the ability to to use Agentic AI but only 9 per cent "have made significant progress using agentic AI to create autonomous, multistep workflows". The report also found that France showed more resistance to AI than other countries, and employees in Saudi Arabia tended to be more resistant to the technology "due to more rigid, risk-averse workplaces, compounded by siloed data and overlapping tools".

title: US removes Syria from terrorism sponsor list after 47 years
description: Decision will 'foster additional investment' in country
content: ​The US State Department has officially removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, clearing a major obstacle in Damascus's economic recovery. The delisting came after US President Donald Trump in July notified the US Congress of his intent to rescind Syria 's designation as ⁠​a state sponsor of terrorism. The action required Congress to conduct a 45-day review to finalise the decision. In 1979, Syria was placed on the US blacklist, which also includes Iran, Cuba and North Korea. “Treasury is following through on President Trump’s promise to give the Syrian people a chance at greatness,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday. “Today’s action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability.” The US also revoked the designation of Al Nusra Front . The group formally severed ties with Al Qaeda in 2016 and later rebranded, merging into Hayat Tahrir Al Sham in 2017. “These actions were all taken in recognition of the positive actions taken and further commitments by the Syrian government under President Ahmad Al Shara to fully distance Syria from acts of international terrorism,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement. “In the past year, the government of Syria has taken significant steps to counter terrorism.” Mr Al Shara was the leader of HTS. Since removing the regime of Bashar Al Assad in December 2024, he has forged a strong relationship with Mr Trump, who has moved quickly to push for Syria's reintegration into the global economy. The Syrian President on Tuesday responded to the US removing it from its list of state sponsors of terrorism. “Today, Syria shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past to embark on a path of development, reconstruction and rebuilding,” Mr Al Shara said in a speech. Washington last year lifted sanctions imposed under the Caesar Act, but the designation as a state sponsor of terrorism was regarded as a major obstacle to Syria's economic recovery after the Assad regime fell. Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey and special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq, said the designation had for too long separated the “Syrian people from the investment, enterprise, and opportunity necessary to rebuild their nation. Today, another wall comes down.” Syrian Foreign Minister Assad Al Shibani congratulated the country's people for what he described as “historic event”, saying this step is “the fruit of the transformation made by the Syrians”. “We will continue the work to remove the effects of isolation and prepare an environment based on transparency, mutual interests and respect, in a way that enhances development and stability in Syria and the region,” Mr Al Shibani wrote in a post on X. The World Bank estimates the country's reconstruction will cost $216 billion. In May, the State Department released an investor handbook and guides for US companies to enter the Syrian market. Damascus's designation status has been a point of friction for would-be investors while anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism concerns are also constraining factors.

title: France and Saudi Arabia call for normal navigation in Strait of Hormuz
description: Push for dialogue comes as US intensifies economic pressure on Tehran
content: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman ended a two-day visit to Paris with a joint call alongside French President Emmanuel Macron for navigation in the Strait of Hormuz to be returned to its "normal state". "The two sides condemned the attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and threats to the security of waterways," they said in a statement on Monday. "They stressed the importance of restoring navigation in the Strait of Hormuz to its normal state," they added, referring to "freedom of navigation, regular shipping traffic, and the absence of any direct or indirect tolls, or restrictions on passage, in accordance with international law". Their call comes as the US unveiled an expansion of secondary sanctions against Iran in a bid to force it to stop attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said countries will have a deadline to shut down activities with Iran that have been identified by his office, or they could have key companies and entities cut off from the dollar-based financial ​system. Iran has warned that more economic pressure will have consequences. Tehran closed down the Strait after a joint US-Israeli attack in late February, nearly completely shutting down traffic in the waterway through which about 20 per cent of the world's oil used to travel. France and Saudi Arabia called on resolving issues with Iran, including its nuclear programme, through a "negotiated solution to avoid further escalation and ensure regional security." The Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen has recently also joined in assaults on maritime transit in the region by attacking ships and Saudi oil infrastructure – a move condemned by Mr Macron and Prince Mohammed. "The French side affirmed its solidarity and full support for the kKingdom of Saudi Arabia, and stressed its rejection of any attacks on the Kingdom's territory," the joint statement said. Mr Macron and Prince Mohammed also discussed the situations regarding Israel, Palestine, Lebanon and Syria. Last month, the French President was the first EU leader to visit Damascus since rebels toppled the regime of president Bashar Al Assad in December 2024. "They highlighted the importance of a robust institutional framework conducive to intensified economic investments and the opportunity of repositioning Syria as a bridge between Europe, the Gulf and Asia by building alternative routes," the statement said. Four business and defence agreements were signed during Prince Mohammed's visit, on a variety of matters including a $6 billion Saudi investment in building manga-themed amusement parks near Paris, and the strengthening of a defence partnership. Paris has formal defence agreements with a number of Gulf states, including the UAE, and a deepening strategic co-operation with Saudi Arabia. France, alongside Italy, was one of the few EU states to help Gulf nations defend themselves from Iranian missile and drone attacks after the start of the war in February. The French Economy Ministry and the Saudi Communications Ministry also signed a preliminary agreement for a co-operation framework in AI, quantum computing and emerging technologies. Business representatives from France and Saudi Arabia held a meeting during which French shipping giant CMA CGM signed a $434 million contract with Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Gateway Terminal to develop one of its terminals in Jeddah. French rail company Alstom signed a €500 million contract with Riyadh's Royal Commission to develop two metro lines. The world's ​top ​oil ⁠exporter, Saudi ⁠Aramco, said it had signed ​agreements with ⁠some French companies that could be worth more than $3.7 billion ⁠in total. The agreements include procurement deals for drilling equipment and oil country goods, as well as a preliminary agreement ​to ‌explore ⁠industrial ​AI and ​related technologies. Saudi Aramco did ⁠not identify the ⁠French companies involved in the agreements.

title: Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour dies aged 79
description: Painter was leading figure in contemporary Arab art
content: Sliman Mansour, one of the leading figures in contemporary Palestinian art, has died aged 79. The announcement was made by Mansour ’s family on his verified Instagram account shortly after a post saying he was in critical condition. No cause of death has been disclosed. “The final chapter has been written,” the family said. “With hearts heavy beyond words, we share that our beloved father has passed away. “To the world, he leaves behind a life filled with beauty, memory, and a legacy that will continue to live through all those he touched. But to us, we lost a father, our source of love, strength and home.” Funeral and memorial details will be announced later. Born in Birzeit, near Ramallah, in 1947, Mansour was at the forefront of Palestinian art for more than five decades. His work helped to shape a visual language for Palestinian identity, drawing repeatedly on the land and the experiences of displacement and occupation. Mansour graduated from the Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design in Jerusalem in 1970. He found his subjects in the landscape and daily life around him. Olive trees and traditional embroidery recur throughout his paintings, while Jerusalem appears as both a place and an object of longing. He was perhaps best known for Jamal Al Mahamel , also called Camel of Hardship . The painting depicts an elderly Palestinian man carrying the city of Jerusalem on his back, and has become one of the most widely recognised images in Palestinian art. The weary but determined figure came to embody the Palestinian concept of sumud, or steadfastness. Reproduced as a poster, the image moved beyond galleries and became a fixture in Palestinian homes and public spaces. In an account he gave to The National in 2021, Mansour recalled that an exhibition featuring work by him, Nabil Anani and Issam Badr at 79 Gallery in Ramallah was closed by the Israeli army after three hours in 1980. Two weeks later, the artists were summoned and warned against producing political paintings. “They told us that painting the Palestinian flag was forbidden, but also the colours were forbidden,” Mansour said . “So Issam said, ‘What if I were to make a flower of red, green, black and white?’, to which the officer replied angrily, ‘It will be confiscated. Even if you paint a watermelon, it will be confiscated.’ So the watermelon was mentioned, but by the Israeli officer.” Mansour was a founder of the League of Palestinian Artists and its leader from 1986 to 1990. During the First Intifada, he co-founded the New Visions collective with Vera Tamari, Tayseer Barakat and Anani. The artists boycotted Israeli art supplies and turned to materials found locally, including mud and henna. Mud became central to Mansour’s work. He layered and moulded it on wooden structures, allowing the material to crack as it dried. The resulting figures carried a sense of fragility and time passing, while the earth itself tied the work physically to Palestine. Mansour also spent much of his career building an infrastructure for Palestinian art. In 1994, he co-founded Al-Wasiti Art Centre in East Jerusalem, established to preserve Palestinian art and connect artists living in Palestine with those in exile. He later joined the founding board of the International Academy of Art Palestine in Ramallah. He taught at Al Quds University from 2000 to 2014 and contributed cartoons and illustrations to the English-language Palestinian newspaper Al Fajr and Al-Awda magazine between 1981 and 1993. His work had longstanding connections to the UAE. Mansour took part in the Sharjah Biennial in 1995 and held a solo exhibition, The Fabric of Memory, at Sharjah Art Museum in 2003. He received the 2019 Unesco-Sharjah Prize for Arab Culture in recognition of his art, teaching and work creating platforms for younger artists. Mansour also received the Palestine Prize for the Visual Arts and the Grand Nile Prize at the Cairo Biennial in 1998, the latter for his mud relief series I Am Ismail . By late 2023, the war in Gaza was changing the way he worked. Mansour had begun a large painting without preparatory sketches, applying colour and brushstrokes directly to the canvas. “All the images that come to my mind are really horrible,” he said. “Some I can’t get out of my mind – I can only get them out through painting. You know, I always hated abstract expressionism. I didn’t like it. But I think now is the time for it.” In the same 2023 interview with The National , Mansour said a stroke two years earlier had affected his left hand and made it harder for him to concentrate and paint. He nevertheless continued to visit his Ramallah studio. “I try to work daily, to go to the studio, to do something there – not painting all the time, but maybe reading or making sketches or something like that,” he said. “I try to go every day. It’s a routine and I don’t like to stop it.”

title: Pakistan's army chief visits Iran on mediating mission
description: Field Marshal Asim Munir meets Iranian interior minister as Islamabad aims to revive diplomacy between Pakistan and Iran
content: Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan's army chief, visited Iran on Monday as Islamabad seeks to revive talks between Tehran and Washington. His mission comes as the Trump administration unveiled “the greatest financial offensive ever” against Iran's trade partners in an economic campaign. Field Marshal Munir and Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran. A Pakistani source told The National that Field Marshal Munir’s focus is on trying to bring the US and Iran back to the negotiating table and persuade Tehran not to attack Gulf countries, particularly Saudi Arabia, which has a defence partnership with Pakistan. The source added that Pakistani officials are “hopeful” that Washington and Tehran will return to talks, noting that “something good will happen”. Pakistan has served as a key mediator in indirect negotiations between the US and Iran. Islamabad said Field Marshal Munir’s trip was part of its efforts “to promote regional peace and stability”. The White House confirmed to Reuters that US President Donald Trump had called Field Marshal Munir last week. The main request was to bring Iran back into negotiations. Mr Trump has developed a strong rapport with Field Marshal Munir and Islamabad in general during his second term. Pakistan nominated Mr Trump for a Nobel Peace Prize and credited him with defusing a conflict with India last year. Pakistan's diplomatic efforts in Tehran come as the US is expected on Monday to broaden the scope of secondary sanctions on firms and countries that do business with Iran, as Washington seeks to isolate the regime's economy in an effort to break the deadlock in the war. The move was meant to serve as a final notice to countries to sever business ties with Iran as the US steps up its economic pressure campaign, the White House said. The US and Iran have not conducted direct military strikes on each other for weeks, but their last official face-to-face talks to end the six-month conflict took place in June, and strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz have continued.

title: CNN outage affects viewers throughout the US
description: Parent company says it is working to resolve technical problem
content: CNN experienced a widespread outage that briefly affected its ability to broadcast programming on Monday. Shortly after noon Eastern time, the signal for many viewers throughout the US began to appear scrambled. In a social media post on several platforms, CNN commented on the situation. "We are aware of a technical issue across Warner Bros Discovery that resulted in losing CNN channels for a period of time today," the statement read in part. "We are working quickly to resolve it and apologise for the interruption. On air, the company also acknowledged the problem. "There was a technical issue, we're very sorry and happy to be back," said CNN's anchor Dana Bash shortly after CNN's signal returned. The network, founded by Ted Turner in Atlanta back in 1980 was among the first to boast of 24 hour news content. Outages impacting the CNN , owned by Warner Bros / Discovery are incredibly rare. At one point during the problem on Monday, CNN started to air a pre-recorded program before returning to live content. CNN's chief media analyst Brian Stelter said that there would be "more to come on this", in reference to the social media post from the company's public relations account. In an article on CNN, Mr Stelter pointed out the varying degree to which viewers may have experienced problems with the channel "depending on the distribution platform they use." He also said that the outage briefly impacted HBO and other channels falling under the Warner Bros Discovery jursidiction.

title: Hundreds of Dubai pupils given school supplies under education plan
description: Community strategy to help families planning for new academic year
content: More than 1,000 pupils in Dubai will be provided with essential school supplies before their return to classrooms next week under a major community campaign. The initiative – launched by the emirate's Community Development Authority – aims to deliver support to families preparing for the new academic year, which begins on Monday, August 31. The authority – which has rolled out the Back to School scheme in partnership with Dubai Community Contributions Establishment (Jood) and the Awqaf and Minors Affairs Foundation (Awqaf Dubai) – said it would help learners achieve their education goals while championing family values. “Through this integrated approach, we strengthen family stability and enhance the quality of life of community members, transforming social responsibility into tangible impact by directing resources towards actual priorities and supporting the aspirations of our students”, said Maitha Al Shamsi, chief executive of the Community Empowerment Sector at the Community Development Authority. Marwan bin Hashem, chief executive of Jood, said the initiative is rooted in the belief that education remains a fundamental pillar of human development. He said ensuring children have essential school supplies will foster a positive environment in which pupils have the confidence to make strides on their academic journeys. The campaign comes as hundreds of thousands of pupils look forward to their first day back at school following the summer break. Pupils, parents and school leaders alike are looking forward to the new term with optimism after the previous academic year was disrupted by the Iran war, leading to a temporary switch to remote learning and the cancellation of many in-person exams. The Back to School initiative is in support of Dubai Social Agenda 33, which is intended to establish the emirate as a global destination for living, learning and investment.

title: Saudi Arabia to invest $7bn in three manga-themed amusement parks near Paris
description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman share 'passion for manga'
content: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund on Monday signed an agreement with the French government to invest $7 billion in creating three manga-themed amusement parks north-east of Paris. The announcement came at the end of a two-day visit to Paris by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman , who was hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron. The two leaders oversaw the signing of the €6bn ($7bn) agreement between Roland Lescure, French Economy and Finance Minister, and Abdullah Al Dawood, Director General of Qiddiya, a subsidiary of the PIF. "We’re not done surprising the world. Very proud of this achievement," Mr Macron said on X. The Japanese manga series Dragon Ball , which became a global phenomenon in the 1990s, will be one of the themes of the new parks, Mr Macron's office said, without giving details on a time frame. The parks, expected to create 22,000 new jobs, will be built near Cergy-Pontoise, about 30km from Paris. "You know my passion for manga. You also know my determination to attract to France the investments that create jobs and make the most ambitious projects possible," Mr Macron said. "Thank you to Qiddiya and Saudi Arabia for their trust in our country, in our talents and in our future." The Saudi side was reportedly attracted to the site due to its proximity to Paris and to the entertainment resort Disneyland Paris, to the west of the capital. The area once housed France's first theme park, which closed 35 years ago. Named Mirapolis, it opened in 1987 with private Saudi funding and aimed to showcase French literature but it closed down due to financial difficulties. The news of the new theme parks is expected to be well received in France, eight months before a presidential election in which Mr Macron will not be able to run, having already served two consecutive terms. The presidential race is dominated by issues related to high public debt and low purchasing power. Mr Macron's office said he first discussed the plan with the Saudi Crown Prince during a visit made by the French President to Riyadh in December 2024. “During a conversation at the Crown Prince's residence, the two leaders realised they share a passion for manga,” an adviser to Mr Macron said. Details were hammered out during a series of meetings starting in March 2025 between the French President's advisers and the Qiddiya Investment Company, a subsidiary of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund which opened an office in Paris last year. In Saudi Arabia, the Qiddiya Investment Company is overseeing the development of a mega-tourism project near Riyadh, including the first theme park dedicated to the Dragon Ball franchise, spanning more than 500,000 square metres. Mr Macron and Prince Mohammed appear to also share an interest in video gaming. On Sunday, they attended the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup , which took place outside Saudi Arabia for the first time, in Paris. Prince Mohammed's visit was otherwise dominated by talks relating to the fallout from the Iran-US war.

title: Israeli forces cross ‘yellow line’ in south Lebanon town as attacks intensify
description: Tanks and bulldozers entered Haris and destroyed a road link to homes on the town’s outskirts
content: Israeli forces have pushed beyond their “yellow line” buffer zone in south Lebanon as tanks and bulldozers entered the town of Haris and destroyed a road link to homes on its outskirts, residents said. The push came amid a wider wave of Israeli attacks and demolitions on Monday across southern Lebanon, where homes and agricultural land were set on fire in Khiam and buildings destroyed in Taybeh, Mays Al Jebel and Yohmor. In Haris, which lies just outside the Israeli-occupied belt, residents said Israeli tanks and bulldozers crossed the yellow line separating the area that Israel considers a buffer zone from land under Lebanon’s control. “A while back, they crossed the yellow line once, to erect an earthen berm. We thought maybe that was it – that they had established the boundary between our village and them so that nobody could cross,” said local official Hussein Jawad. “But today they crossed it. They entered the heart of the village.” Videos of armoured Israeli bulldozers destroying a paved road in Haris circulated on social media. Mr Jawad said Israeli tanks and bulldozers descended from a nearby hilltop to bulldoze the road, effectively cutting off a populated neighbourhood on the outskirts from the rest of the village. Residents of the neighbourhood left their homes out of fear after seeing Israeli troops operating nearby, said Mr Jawad. While Israel has insisted it has no plans to permanently remain in south Lebanon, it has withdrawn from only one small village and continues to occupy dozens of towns. In some cases – such as the village of Mansouri, where residents are no longer permitted to return after Israel issued a forced displacement order this month – it has effectively expanded the territory it controls inside Lebanon, which extends up to 10km from the border, through artillery shelling and air raids. Lebanon’s National News Agency reported that the Israeli military set fire to homes, buildings and agricultural land in the large town of Khiam – within the yellow line – where large areas of the town were reduced to rubble after the war between Israel and Hezbollah broke out again in early March. Since a ceasefire was extended in June, Israeli demolitions have continued inside the town. A “major bombing operation” also took place in Taybeh, while in Mays Al Jebel the Israeli military demolished what used to be a temporary school on the western outskirts of the town. The Israeli military also detonated buildings in Yohmor, which sits adjacent to the historic Beaufort Castle . Elsewhere, there was fighting near the contested and strategically significant Ali Al Taher ridge line, with Israeli air strikes at dawn landing near the hill and artillery shelling in neighbouring Kfar Tebnit. Paramedics recovered the bodies of two men who were killed by an Israeli air strike in the nearby Kfar Roummane on Sunday. The Israeli military is poised for, but has yet to carry out, a full offensive on Ali Al Taher, a hill around 600 metres high that overlooks the major southern city of Nabatieh, which, while severely damaged, remains under Lebanese control. Buried deep inside the hill, which is effectively under siege, is believed to be an important Hezbollah base and network of tunnels, which the Iran-backed Lebanese armed group and political party has refused to cede to anyone. A number of Hezbollah fighters are believed to be inside the base protecting it, along with advisers from Iran's IRGC. Last week Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s Speaker of Parliament and lead negotiator with the US, appeared to highlight the importance of Ali Al Taher when he said he remained in constant contact with fighters on the ground.

title: UN aid chief condemns world's lack of action on Sudan
description: More than two thirds of African nation's population in dire need of life-saving aid, as civil war wreaks havoc
content: The UN humanitarian chief heavily criticised the international community on Monday for failing Sudan , as civilian deaths rise and aid operations face severe funding shortages. More than two thirds of Sudan's population are now in desperate need of life-saving assistance, UN aid chief Tom Fletcher told the Security Council. “The people of Sudan need food, water and medicine,” he said. “Yet the world sends drones, weapons and mercenaries.” About 1,400 civilians were killed in Sudan in the first half of this year, including more than 1,100 in drone strikes, the UN says. Mr Fletcher, the undersecretary general for humanitarian affairs and emergency relief co-ordinator, said drones were attacking markets, fuel stations, and critical power and water infrastructure in El Obeid in North Kordofan, where fighting has driven 15,000 families into the city since mid-July. Air strikes were also reported south-west of the city over the past 72 hours. Despite the violence, aid agencies reached nearly 11 million people with some form of assistance by the end of June. But Mr Fletcher warned that funding remained far short of what is required on the ground. Massad Boulos, US presidential adviser on Arab and African Affairs, echoed Mr Fletcher's concerns and called on the Security Council “to do more”. “Civilians across Sudan are living a nightmare,” he said. “The brutality of the war waged by the Rapid Support Forces and Sudanese Armed Forces has discredited their claims to be legitimate governors of the Sudanese people. “Civilians have been run out of their homes that were then looted. They have faced terrible atrocities and abuses, even as they have fled to safety. “How devastating the human toll of the increased use of armed drones has been. It is horrifying to know that armed drones have taken the lives of more than 1,120 Sudanese civilians already in the first half of this year.” The Darfur arms embargo, in place for more than two decades, is set to expire on September 12 if a new agreement is not reached. Expanding the restrictions to all of Sudan would require a vote of the UN Security Council, with veto-holding Russia warning on Monday against new measures that would affect the Sudanese army. Washington has put forward a draft Security Council resolution that would expand the existing arms embargo across all of Sudan and explicitly place drones and related technology within its scope. He said Washington has put forward a draft resolution that would expand the arms embargo across Sudan and clarify that drones and related technologies fall under its restrictions. The resolution would also request the UN Secretary General to “increase the number of experts on the 1591 panel, and four, directing the 1591 panel of experts to collaborate with other panels covering the region to better inform the council of violations of the assets freeze, travel ban, and arms embargo”. “If this council refuses to act, those who will suffer most are the Sudanese people,” he warned.

title: Tadej Pogacar pulls over peloton as torrential hailstorm forces Vuelta a Espana stage to be abandoned
description: Chaotic scenes in Pyrenees as severe weather conditions bring day's action to premature end
content: There were extraordinary scenes in the Vuelta a Espana on Monday when Stage 3 had to be abandoned with 15km to go due to a torrential hailstorm in the French ⁠Pyrenees. The 166.7km route from Guissan to Font Romeu contained the first summit finish but as the peloton scaled the Col de Mont-Louis, the skies darkened and conditions quickly deteriorated. Soon the peloton were being hammered by huge hailstones that forced riders to seek shelter off road with UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider – and race leader – Tadej Pogacar seen indicating to the main group to slow down and eventually pull over. The hail had come down so heavily that it resembled snow on the road and organisers were left with no choice but to cancel the stage. “For the security of the riders, stage three has been cancelled due to hail and severe weather. There will be no winner and no podium ceremony,” said an official announcement. At the time of its abandonment, the race was led by a lone breakaway rider, Equipo Kern Pharma’s Mats Wenzel, with all the major general classification (GC) contenders still in the leading group. The cancellation means Pogacar remains nine seconds clear of Wout van Aert (Team ​Visma- Lease a Bike) at the top of the GC standings. Meanwhile, Pogacar had insisted after Sunday's Stage 2 there was no major preoccupation with retaining the red jersey from beginning to end of the race. The Slovenian is looking to complete a clean-sweep of Grand Tour races having won the Tour de France five times and the Giro d'Italia once. After edging an ultra narrow victory in the opening day time-trial , he kept hold of the leader's jersey after Stage 2. “When you have the leader's jersey, you always appreciate it, you go from moment to moment, you wear it with honour,” he said. “But sometimes in a Grand Tour, it happens that there's no chance to keep it. There's a big chance that some day like this happens.” “I don't think any rider was thinking like this in the past to try to keep the jersey all the way to the finish. In the Giro [in 2024] I kept it from Stage 2, it's true, but it's not the goal. “You never know, maybe I could have lost it today, I could lose it tomorrow. You never know.” Tuesday's Stage 4 is a 104.8km high mountain route – with three category one summits – held entirely in Andorra for the first time since 2019, which saw Pogacar claim his first stage win in what was his Grand Tour debut. 1. Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-BORA hansgrohe) +14

title: Dubai's Parkin to expand into Bahrain and Egypt
description: Emirate's public parking operator has already moved to extend services to Abu Dhabi and Sharjah
content: Dubai's public parking operator is gearing up for a regional expansion drive after unveiling plans to deliver services in Bahrain and Egypt. Parkin has joined forces with Bahrain's Car Parks Company (Amakin) to provide smart parking in the kingdom, in what it hailed as a “milestone” achievement. The agreement – announced on Monday – comes only days after Parkin confirmed a similar partnership in Egypt, with Modon Misr for Asset & Facility Management, Mwasalat Misr and Redcon Properties. “Our partnership with Amakin represents a significant milestone in expanding our smart parking capabilities beyond Dubai, bringing together our complementary technologies and digital platforms to deliver a seamless customer experience and unlock future growth opportunities across the GCC and beyond,” said Mohamed Al Ali, chief executive of Parkin, said. Parkin, set up in January 2024 by the Dubai government, has sought to gradually extend operations beyond the emirate in recent months. In July, Parkin teamed up with Arada to introduce smart parking services at Aljada , a large-scale residential, business and retail development in Sharjah. In December, Parkin signed a five-year partnership with Damac Properties to manage 3,600 paid parking spaces in its residential communities. It will manage paid parking areas at dozens of residential and commercial towers, including at Reem Island in Abu Dhabi, its first entry into the capital. Parkin expanded its parking spaces by 27 per cent year-on-year and currently operates 268,300 paid parking spaces across Dubai. Paid parking areas across the city are expected to expand as the city grows , the chief executive said. Mr Al Ali told The National last week that regulated parking is critical infrastructure. “Parking is reaching every single person here,” he said. “We can see continued urban expansion, changing mobility patterns, and the growing expectations for smarter and more seamless services.” The company is focused on spreading its technology – cameras, equipment and more – in addition to its parking operations. “With our capabilities, operations, our technology, it's given us a great position in the market to provide not only operations,” Mr Al Ali said. “We are expanding, either in operations or on the technology platform.”

title: UAE minister issues call to empower communities to tackle humanitarian crises amid global funding cuts
description: Minister delivers key message as expert warns of impact of cutbacks on aid efforts
content: An Emirati minister has spoken about how needy communities can play a crucial role in addressing humanitarian challenges – as major funding cuts hamper aid efforts around the world. Maitha Al Shamsi, Minister of State, said people in crisis and disaster-stricken areas should be given support under a mission to transform “recipients of aid into active participants in development”. Ms Al Shamsi set out her vision for the future at the Dubai International Humanitarian Aid and Development Conference and Exhibition on Monday. She told of how investing in education and specialised training of refugees could drastically reduce the burden on countries and offer a lifeline to families. “It is essential to explore economic alternatives that empower them, transforming them from recipients of aid into active participants in development rather than mere contributors,” she said. Ms Al Shamsi cited the UAE's work with Mauritania, in north-west Africa to reduce maternal mortality by training women as midwives. About 30 women have undergone six months of training as midwives to curtail the number of deaths among women and children during childbirth. She said such programmes demonstrated the value of investing in the skills and capabilities of people within vulnerable communities. “Empowering this human capital is vital, as they are partners in this transformation and uniquely capable of finding solutions, especially if they are empowered in the field of technology, encouraged to innovate and their capabilities strengthened to face all circumstances,” she said. The call to harness people power comes as humanitarian aid organisations grapple with a sustained drop in funding for their essential work. “Humanitarian resources are stretched and the gap between what we know how to do and what we have the resources to do is becoming dangerously wide,” Rania Dagash-Kamara, assistant executive director for partnerships and innovation at the World Food Programme, said during the two-day event, being held at Dubai World Trade Centre. Ms Al Shamsi also highlighted the need to prepare women in conflict-prone areas for displacement and other risks before emergencies occur. “It is illogical to wait for danger to occur before finding ways to deal with it. Rather, proactive preparation is necessary, providing women, in particular, with training opportunities to confront any danger such as displacement or forced migration,” Ms Al Shamsi said. She spoke of the vision of Sheikha Fatima bint Mubarak, the Mother of the Nation, for the protection and training of women in conflict zones and for addressing the dangers of forced migration. She stressed that protection training should be integrated into existing programmes for women in areas where forced migration and armed conflicts are likely to occur. According to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, there are more than 41 million refugees worldwide. For the World Food Programme, partnerships were critical to changing lives and rebuilding dignity. Ms Kamara said better data and technology could save lives through early warning systems that prevent catastrophe in the event of floods, cyclones and other natural disasters. “Technology and innovation help us to reach people faster, target assistance and make scarce resources go further,” she said. She said continued co-operation with countries such as the UAE was important in responding to emergencies and reaching vulnerable populations. “The UAE is a key partner for us who has, together with us, responded to emergencies, advocated for the most vulnerable, and worked alongside us to overcome some of the world’s most difficult challenges,” Ms Kamara said. Ahmed Al Muhairi, director general of the Islamic Affairs and Charitable Activities Department (IACAD), Dubai, said the humanitarian sector needed to move from crisis management to preparedness. He said the shift would be from providing assistance to community empowerment, and from individual action to integration, partnership and trust, to help the world face the current set of natural disasters and economic crises. “The question today is not related to the volume of expenses or how many projects we have done. Real humanitarian action is not measured in relation to the size of resources or by the number of initiatives but is measured by regaining hope and empowerment for a better life,” Mr Al Muhairi said. The Dihad conference is in its 22 nd year and addresses how governments and organisations can work together to address displacement caused by armed conflict and climate-related disasters that are becoming more frequent.

title: US announces sweeping new set of sanctions against Iran
description: Bessent expects more countries to join in halting Iran trade ties
content: The US has announced a sweeping new set of sanctions on Iran, as Washington seeks to isolate the country’s economy in an effort to break the deadlock in the war. In what it referred to as “Operation Economic Outcast”, the Treasury Department said it was broadening the scope of secondary sanctions on companies and countries that do business with Iran . It said every country would be given a deadline to shut down Iran-related activity and serve a final notice to cut its economic ties. “Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” said US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The Treasury said it had identified five sectors Tehran uses to support its economy – digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. The department also imposed sanctions on 60 companies, people and ships it accused of supporting Iran’s nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations and oil revenue generation networks. The US has also suspended licences that had authorised remittance payments to Iran. Any business or country operating on Iran’s behalf could be cut off from the dollar-based financial system, the Treasury warned. The Trump administration has shifted from military operations to economic pressure after a bombing campaign and naval blockade of Iranian ports failed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for about 20 per cent of the world’s energy supplies. Iran’s rial slumped to a new low against the US dollar before Monday's announcement, with the currency trading at about two million to the dollar after falling by 4.5 per cent since last week, when President Donald Trump threatened to impose new sanctions. Meanwhile, inflation remains higher than 80 per cent in the country of 93 million people. Oil shipments from Iran have all but dried up, cutting off a key source of government revenue. “Iran is completely collapsing,” Mr Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform. Describing the latest announcement as an “economic D-Day”, Washington has said countries must side with the US or risk becoming “global pariahs”. “Those who tether themselves to Tehran should expect to share in the isolation of a withering regime,” Mr Bessent said. It was not clear how Russia, China, India and Turkey – all of which maintain strong business ties with Iran – would be affected by the sanctions. However, Mr Bessent singled out countries that enable Tehran’s energy exports, financial transfers, aviation, shipping and banking. The US has previously imposed sanctions on independent Chinese “teapot refineries”, which buy discounted Iranian crude. Taking further action against Chinese banks could provoke tension before President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington next month and may unravel a trade truce the two countries agreed to last year, while China’s rare-earth mineral restrictions also loom. The UAE announced it was severing trade and financial tie s with Tehran last week. The announcement came after two Iranian missiles were fired at the Emirates, and drone attacks on Adnoc-owned ships. “I would think that the actions they took last week were not a coincident, but likely causal,” Mr Bessent said of the Emirates. He added that he believed other countries would follow suit. The US and Israel launched co-ordinated strikes against Iran on February 28, killing its supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran retaliated by launching hundreds of drones and missiles at Gulf states, attacking US military sites across the region as well as vital energy infrastructure and desalination plants. “The UAE have been very good partners and have taken the brunt of the Iranian attacks in the Gulf,” Mr Bessent said. Currently, diplomatic talks between the US and Iran remain at a standstill and the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, disrupting global energy flows. Tehran has for decades weathered economic sanctions against its financial, aviation and cryptocurrency sectors, as well as members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Last month, the US Treasury imposed sanctions on more than 100 ships linked to Iran’s shadow fleet, which it describes as a covert logistics network that allows Tehran to keep oil revenues flowing. Washington has also placed restrictions on exchange houses, clandestine currency networks and cryptocurrency channels used by Tehran to move money outside the conventional banking system. The EU, UK, Canada, Australia and Ukraine have also imposed measures against Tehran, while UN sanctions against Iran’s nuclear and missile activities were reimposed in September last year through the snapback process under the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action. The UN measures include restrictions on arms transfers, sensitive nuclear materials and technology, ballistic missile activity, asset freezes and other limits on designated people and entities. Iran had vowed to retaliate against any new US sanctions. In a post on social media, Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, threatened that any country that joins the US economic campaign would be treated as an “enemy”. The result would be that “not a single drop of oil will be exported, neither through the Strait of Hormuz nor from anywhere” in the Gulf, he added. Tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has been dwindling since the war began. Yesterday, a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile west of the Saudi port city of Yanbu, leading to a fire on the ship’s main deck, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said. All crew members were safe and accounted for, with no reported environmental damage. Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Iran yesterday for talks, which Islamabad said were intended to “promote regional peace and stability”. Badr Al Busaidi, Oman’s Foreign Minister, is scheduled to visit Tehran today to continue negotiations on the management of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: UN chief proposes mechanism to protect fertiliser flow through Strait of Hormuz
description: Oil prices remain about 33 per cent higher since start of conflict
content: UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Monday proposed a new mechanism to keep fertiliser and other essential goods moving through the Strait of Hormuz . The UN chief's comments came as he warned that traffic through one of the world's most important shipping routes had nearly ground to a halt as conflict drives up global energy and food costs. Oil prices remain about 33 per cent higher than at the start of the conflict, while global container rates have risen 84 per cent from a year ago, Mr Guterres told reporters in New York. Fertiliser and other essential input costs are also climbing sharply. “These crises are choking arteries of global trade and squeezing the global food system especially hard,” Mr Guterres said, citing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and shipping routes also affected by the war in Ukraine. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that Iran was “collapsing” as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign. The US naval blockade of Iran has resulted in Tehran's oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz falling from two million barrels a day prewar to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important energy chokepoints, handling around a quarter of global seaborne oil trade as well as significant flows of liquefied natural gas and fertilisers. The disruption has intensified as efforts to end the US-Iran conflict have stalled. Tehran continues to blockade the strait, which it did not restrict before the war, driving up global inflation and increasing domestic pressure on Mr Trump ahead of midterm elections in November. Mr Guterres said a UN task force he established in March had developed a time-bound confidence-building mechanism initially focused on fertilisers and related raw materials, with the possibility of extending it to other products. Under the initiative, the UN would act as a neutral facilitator to reduce immediate risks and support more orderly and predictable transit through the Strait of Hormuz. It would not authorise passage through the strait or alter states' rights or obligations under international law, he said. “It can be operationalised quickly,” he added. “All the parties involved have a detailed knowledge of … how the mechanism would work,” Mr Guterres said. The UN chief also called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the Black Sea, an end to attacks on shipping in the Red Sea and around the Bab Al Mandeb, and the full restoration of navigational rights in Hormuz. “Maritime chokepoints must never become instruments of coercion,” he warned. “And the world's food supply must never become collateral damage of conflict.”

title: Abu Dhabi F1 concerts: 65 artists who have performed, from Beyonce to Katy Perry
description: Before the 2026 race, we look back at the artists who have taken to the stage since the inaugural Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in 2009
content: The confirmation that the Formula 1 Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix 2026 will go ahead as planned means the return of one of the country’s longest-running music events. Since the inaugural race in 2009, live music has played an integral role in the weekend, with up to four concerts staged at the end of each day at Etihad Live , formerly known as Etihad Park. The headliners have ranged from pop star Beyonce and rapper Eminem to rockers The Who and heavy metal titans Metallica. Along the way, the concerts have marked musical milestones both minor and major. Beyonce played the biggest show of her 2009 world tour, Kings of Leon made their Middle East debut that same weekend, Armin van Buuren became the first DJ to headline the series in 2014 and Rihanna’s 2016 appearance marked the final date of her most recent run, the Anti World Tour . This year’s concert offerings feature Swedish pop star Zara Larsson and British soul singer Lewis Capaldi on Thursday, December 3, before a Saturday, December 5, show by rock group Imagine Dragons . The artists performing on Friday and race day on Sunday are yet to be announced. Over the years, 65 acts have taken to the stage with shows big and small, loud and mellow, brilliant and, in a few cases, underwhelming. We head down memory lane to look back at those who have taken to the stage since 2009 ... Not only was the gig part of her first solo world tour, but the burgeoning pop star's show was the biggest of the tour, says Lickrish. Nearly 40,000 people packed Etihad Park to see Bey perform a selection of solo hits including Crazy in Love and Irreplaceable, and a fiery medley of Destiny's Child tracks including Say My Name and Survivor. While the UK group only played a handful of shows that year, they were a well-oiled machine in Abu Dhabi with a sparkling set that took off with the stomping The Kids and went on to include favourites Little L and Canned Heat . The sextet ended the show with the one-two punch of Love Foolosophy and Deeper Undergound , transforming Etihad Park into a mammoth open-air club. The US rockers made their debut performance in the Middle East on the back of a tour supporting their fourth album Only by the Night . The crowd were able to hear fresh takes on hits Sex on Fire and Use Somebody as well older tracks King of the Rodeo and California Waiting. The historic inaugural Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend ended with the US rockers performing a greatest hits set which included Walk this Way and I Don't Want to Miss a Thing . The performance helped set the course for future Abu Dhabi Formula One race day concerts, in that they mostly comprised artists with a big catalogue of anthems. could be argued that West was in his prime during this period. Ten days before releasing his career-best album, My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy , the rapper performed a commanding set that included album bangers Monster and Power , in addition to fan favourites Diamonds from Sierra Leone and Touch the Sky . A bittersweet experience for seasoned UAE concertgoers, with Linkin Park singer, the late Chester Bennington, in roaring form as he tore through many of the band's powerful anthems including What I've Done and In the End. The group ended their show with their hit, One Step Closer . The Purple One began the gig with the storming 1984 hit Let's Go Crazy , and the crowd responded in kind in what has come to be viewed as one of the UAE's greatest ever concerts. Backed by cracking musicians, Prince delivered a celebratory set including Little Red Corvette and Raspberry Beret, in addition to covers of Chic's Le Freak and Sarah McLachlan ballad Angel. The show featured up to four encores, including a guest appearance by The Pussycat Doll Nicole Scherzinger for the Sheila E. cover, A Love Bizarre. The pop diva was not at her best in Abu Dhabi. Despite an enthusiastic crowd, Spears went through the motions in a surprisingly short 70-minute show that was high on choreography but low on energy. While the hits were performed, they were bizarrely cut short for medleys, including a completely unnecessary fusion of Baby One More Time with Rihanna's S&M. One of the oddest Abu Dhabi Grand Prix shows to date. With a major rock act pulling out in the figurative last minutes before the big day, promoters Flash Entertainment hustled to pull together a show worthy for rock fans. On paper, nu-metal group Incubus and goth-rockers The Cult are both successful in their own right, but putting them back to back in one night seemed too random for even the most eclectic listener. It arguably remains, one of the smallest crowds to attend an after-race concert. The greatest ever Abu Dhabi Formula One gig is a close tie between Prince in 2010 and Paul McCartney. Even if the Beatle delivered those timeless group and solo hits half-heartedly, it still would have been a great gig. But McCartney, 69 years old at the time, was more than up for it and was in fine voice in an epic 37-song set which featured The Beatles' Hey Jude and Get Back, Wings favourite Jet and Live and Let Die, and solo classic Maybe I'm Amazed. Opening with the hit Wow and ending with modern pop classic Spinning Around , the Aussie pop star was all class and verve in what was a great performance. Minogue kept it fun and breezy throughout the night and fortunately jettisoned the snooze-worthy material from her ill-fated dalliance with electronica and trip hop in the early 2000s for the jubilant sounds of Kids and the ever-green classic The Loco-Motion . The surprising thing is that perennial rock punchlines Nickelback are far more fun than they get credit for. Critics deride the group for peddling second-rate grunge, but live, the group look further back to the glam acts of the 1980s. The big hit Something in Your Mouth is a modern-day version of Motley Crue's Girls, Girls, Girls , while Bottoms Up is the kind of stomping hard-rock Poison rode to fame on. Nickelback performed these songs well enough, with lead singer Chad Kroeger in fine voice. Eminem's thrilling set at du Arena confirmed his status as a pop phenomenon and was a great illustration of hip-hop's growth from street corners to stadium-filling spectaculars. Backed by an eight-piece band and hype man Mr Porter (also known as the Kon Artist from rap collective D12), Eminem stepped onstage to the urgent riffs of Won't Back Down before launching into the forceful 3 a.m. . While intensely chewing up the stage throughout the show, levity was regularly supplied with big anthems I Need a Doctor and Love The Way You Lie. A Dr Dre-produced medley of My Name Is and The Real Slim Shady was performed before the set was rounded off with Without Me, Not Afraid and the encore Lose Yourself - the latter cementing itself as the Eye of the Tiger for this generation. One of the first of a short-lived run of Arabic Abu Dhabi Formula One after-race concerts featuring an all-star line-up. Egyptian pop-star Amr Diab led a strong bill including Lebanese singer Elissa and Emirati Hussain Al Jassmi for a hit-filled night representing the best of the genre. After an increasing number of bloated album releases, the superstar went back to basics when he stepped onto the stage at Etihad Park. With the exception of the strobe lights and LED screens, Jay Z's stage presence was deliberately stripped down. Only four musicians - including special guest and music giant in his own right, Timbaland, on the keys and beat machine - stood behind on an elevated stage. With such a relatively simple set-up the only way Jay Z could engage the large Etihad Park field was through pure energy. This is what he did brilliantly, with a kinetic set that had the crowd on their feet. Swaggering on to the symphonic backdrop of Higher , Jay Z tore into the thumping set including You Don't Know , On to the Next One and 99 Problems . Even a 10-minute stage blackout due to a technical glitch didn't detract from what was a triumphant performance. Another left field choice for the event but a welcome one. British prog rockers Muse took us outer space with their dense and cinematic sounds that's both ethereal and thunderous. From Supermassive Black Hole and United States of Eurasia to Madness and Unnatural Selection , they managed to retain the audience's attention throughout their challenging set due to their exhilarating musicianship. This was no warm and fuzzy trip down memory lane, a la Paul McCartney in 2011. The goth kings reminded us they are still a dark musical force by opening the show with tracks from their latest album, Delta Machine . The bruising opener Welcome to My World relied on singer Dave Gahan’s crystalline vocals to inject some much-needed light into the aural gloom. The group’s vintage synth sounds came to the fore in Policy of Truth before Martin Gore took the lead and performed a torch-song version of the fan favourite Shake the Disease . Rounding off with an encore featuring the sprightly Just Can’t Get Enough , the hard-rocking Feel You and the kiss-off Never Let You Down Again , the Mode proved they are in no danger of slowing down. Another bumper bill of Arab pop talent was on offer to start the Abu Dhabi Formula One music festivities that year. While Lebanon’s Carole Samaha and Egyptian Tamer Hosny provided hits stretching back two decades, the star of the night was undoubtedly Assaf. The Palestinian was still coasting off the international acclaim from winning the 2013 season of Arab Idol , and fans were out in force for what was then his biggest Abu Dhabi show to date. It was the year EDM was formally invited to the Formula One party in Abu Dhabi – when trance music survivor Armin van Buuren became the first DJ to headline the Yasalam After-Race Concerts. The Dutchman brought his club staples – such as Communication and Blue Fear – and a blinding light show for a memorable set that enshrined dance music's place in subsequent years. A Middle East debut best described as hit and miss. As a distillation of his amazing career – from solo tracks to hits produced for others – it was an awe-inspiring confirmation that Pharrell Williams could perhaps be the Quincy Jones for the streaming generation. As a performer, however, he lacked the showmanship and charisma needed to carry off an arena show – and the fact his voice gave out three-quarters of the way through didn’t help. If volume is a statement of intent, then The Who arrived in Abu Dhabi with big intentions. The influential British rockers were in emphatic form with decibel piercing opening renditions of I Can't Explain , Substitute and Who Are You? With Roger Daltrey's bluesy roar in top form and guitarist Pete Townshend's riffs as crushing as they were lyrical, The Who played one of the loudest shows of Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. The third and currently last all-Arabic pop concert held as part of the Yasalam Abu Dhabi After-Race Concerts series. This time around Cheb Khaled was the undoubted star of the show with a typically exuberant take on his native Algerian folk music tradition of Rai. Also performing was Fares Karam, who showcased his stature as one of the leading purveyors of Dabka-inspired Lebanese pop. Making a welcome appearance was Emirati singer Aryam with a comeback show after more than a year away from the stage. The Spanish star’s songbook of evergreen international hits proved an ideal fit for the casual Grand Prix crowd. But more than anything, Iglesias won Abu Dhabi over with his charm – and the heartthrob had it in spades. From the bangers I'm a Freak and I Like How It Feels to the Spanish pop of Bailamos and stirring ballad Hero , Iglesias was an energetic presence and managed to pull off a euphoric set. This is all the more impressive, considering he was met with a slightly disgruntled crowd after taking to the stage nearly 40 minutes late. Florence Welch didn't walk onto the stage of Etihad Park. Instead, it seemed like she floated, with her long flared trousers and puffy blue blouse trailing behind her. Backed by "the Machine," an 11-piece group of singers, guitarists, harpists and drummers, the ethereal singer and group cast a spell on the Abu Dhabi crowd with songs swinging from baroque-pop to progressive and histrionic rock. Highlights include the brazen Ship to Wreck and the crowd favourite Rabbit Heart (Raise it Up ). Soulful and eccentric, Florence + the Machine were on point. With the veteran Britpop group reforming six years prior to their Abu Dhabi debut, the band felt rejuvenated with a swaggering set featuring 1990s favourites Girls and Boys and Park Life, and tracks from new album The Magic Whip. UAE fans even got a treat with Blur performing Country House, reportedly the first time they'd played their sole UK No 1 hit on tour that year. One of the less remarkable shows of the Abu Dhabi Formula One, with the Cuban-American rapper Pitbull functioning at half speed at Etihad Park. While backed by a gaggle of dancers, and clad in a designer suit and shades, "Mr Worldwide" seemed disconnected throughout the set and played second fiddle to many of his own songs. An affliction that could be blamed on the amount of guest vocalists he employs, so much so that his own raps seemed an afterthought in tracks such as International Love and Hey Baby (Drop it to the Floor). “Hey boy, hey girl, superstar DJs – here we go.” So began The Chemical Brothers' 1999 smash Hey Boy Hey Girl – which launched the British dance duo's Abu Dhabi gig. The Chemical Brothers delivered an uncompromising 90-minute set drawing from more than two decades of work. A key moment was the back-to-back arrival of hits Galvanise and Block Rockin' Beats . Delivered casually without pomp, the duo showcased how electronic music can maintain the integrity of a club performance in an open-air arena. A promoters dream, Lionel Richie has been giving the fans what they want for decades without missing a beat. Once again, the singer-songwriter delivered the goods with an all-killer, no-filler set of hits from his imperial 1980s chartbusting period as well as his time with funk group Commodores. Delivered with conviction, tender tracks Easy and Stuck on You gave us the feels while party anthems All Night Long and Dancing on the Ceiling had the perfect mix of energy and irony to make for a wonderful evening. The Bajan superstar delivered a slick yet engaging set that catered to the eyes as much as the ears. With a startling backdrop of brooding lights and large screens with evocative imagery, RiRi's show featured plenty of tracks from her experimental album Anti . Set highlights included the anthem Love the Way You Lie, the abrasive beats of Birthday Cake and the tropical treat that is Rude Boy . Rihanna's Abu Dhabi show remains her last official tour performance, with the singer spending the ensuing years turning her fashion and beauty Fenty lines into a global success. With lasers, fire and smoke, one of the world's highest paid DJs managed to seamlessly transition songs from top hits on the billboards to fan favourites – such as the remix of House of Pain's Jump Around – to keep the energy going throughout the night.
