Other tracks featured in the set included My Way and Sweet Nothing, all serving to prove how Harris dominated radio and clubland at the time. A replacement for fellow hip-hop star Kendrick Lamar, who pulled out weeks before the show, J Cole more than managed to assuage the disappointment. Dressed in a white Bob Marley shirt and tracksuit pants, Cole began his set with the brooding For Whom The Bell Tolls , which had him swiftly moving from a smooth croon to forceful rapping. Next up was Immortal , in which Cole looks back at his turbulent childhood over a stuttering bass heavy beat. By the time the soothing Vile Mentality came along, with its mix of spoken word and soulful vocals, the crowd were with him all the way. The London-based folk-rock troubadours were an intriguing prospect, considering they come after the two commercial radio friendly pop acts of Calvin Harris and J Cole. Could they sustain the energy created by their peers? Well, just about, with a solid set showcasing their deft interplay of double bass, violin, guitar and bass. While Little Lion Man and I Will Wait got a warm response from the crowd, Mumford & Sons's gig can be charitably described as a fans-only affair. No wonder the US pop star elected to stay away from the celebrity action of the Yas Marina Circuit earlier in the day in order to prepare for the show. With the high-end production and acrobatics, let alone belting out nearly two decades’ worth of hits, the singer had a lot on her plate when stepping into the arena. Fortunately, she handled it all with aplomb, delivering a show that was both joyful and feisty. From the rousing Let's Get the Party Started and U + Ur Hand, to the rollicking Trouble , Pink illustrated why she remains one pop music's biggest live draws. Throughout his 70-minute show, Malone was a riot of contradictions: his trademark slacker attitude perfectly represented in his choice of stage costume: pyjamas. But he is still a hip-hop lover, so those expensive sneakers were there for all to see. Sometimes claiming to be a hip-hop artist, Malone was not joined on stage by an accompanying DJ. Instead, he did it solo – literally. With two dozen spotlights behind, as well as a large screen, a solitary Malone carried the show himself as he sang instrumental version of his hits, including White Iverson and Better Now . It was a risky move that ultimately paid off. It allowed us to move past the pointless musical debates and his penchant for face tattoos – he has “always” and “tired" inked beneath each eye – and focus on his talent instead. After years of playing small clubs in the UAE, The Weeknd returned to perform his biggest show yet. Armed with hits from successful album Starboy, the Canadian stayed true to the stark aesthetic of the release with minimal stage design and powerful light show. From Pray for Me and Secrets to I Can't Feel My Face , The Weeknd remained cool at all times, his aloof onstage persona making for an intriguing juxtaposition with the emotionally wrenching material of the songs. A low-key triumph. Nearly a decade on, we have become used to the Saturday slot often reserved for a low-key act, so the crowd knew what to expect from Sam Smith. While the UK crooner delivered the customary ballads, such as Money on my Mind , they showed us they are capable of being at home with upbeat electro tracks, such as the Calvin Harris-produced Promises and the jazzy Omen , with UK dance duo Disclosure. That balance of both sounds resulted in a well-received set that should have broken some misconceptions surrounding the singer – the main one being Smith doesn't always sound miserable. A show that left frustrated fans wondering what could have been. The rock behemoths were on their way to deliver another blazing show as part of their epic world tour, with winning takes of It's So Easy and Mr Brownstone and a wonderfully demented version of Welcome to the Jungle, only for the concert to falter due to singer Axl Rose feeling visibly unwell. Despite that, the band managed to play nearly 90 minutes without an encore that would have normally featured fan favourites Paradise City and Night Train. That said, while ultimately underwhelming, one has to admire Rose for keeping the show running as much as he could. The bucket-headed DJ played in front of one of the youngest crowds at an Abu Dhabi Formula One concert. With children standing on the shoulders of parents, and enthusiastic teenagers there in droves, Marshmello played TikTok-friendly favourites including Selena Gomez collaboration Wolves and the slinky rhythms of Friends with Anne-Marie. It all served to conjure a party atmosphere that was a fitting way to start off the year's Abu Dhabi Grand Prix music weekend. Such is the star power of controversial rapper Travis Scott that it took two strong artists to replace him when Scott pulled out for personal reasons. Rappers Future and Gucci Mane turned Etihad Park into a super-sized club with separate one hour slots. While Mane’s set was sloppy at times, it was Future who seized the moment. His swaggering set, featuring hits Pluto and Mask Off, was vibrant, serving as a reminder that he is only a couple of hits short of becoming an arena act in his own right. The show confirmed Del Rey is a big deal in the Mena region. After a previous sold-out show in Beirut back in 2013, the US singer was taken aback by the raucous reception from a crowd who had descended on Abu Dhabi from all corners of the Middle East. Fan posters were projected across the screens stating they travelled from Saudi Arabia and Jordan to see their musical hero, and what was delivered was a show that divided opinion. If you were a fan, then Del Rey was a hazy dream come true. If you were not, you might have been bored to tears. And if you were the casual concertgoer, it was a slightly underwhelming affair with occasional flashes of brilliance. The Las Vegas rockers took to the Etihad Park stage almost a decade ago to the day since their last appearance in Abu Dhabi. By this time, the group were one of world's biggest rock bands with more than a dozen hits to their name. Confident of their material, The Killers opened their set with the, well, killer, opening trio of Jenny was a Friend of Mine , Spaceman and Somebody Told Me. The hits continued to roll on for what was another successful conclusion to the Abu Dhabi Formula One weekend. Little did we know, the show marked the last after-race concert for about two years. Khalid's performance was both a soulful way to begin the Abu Dhabi F1 party and an emotional return for UAE music lovers to Etihad Park after more than two years. Arriving in Abu Dhabi after a low-key Bahrain show a couple of days prior, Khalid was in smooth form and was joined by dancers as he performed hits 8teen and Twenty -One. "Hi Abu Dhabi," he said. “It’s my first time in the UAE and I’m so happy to be here. Thank you Abu Dhabi for so much love." The singer went on to perform Hundred and American Teen to a big reception before ending the set with early hit Saturday Nights . Stormzy came back to the UAE and picked up where he left off. Seventeen months after a set at Redfest DXB in Dubai, the British grime rapper headlined the second of the four Abu Dhabi F1 after-race concerts at Etihad Park. “I have been looking for this show for so long,” Stormzy said. “It has been a long time since I have been on stage like this … let's make this a great memory for us with dance, vibes and energy.” Simply put: the man is happy to be back. With a DJ in the background and the venue brought to life with evocative lightning and high-tech visuals, Stormzy pounced on stage to the imperial-sounding horn blasts of opener Big Michael, a strident motivational anthem fit for the times. From the energy thanks to hits such as Audacity and Own It , the crowd was with him all the way. "Abu Dhabi, are you ready to party?” Scottish crooner Lewis Capaldi asked at the start of his show, a tongue-in-cheek comment considering the ballad-heavy nature of his work. That said, the singer-songwriter performed a set full of good vibes courtesy of singalongs like Forever and the lovely Maybe . Proving to be the ultimate charmer, halfway through the concert, Capaldi brought out a member of his crew to celebrate his birthday on stage. In a day of high drama on and off the Yas Marina Circuit, concert promoters were forced to look for a last-minute substitute act after rock group Foo Fighters cancelled owing to a medical emergency. After contacting artists far and wide, it was decided that the coveted race-day gig would be headlined by two of EDM's biggest stars. Martin Garrix and DJ Snake performed back-to-back sets and helped release the tension after a nail-biting race. Enjoying the party the most was undoubtedly Red Bull racer Max Verstappen, the newly crowned Formula One champion was spotted on stage partying with fellow Dutchman Garrix. Large occasions such as the Abu Dhabi Formula One were increasingly becoming the norm for Dave , whose star was rising at the time on the back of the previous year’s release, We’re All Alone in This Together , and his breakout album Psychodrama . Standout efforts include We’re All Alone , the ethereality of which is undercut by hard-hitting lyrics on mental health and insecurity. Professor X delivers with its bouncy beats, while Dave is all lyrical finesse in Wanna Know . As an entry point into the region, he did enough to warrant his own headline show, and UAE fans are still waiting. Usher’s return to the UAE was a case of unfinished business. His previous major appearance was at the closing ceremony of the 2012 World Parachuting Championships Dubai, which wasn’t exactly his crowd. At Etihad Park, he cut a friendly and suave figure during an hour-long journey through his greatest hits. Backed by a cracking band, horn section and dancers, Usher channelled the razzle-dazzle of his Las Vegas residency. From the stomping Caught Up to smooth ballads such as Burn , the songs were lovingly performed with his velvety croon. Confessions was another standout, with Usher leaning into its stark subject matter with an emotionally committed performance. This mature vibe suited Usher. Nearly 30 years into his career, he had nothing left to prove and had seemingly embraced his seasoned status. After reforming with an epic set at Coachella in April, Swedish House Mafia brought the full production to the Abu Dhabi F1. The trio performed beneath a structure resembling a tilting flying saucer amid frenetic visuals, lighting effects and pyrotechnics. While they had returned with the solid new album Paradise Again , their Abu Dhabi set traded heavily on nostalgic sounds. The Swedes were not the most charismatic performers and spent much of the concert in silhouette, but no extra song-and-dance routines were necessary when the set list contained some of the genre’s biggest anthems. The emotional release arrived with Don’t You Worry Child , For You and Save the World , blended together to induce the kind of euphoria that allowed the trio to reclaim their top-tier status after nearly a decade away. Kendrick Lamar delivered an explosive show. Simply put, it was the best performance by a hip-hop artist at the Abu Dhabi F1. The concert was powerful, kinetic and uncompromising, with just the right amount of production to keep the non-fan engrossed. Songs from Mr Morale & the Big Steppers were often dark explorations of childhood trauma, but Lamar made them work on the festival stage by dialling up the drama. He performed each track with the cold intensity of a supreme technician, making United in Grief and N95 feel almost operatic in their grandeur. Nearly 30,000 people bounced along to Humble and the horn-soaked funk of King Kunta . With all the performative fireworks on display, it was easy to forget how minimal the show was. Lamar took and owned the stage alone before ending with Saviour and a fireworks display. Def Leppard concluded the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend with a rollicking greatest-hits performance. Celebrating their 45th anniversary at the time, the British rockers showed they had lost none of their vigour with a euphoric greatest-hits set. They began with Take What You Want from Diamond Star Halos before dialling things back to 1981 with Let It Go . Animal still had one of the best choruses of the 1980s rock era, while Armageddon It brought out the air guitars. By the chiming introduction to Love Bites , Def Leppard were cruising towards another victorious gig. Judging by the show and the group’s enduring appeal, it was a feat achieved through consistency and having a lot of fun on the way. Ava Max opened the 2023 concert series with a high-energy performance that delighted cheering fans. Dressed in black, the American pop star arrived singing and dancing to Cold as Ice before drawing from her two albums, Heaven & Hell and Diamonds & Dancefloors . Max remained engaged with the crowd throughout, cracking jokes and inviting them to sing along. They duly obliged during Sweet but Psycho , after earlier renditions of Belladonna , Not Your Barbie Girl and Million Dollar Baby . Tiesto returned to the UAE to perform after Ava Max on the opening night of the 2023 Abu Dhabi F1 concerts. It was a mix of old and new, pairing one of dance music’s most established names with an emerging American pop talent. The two were also linked by their hit collaboration The Motto . Chris Brown’s debut Abu Dhabi concert marked a fresh beginning for the R&B star. The F1 after-race show was his first since releasing the album 11:11 earlier that month and, in many ways, was the best representation of the record. It was sprawling and eclectic, with Brown delivering a mixtape of a set spanning R&B, dance, pop and Afrobeats. Flanked by dancers, he opened with Beautiful People , a fine showcase of his silky vocals over burbling dance beats. Old-school fans were rewarded with energetic takes of Run It! and Deuces , while the new single Summer Too Hot fit neatly between those nostalgic works. Brown’s nimble feet blazed throughout, particularly during buoyant jams such as Party and Poppin’ . Shania Twain turned back the years with a hit-filled set. In her regional debut, the Canadian singer reminded audiences why she dominated the 1990s pop landscape, but also showed there was plenty left in the creative tank with new material from Queen of Me . Her warm and husky tone, flecked by that winning twang, was in fine form. Twain felt most at ease grasping a guitar, particularly during the sweet, nostalgic combination of Come On Over and You’re Still the One . She saved some of her biggest salvos for last, including From This Moment and That Don’t Impress Me Much . Man! I Feel Like a Woman! ended the evening with a therapeutic mass singalong, proving these timeless songs were worth the three-decade wait. It may have been a long time coming and a road etched with tragedy, but the Foo Fighters finally made it to the Abu Dhabi F1. The US rockers were originally due to headline the 2021 race-day show before cancelling because of the ill health of drummer Taylor Hawkins, who died the following year. After taking an emotional break, the band returned with the cathartic album But Here We Are and arrived in Abu Dhabi in scorching form. All My Life was an ideal opener, moving from a brooding verse into a wailing trio of guitars and Dave Grohl’s guttural roar. Learn to Fly had more than 20,000 voices bellowing across Etihad Park, while Breakout was simply furious. The small disappointment was the absence of songs from their latest album, But Here We Are , but this was a performance bursting with modern rock staples. As Grohl said: “It took us 28 years to get here.” Let's hope an encore performance happens much sooner. Teddy Swims could be the first viral sensation to headline his own Abu Dhabi F1 show. Several years after stunning social media with his unlikely mix of a tough, tattooed exterior and sensitive, husky voice, the Atlanta singer opened the concert series to a modest but loving crowd. Goodbye’s Been Good to You was carried by swaggering piano riffs and pinpoint vocals that quavered and croaked in all the right moments. What More Can I Say delved into the 1970s soul songbook, while Hammer to the Heart moved from melodic spoken word to an anguished howl. That winning intensity showed Swims beginning to emerge from his influences. After making her name in dance citadels such as Berlin nightclub Berghain, Peggy Gou was at ease performing on the massive Etihad Park stage. Her set crossed various rhythm-driven soundscapes, from propulsive techno beats and Latin percussion to manic jungle loops. While her refreshing takes on Dom Dolla’s Miracle Maker and Masters at Work’s Work were a treat, the true highlights were her own anthems. These included the pulsating (It Goes Like) Nanana , with its wormy synth hook, and the house-techno fusion of Starry Night . Backed by 1990s-inspired visual motifs, from chrome-coloured designs to Tamagotchis, Gou showed why her deft nods to the past cemented her place as one of dance music’s future stars. Maroon 5’s growing fortunes over almost three decades mirrored the rising spectacle of their regional concerts. Their Etihad Park appearance was one of their biggest yet, with about 30,000 people witnessing a greatest-hits set delivered with all the sleekness and professionalism of a Las Vegas show. For 90 minutes, the 20-song hit fest offered an ideal representation of the band’s commercial prowess and undeniably tight musicianship. Adam Levine’s resonant voice showed no signs of wear during Animals , while One More Night paired a faux-reggae groove with his seamless falsetto. Following the barrelling version of Moves Like Jagger , Maroon 5 ended the show with an encore of She Will Be Loved , Girls Like You and, perhaps their greatest hit, the undeniably brilliant Sugar . Fine-tuned and barely breaking a sweat, the band left the stage, making this whole pop-stardom thing look quite effortless. Eminem roared into the Abu Dhabi F1 Grand Prix for what could have been his biggest concert in the city to date. Performing to more than 40,000 people, the bittersweet show came only five days after the death of his mother, Debbie Nelson. With a dark, Gotham-like skyline behind him, Eminem emerged from a coffin wearing a hockey mask and wielding a chainsaw, recalling his early-2000s stage persona. Lucifer showcased the technical excellence and delightfully off-colour lyrics of The Death of Slim Shady , while the strident Won’t Back Down made full use of his live band. The second-ever live performance of Godzilla featured an absolutely blistering verse. With rock’s significance on the large stage increasingly confined to heritage artists, Muse remained an intriguing exception. Well into their third decade, the British trio continued to capture attention with high-concept albums and grandiose concerts brimming with pomp and spectacle. Their closing Abu Dhabi F1 concert was their first show of the year, but the time away had not left them rusty. Won’t Stand Down began with an Eastern-inspired guitar motif before launching into a wall of crushing guitars and Dominic Howard’s thunderous drumming. On Hysteria , Matt Bellamy’s potent vocals were matched by Chris Wolstenholme’s dazzling basslines. It conjured the kind of energy only a committed rock band could deliver and showed Muse had lost none of their grandeur and bite. They say that in show business, you should save your best tricks for last. Benson Boone clearly missed the memo. The American opened the concert series with his trademark flip, one of half a dozen in the first hour alone. Despite arriving from the US only a day earlier and feeling jet-lagged, he delivered a Middle East debut that was both fun and sweet. There were shades of Freddie Mercury and the Killers frontman Brandon Flowers in a voice that could be bombastic and tender in the same song. I Wanna Be the One You Call displayed his high register, while Wanted Man paired a strutting bassline with his crystalline falsetto. Boone lifted some of his songs through sheer force of will, turning Man in Me into a startling live epic. Elyanna’s return to Abu Dhabi marked the end of a year that pushed her forward. After supporting Coldplay at Zayed Sports City Stadium in January, she stepped on to the Etihad Park stage with more assurance. The set moved between 1990s-inspired Arabic pop, mahraganat, Levant wedding music and folk, all held together by dynamic modern production. A dabke section was folded cleanly into the flow, while Mama Eh moved from power in the verse to a more vulnerable melody. Ghareeb Alay began as a ballad before pivoting into an earthy dub rhythm. She ended with Ganeni , its sharp choreography and explosive visuals hopefully hinting at a future solo arena tour. Post Malone returned to the Abu Dhabi F1 concerts seven years after his maiden Middle East performance at the event. Performing after Elyanna, the American headlined the second night with a genre-blending catalogue spanning hip-hop-infused pop hits such as Sunflower and Circles and the country music direction of his album F-1 Trillion . The appearance was his third at Etihad Park. His 2018 F1 debut saw him carry the show alone as he sang to instrumental versions of hits including White Iverson and Better Now . It was a risky move that ultimately paid off. He returned to the venue in 2022 for another hit-filled show , receiving a rapturous reception with songs including the tender Sunflower , the bouncy hip-hop of Wow. , the summery I Like You (A Happier Song) and the dark synth-pop of One Right Now . Metallica’s return to Etihad Park could comfortably be described as their Middle East hometown show, having packed more than 25,000 fans on all three visits. It was the biggest crowd of that year’s F1 concert series, with the band performing with scintillating precision and drive. Forty years at the forefront of heavy metal had not dimmed them. Although they arrived behind 72 Seasons , the Abu Dhabi concert was a greatest-hits display of their power and precision. Creeping Death remained as direct as ever, while Fuel was a cyclonic hit of guitars and frenetic pyro. The band closed with One , Master of Puppets and Enter Sandman , leaving the stage to fireworks and further evidence that Abu Dhabi had earned its place in the global “Metallica family”. Katy Perry was trying to make lemonade out of lemons. After the cool reaction to her album 143 , she launched a full-scale world tour that reminded fans of her pedigree and placed the new songs in a sharper live setting. Her race-day concert was built around more than 30 LED screens, with Perry descending on to the stage as a humanoid figure. She began with Chained to the Rhythm before delivering a fresh, rock-leaning take on Dark Horse that played better outdoors than it did in its original production. Even overlooked 143 tracks such as Nirvana and Crush gained more drive within the larger routine. Perry closed with Firework , its sky-scraping chorus fitting her booming voice and showing a bruised pop star still moving forward.

title: Jordan and China seek answer to 'root causes' of war as King Abdullah meets Xi Jinping
description: Leaders hold talks in Beijing on Middle East issues
content: Jordan and China called for a negotiated end to the US-Iran war that addresses the “root causes” of the conflict after King Abdullah met President Xi Jinping in Beijing on Monday. After the leaders discussed Middle East affairs, a joint statement said “normal navigation” should be restored to the Strait of Hormuz and called for a “comprehensive solution” to replace the flimsy US-Iran ceasefire. They also accused Israel of initiating a “dangerous escalation” in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem, as episodes of settler violence pile up. Mr Xi said the Palestinian issue “is the core of the Middle East issue”. King Abdullah met Mr Xi on the final day of a week-long visit to China, seeking economic opportunities for Jordan in industries such as farming, medicine and engineering. Several agreements were signed in what King Abdullah said was a sign of “shared determination to continue building on their strong ties”. The two heads of state discussed Gaza, the West Bank and Iran. “The ceasefire between the US and Iran should be maintained, and a comprehensive solution capable of eliminating the root causes of tensions should be reached through dialogue and negotiation,” their joint statement said. It said Jordan and China expressed “deep concern at Israel’s dangerous escalation of the situation in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, including the increasing frequency of settler violence, land confiscation, and the construction and expansion of settlements”. China is one of several countries to have positioned itself as a potential peacemaker in the Iran conflict. In March, China and Pakistan put forward a five-point proposal that called for safe passage in the Strait of Hormuz and an end to attacks on power plants. A new US sanctions announcement for Iran on Monday could increase pressure on China, which reported $9.96 billion in trade with the Iranians last year. The true figure may be significantly higher due to unreported Iranian crude oil exports. China is also the buyer of a fifth of Jordan's imports, the biggest share of any country. The costs of those imports have increased sharply as a result of disruption to shipping between the Middle East and Asia.

title: Harry and Meghan's UK return should inspire Andy Burnham to tweak the tax code
description: The Prime Minister has a new opening to court wealth creators
content: News that the UK’s revenue commissioners plan to access individual homes to enforce a new wealth tax on £2 million ($2.7million)-plus properties marks a new low in the country’s scramble for finance from its richest. It is a policy that new Prime Minister Andy Burnham inherited from his predecessor, Keir Starmer, but the buck inevitably stops at the door of 10 Downing Street. Among those most certain to face this knock on the door is royal couple Harry and Meghan, who are moving back to England from California in time for the new school year. Mr Burnham has said in relation to providing for the couple’s security that the return to the UK is a private individual matter, not an issue of state. As most of the UK media’s coverage surrounding the couple tends to revolve around money, there is another tier to the story of their return to the UK after a six-year escape to the New World . It is perhaps time for Mr Burnham to rethink not only his stance towards the errant prince but also his governing Labour party’s failing tax regime for the rich and wealth creators. The concerns this week over the new surcharge and inspection regime for homes valued in the millions, which are predominantly in London and England’s south-east, could serve as a moment to go back to the drawing board. Mr Burnham has brought two elements to his first month in power. One is that he strikes a note of optimism as he goes about his political message. This is in stark contrast to Mr Starmer who talked the country’s economic and fiscal prospects down in an effort to crush the last remnants of Conservative reputation. Mr Burnham is rolling out a new type of party politics, and we have only glimpsed a fragment of his ultimate vision. The second is that Mr Burnham knows the intensity of the video-based messaging he must sustain to keep the focus on his leadership in the way that serves his need. In his success at mastering the hand-shot video, the new Prime Minister is explicitly an influencer using his output to shape the agenda. In this respect, he will no doubt recognise the potency of the Harry and Meghan brand as an image-maker for the UK. Cast in this light, it is possible to see Prince Harry’s return as a gain for the UK in terms of wealth creators on the move. Although their reasons for quitting Britain in 2017 were rooted in a royal schism, the prince and his actress-wife were at the head of a wave that has seen thousands of the wealthiest leaving. The UAE has seen its resident population of working Britons rise above an estimated 200,000 in this time as it became one of the leading destinations for aspirational residents quitting the UK tax system. Alongside Italy, Greece and Portugal, the Emirates is a magnet for opportunities tapped by those leaving the UK. After six years away, some commentators noted that Prince Harry could already count on one tax benefit from his time abroad. Nimesh Shah, a tax adviser, wrote that the couple could avail of capital gains tax exemptions under “temporary non-resident” rules. There is, potentially, one cloud on the horizon from their time in California if voters there endorse the Proposition 40 wealth tax on the ballot in November: they will be subject to a 5 per cent levy on their wealth as of January 1 this year. So taxes matter in the movements of Prince Harry and Meghan, and this is something that Mr Burnham could reflect on with his own plans. The signature first budget of his premiership is due in the autumn, and it represents a chance to change the tone. Having the confidence to see the return of people like the Duke and Duchess to the UK as a turning of the tide for Britain under Labour could even boost revenues in the long run. After all, using the Laffer Curve theory – which says that revenues can remain the same even as taxes are cut – the government can bring in the same amount of revenue, or more, by encouraging people to stay rather than leave. There are doubts that a rejig of the so-called non-dom tax regime under both the Conservatives and Mr Starmer is going to work. Officials have been betting that abolishing tax breaks on overseas wealth of the 75,000 tax papers involved would bring in about £33 billion in extra taxes, but experts say a steady drain of these people is undermining the forecasts. Reinforcing his optimism agenda by having wealth creators onside is a trick that Mr Burnham pulled off as a populist mayor of Manchester. He would be well advised to see a royal return as a chance to make a similar leap away from his predecessors’ failures on the tax front.

title: UK energy alert issued after Iranian cyber attack on power plant
description: Hackers linked to IRGC are suspected to have carried out attack
content: Power companies in the UK have been put on alert after hackers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shut down an energy site. The attack took place in July and is suspected to have been carried out by a group calling itself CyberAv3ngers, which is affiliated with the IRGC's electronic warfare arm and specialises in breaching infrastructure. The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero has insisted the attack was on a small plant and that at no point was there a risk to the wider energy system. But the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), which is a branch of the signals intelligence agency GCHQ, has sent out an alert to energy companies, the department added. “In response to this specific incident, the NCSC and Department for Energy Security and Net Zero briefed energy CEOs and directly wrote to companies with advice, direction and next steps,” said a representative. “The UK has a highly resilient energy system. We work closely with the energy sector to protect infrastructure and ensure the highest security standards." Michael Shanks, the Minister for Energy, said the government and industry had taken the incident seriously and were working with regulators and the NCSC to assess threats and strengthen protections. Richard Moore, the former head of the MI6 overseas spy agency, said the UK faced cyber attacks from a number of states. “The fact is that a combination of China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are all focused on cyber-attacks against the UK, as they are against many other western and democratic societies, and again, it comes back to the importance for us of building our own resilience and ability,” he told the BBC. The IRGC's electronic warfare arm is headed by Hamid Lashgarian, who was placed under sanctions in 2024 by the US. Washington has offered a $10 million reward for information about his activities. The US says that CyberAv3ngers are affiliated with the IRGC’s Cyber-Electronic Command. The hackers have compromised the Vision series of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) made by Israel-based Unitronic. The PLCs are rugged, industrial-grade computers designed to automate machinery, manufacturing lines, and critical infrastructure. They are used by the water and wastewater, energy, food and beverage, manufacturing, healthcare and other industries. A recent report by cyber security company Tenable found that CyberAv3ngers has “repeatedly compromised small water utilities, municipal facilities, and rural energy operators, and the reason is structural, not coincidental”. Tenable said many of these organisations use remote access tools such as TeamViewer or AnyDesk and also expose their PLCs “directly to the public internet,” making them vulnerable to attack.

title: Russia accuses Burnham of fuelling Ukraine war
description: British leader makes first overseas visit to Kyiv on Ukrainian Independence Day
content: The Kremlin has accused Britain of siding with Ukraine in the war and said the latest missile announcement would fuel the fire of the conflict. As Prime Minister Andy Burnham was visiting Ukraine, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov accused Britain of doing everything it could to prevent any progress towards an eventual peace deal after it was reported UK-made drones were carrying out attacks on Russian soil. “Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime,” he said. “Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire, and methodically and regularly hatches schemes to prevent even the slightest progress in the ​peaceful settlement process.” Mr Burnham was in Ukraine on his first official visit as UK Prime Minister, where he told President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that Britain was “100 per cent behind you” and condemned what he called “outrageous threats” coming out of Moscow. He arrived in Kyiv as Ukraine was marking its Independence Day. Mr Burnham is also reportedly handing over blueprints so Ukraine can build its own long-range missiles. Moscow warned London last week of unspecified “consequences” for supplying drones to ⁠Kyiv, accusing Britain of deepening its involvement in the war following a report that British-made drones had been used for long-range strikes against Russia ​for the first time. Mr Burnham said at the time that London was fully committed to supporting Ukraine in “this illegal war”. Sir Richard Moore, the former head of MI6, told the BBC on Monday that Russia had a history of perpetrating attacks in the UK stretching back almost a decade. “All the UK is doing is supporting the Ukrainians' right to defend themselves against aggression,” he said. “Of course we need to be mindful of Russian activity and I'm afraid the Russians do have us in their sights, and we have to make sure that we are resilient enough to defend ourselves appropriately against the sort of what is sometimes called 'grey-zone activity' from the Russians.” Russia's embassy in London confirmed the country's long-standing ambassador was withdrawn this summer. Andrey Kelin left last month after seven years in the UK capital in which he developed a combative profile, warning of how the country was implicated by its support for Ukraine. “London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” declared one Telegram post by Mr Kelin. Mr Burnham used his first foreign policy speech to resist the Russian line. “Despite Russia’s outrageous threats to my country, we will continue our support for Ukraine,” he said. “Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security but the front line in keeping Europe safe.” Mr Burnham announced the UK would permit defence company MBDA to release classified information on British components of long-range Scalp missiles, so France and Ukraine can proceed with a plan for Ukrainian assembly of the missile. He is co-chairing a meeting with Mr Zelenskyy, as well as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron, who will join by video link.

title: Oman foreign minister to visit Tehran for talks on Strait of Hormuz
description: Badr Albusaidi’s Iran trip follows diplomatic efforts by Pakistan’s army chief
content: Oman's ​Foreign ⁠Minister Badr ⁠Albusaidi will ​visit Tehran ⁠on Tuesday to continue talks between Tehran ⁠and Muscat ​on ⁠the ‌Strait ​of Hormuz, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei has said. Mr Albusaidi will meet his Iranian counterpart to discuss “the security of the Strait of Hormuz and its shipping lanes”, Mr Baghaei said on Monday in a statement carried by official news outlets. “This trip is in line with strengthening Iran-Oman bilateral co-operation and continuing sustained political consultations between the two sides as littoral states of the Strait of Hormuz, to help bolster peace and stability in the region,” he added. US President Donald Trump threatened last week to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of US efforts to end the war with Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The US and Iran remain divided over how to end their months-long conflict, while Oman has pursued separate discussions with Iran over arrangements for navigation through the vital waterway. Mr Trump himself agreed in a signed document that Oman would “conduct dialogue” with Iran to define the future administration and maritime services in the strait. The 14-point memorandum of understanding negotiated in Islamabad and signed on June 17 was intended as an interim framework for ending the war, opening a window for negotiations on a longer-term nuclear agreement. The MoU expired on August 17 after the broader understanding had already collapsed amid a flurry of tit-for-tat strikes. The main dispute centred on how each side interpreted the clause on the Strait of Hormuz . Iran viewed the language in the text as recognising its right to manage the whole strait. The US, however, took it to mean that Iran must guarantee freedom of navigation and refrain from using access to vital waterways as leverage. Oman shares the strait with Iran. Last week, the Iranian Foreign Ministry said Oman and Iran had reached an “understanding” regarding the waterway and were working to finalise a joint statement. Mr Albusaidi’s scheduled arrival follows diplomatic engagements by Pakistan’s army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, who arrived in Tehran on Monday. Pakistan, which has served as an active mediator in indirect negotiations between the US and Iran, said Mr Munir’s trip was part of its efforts “to promote regional peace and stability”. The Pakistani military chief’s talks in Tehran come as the US prepares to roll out what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called “the greatest financial offensive ever” targeting Iran’s trade partners. Iran dismissed the US threat, vowing to shut down all oil exports from the ⁠Gulf “if the economic war continues”. It also issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission. Mr Bessent has promised to reveal severe measures on Iran, which has endured near-continuous economic sanctions since the Islamic Revolution of 1979. Mr Bessent issued the warning in an opinion piece published on Monday in The Financial Times . He is due to hold a press conference at 9pm UAE time. “At dawn begins an economic D-Day – the ⁠single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary,” Mr Bessent wrote.

title: Khalifa University moves into global top 200 across four UN Sustainable Development Goals
description: Abu Dhabi university rises in ratings across a number of major metrics
content: Khalifa University of Science and Technology has moved into the top 200 universities in the world across four UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), while recording a substantial improvement in its overall position in the Times Higher Education Sustainability Impact Ratings 2026. The Abu Dhabi institution moved into the 301-400 global band, rising from 401-600 in 2005, demonstrating a growing recognition of its research, innovation and partnerships. It achieved its best results in four SDGs, ranking among the top 200 in Decent Work and Economic Growth; Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure; Responsible Consumption and Production; and Partnerships for the Goals. The Times ratings assess universities worldwide against the UN SDGs, examining their contributions through research, stewardship, outreach and teaching. Professor Ebrahim Al Hajri, President of Khalifa University, said the results reflected the university’s commitment to education that delivers a tangible impact for society. “They recognise not only the quality of our research and education, but also our ability to translate scientific excellence into innovation, partnerships and solutions that advance the UAE's sustainable development ambitions,” he said. “As a research-intensive university, we remain committed to developing future talent, strengthening international collaboration and contributing to a knowledge economy that benefits our nation and the world.” In the case of other SDGs, the university also ranked in the 201-300 global band for both Clean Water and Sanitation and Reduced Inequalities. Some of the most striking gains were recorded in health and education. The university surged from the 1,001+ band to 401-600 for Good Health and Well-being, while its position for Quality Education rose from 1001+ to 601-800. The results reflect the implementation of Khalifa University’s 2025-2030 Sustainability Strategy, which integrates sustainability across research, education, campus operations and partnerships. In June, the university celebrated a UAE first after being ranked in the top 150 of a global higher education league table. The university rose 30 places to 147th in the QS World University Rankings 2027, cementing its place as the country's leading institute for the ninth consecutive year. The QS rankings evaluated 8,808 universities across 106 locations, with 1,504 institutions named in the final list. Its impressive achievements in research impact, in which it placed 87th globally in citations per faculty member, were a driving force behind its academic success. The university was ranked 12th worldwide for the international make-up of its faculty, reflecting its work in attracting and retaining top talent from around the world.

title: Palestinian family who drowned in UK to be buried in Palestinian camp in Lebanon
description: Grieving mother of Hassan Al Khawas wants to see her son and his family 'one last time' in Rashidiya Camp
content: A family of Palestinian origin who drowned off the south coast of England last week will be buried in a Palestinian refugee camp in Lebanon , according to another family member who lives there. Hassan Al Khawas, 55, his wife Zeina Alayn, 37, and daughter Sara , 14, drowned in Shoreham after getting into difficulties in the sea. Another daughter Sajad , 6, died a few days later in hospital. Mr Al Khawas – who is known to relatives as Hossam – and his wife were British citizens born in the Rashidiya refugee camp in southern Lebanon, which shelters more than 30,000 displaced Palestinian families. Sussex Police said the deaths are being treated as a tragic accident, with no third-party involvement. A ceremony of condolences has been held in London and in the family home in Rashidiya. Hassan’s brother, Jalal Al Khawas, who lives in Rashidiya, told The National the family are now waiting for the repatriation to Lebanon. “It’s important for us. His mother is old, she is over 90 years old, she wants to see him one last time,” he said. “She hadn’t seen him in a long time. She wants to see him. It has been very hard on her.” Mr Al Khawas and his family had not been to Lebanon in three years because of the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hezbollah, which particularly affects southern Lebanon. Rashidiya camp has also repeatedly been targeted or damaged by Israeli airstikes. “He wanted to come and we told him not to, we told him to wait,” his brother said. The family has been holding condolences in their home in Rashidiya camp while they wait for the bodies to arrive. Jalal said friends living in the UK had also come to comfort the family. “We’ve had Lebanese and Palestinians from London coming to our house. They were crying. Their wives were crying. They told us how Hossam always looked out for them,” he said. The two girls, he said, “had lovely life”, with Sara attending Ellen Wilkinson School in West London. “They were doing well at school, their parents cared for them,” he said. The couple’s two other children, a 15-year old girl and 10-year old boy, are being taken care of by uncles in London. Jalal said: “We will work on finding the right path for them. It will be better for them to stay in London.” But he has huge concerns about the impact the tragedy night have on them. “We hope to help the children. They were witnesses to what happened. The boy saw his father drown. This is going to be very difficult for them,” he said. There has been an increase in water-related deaths in the UK this year due to rising temperatures and a number of heatwaves. Nineteen people died in one week in May, many of them children and teenagers. The latest deaths have had a huge impact on the community in Shoreham, who held a vigil on the beach for the family on Sunday. People came with paddle-boards and kayaks as part of a commemoration ceremony. Among them was Wesley Horscroft, who attended on behalf of paddlers in the Kingston beach community. He said he had originally planned to go out alone and “put some flowers on the water” to honour the family, before he decided to invite others. “It's kind of grown and a lot of people wanted to turn up to do the same,” he told the BBC. Sara Al Khawas's school also paid tribute to the “sweet” and “well-liked” pupil. “Sara was a sweet girl, well-liked by staff and students, and she will be greatly missed,” a statement on the Ellen Wilkinson School website read. “Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with her family, friends, and all those affected. We are also thinking of her sister and loved ones at this extremely difficult time.”

title: No Other Land directors’ documentary on Israel’s ‘calculated mass killing’ to premiere at Venice
description: Film takes its title from an Israeli military term for civilians expected to be killed in an air strike
content: Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the four directors of the Oscar-winning Palestinian-Israeli documentary No Other Land , will premiere a new film about the killing of civilians in Gaza at the Venice Film Festival. Naza has been added to the festival’s main competition and will have its world premiere on September 10. The late addition completes the 21-film line-up and makes it the only documentary feature competing for the Golden Lion. “Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” the official synopsis states. The title is a military acronym used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians expected to be killed in a planned air strike, according to the filmmakers. Naza draws on investigations published between 2023 and 2025 by Israeli-Palestinian publication +972 Magazine, Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and The Guardian . The production announcement does not specify which findings will feature in the documentary. Abraham wrote several of those reports. One 2024 investigation , based on interviews with six Israeli intelligence officers, alleged that the military used an AI-powered system called Lavender to generate a list of 37,000 potential targets with apparent links to Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad militant group. The report claimed that officers performed only minimal checks on the system’s selections, with one saying he spent about 20 seconds reviewing each target. The report also alleged that suspected militants were frequently attacked inside family homes despite the expected civilian casualties. The Israeli military rejected the claims at the time. Naza is produced by The Guardian and British producer James Wilson, with Jonathan Glazer as executive producer. Wilson and Glazer previously worked together on The Zone of Interest , which won the 2024 Academy Award for Best International Feature Film . Abraham and Szor made No Other Land with Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal. The documentary chronicles the struggle against the forced displacement of Palestinian communities in Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank and became the first Palestinian production to win an Oscar when it received Best Documentary Feature in 2025. Naza joins a Venice programme that already includes two works by Palestinian directors. Ahmed Hassouna’s Gaza documentary Citizen Osama will screen out of competition, while Muayad Alayan’s Jerusalem-set drama Conversation With the Sea has been selected for Venezia Spotlight. Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania, whose Gaza drama The Voice of Hind Rajab won the Silver Lion last year, will serve on the main competition jury. The 83rd Venice Film Festival runs from September 2 to 12.

title: Masdar boosts presence in UK with second battery energy storage project
description: Commercial operations begin at 35MW Rochdale project
content: Abu Dhabi’s Masdar has launched its second battery energy storage system (BESS) project in the UK, as the company continues to boost its presence there amid higher demand for clean energy. The 35 megawatt/70 megawatt hours plant in Rochdale, near Manchester, will provide enough clean energy to power 35,000 homes a day. It follows the launch of another project in nearby Stockport in December, Masdar said on Monday. Masdar is also developing two more projects in British cities Chesterfield and Cardiff, which will have a combined capacity of 150MW. All four projects form part of Masdar’s £1 billion ($1.3 billion) investment commitment to BESS projects in the UK, as the government targets up to 27 gigawatts of battery storage by the end of this decade. Financing for the four projects was successfully completed last month, with Masdar securing up to £97 million from SMBC and ING. “As electricity demand grows and renewable generation continues to expand, battery storage is becoming an increasingly vital component of maintaining a secure, reliable and affordable electricity network,” said Husain Al Meer, executive director of global offshore wind & UK at Masdar. “Our continuing roll-out of our £1 billion pipeline reflects Masdar's long-term commitment to the UK.” BESS solutions are critical to integrating renewables into modern electricity networks, providing flexible energy to the grid by storing energy in periods of low demand and releasing it at peak times. The technology helps to balance and stabilise the intermittent supply from renewable sources and helps to boost clean energy supply to the grid. Masdar is also active in offshore wind projects in the UK. This includes a €5.2 billion co-investment with Iberdrola in the 1.4GW East Anglia Three offshore wind unit, which will power the equivalent of 1.3 million homes, and the 3GW Dogger Bank South offshore wind farm being developed in partnership with Germany’s RWE. Masdar, jointly owned by Taqa, Adnoc and Mubadala, has developed projects in a number of countries with a combined capacity of more than 65GW. The company’s global ambition is to reach 100 100GW of renewable capacity by 2030. Last month, the company signed an agreement with Montenegro’s national power utility, Elektroprivreda Crne Gore, to develop two solar projects and a hydro energy storage project as part of its European expansion plans. Although renewable energy is expanding rapidly , it is not growing fast enough to meet targets set for 2030, the International Renewable Energy Agency said last year. Capacity needs to grow by at least 16.4 per cent annually until 2030 to achieve the tripling target pledged at the Cop28 climate conference in Dubai, the Abu Dhabi-based agency said in a report.

title: Filipina star Alex Eala becomes highest-ranked Southeast Asian woman in history
description: Eala, 21, teams up with Canada's Felix Auger-Aliassime in the mixed doubles of the US Open
content: The Philippines' Alex Eala has risen to a career-high No 18 in the WTA rankings, making her the highest-ranked woman from Southeast Asia in tennis history. Eala, 21, surpassed the previous record of No 19 jointly held by Indonesia’s Yayuk Basuki and Thailand’s Tamarine Tanasugarn. The Filipina is set to take part in the singles and mixed doubles at the US Open, the fourth and final Grand Slam of the year. She will team up with Canadian Felix Auger-Aliassime in the mixed doubles on Tuesday. They face the husband-and-wife team of Gael Monfils of France and Elina Svitolina of Ukraine. The winner will advance to face either top-seeded Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic or Leylah Fernandez and Frances Tiafoe. Eala has enjoyed another successful season, winning two singles titles: the Birmingham Open in June and the Mubadala DC Open in August. Her win at Birmingham made her the first Filipino player in history to win a WTA title . Her best performance at this year's Grand Slams was a run to the fourth round at Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek .

title: 'Did you lose a bet?': Erling Haaland's haircut draws reactions from fans and footballers
description: Manchester City goal machine continues to prove he is master of memes
content: It is not often that a single haircut makes global headlines, but Erling Haaland’s decision to shave off his flowing locks – and document the process on social media – has drawn reactions from around the world. The Manchester City and Norway striker, 26, traded his long ponytail for a buzz cut, sharing the transformation in an Instagram carousel captioned: “Short hair don’t care.” The post currently has 12 million likes. The reaction went beyond fans. British and Real Madrid footballer Jude Bellingham simply commented: “No way.” Haaland also FaceTimed friends during the cut, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher , who responded: “No way mate! When’d you get that done?” On another call, former Swedish footballer Zlatan Ibrahimovic joked that he no longer recognised Haaland. “You lost a bet, or what? Block me and erase my number.” Haaland’s former Manchester City manager, Pep Guardiola , had perhaps the most envious response. Stroking his own bald head, he said: “No way! You are lucky to have hair, I would love to have hair.” The attention should come as little surprise. Recently, almost everything Haaland does has sent the internet into a frenzy. Already a superstar among football fans, this summer’s World Cup in America catapulted him to another level of fame, thanks not only to his performances on the pitch but his imposing stature, long blond hair, wildly valuable bag collection and seemingly endless ability to become central to a meme. By the end of the tournament, Haaland had become a global celebrity far beyond football. Part of his appeal is that, as someone conversant in the vernacular of the online social age, Haaland seems entirely at ease on camera and instinctively understands how to manage his online presence. He is happy to be goofy, self-deprecating and, crucially, in on the joke. It helps, of course, that he is also one of the world’s most acclaimed footballers. Were he not performing on the pitch, it is fairly safe to say there would be less tolerance for all the off-pitch fun. But his willingness to appear unfiltered also matters. At a time when celebrities can have every public move co-ordinated by teams of publicists, lawyers, managers, stylists and social media experts, Haaland comes across as joyful, spontaneous and remarkably unguarded. His belly laugh while being insulted by Ibrahimovic, for example, revealed an appealingly unpretentious side. Haaland’s new haircut – like most fresh cuts – will take a bit of getting used to but it has somehow already taken on the heft of a cultural hairstyle moment.

title: Gaza in race against time as hundreds of thousands urgently need shelter and standoff delays reconstruction
description: Recent assessment found that 94% of the population needs proper shelter
content: With a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas linking the start of reconstruction in Gaza to demilitarisation, Palestinians feel they are in a race against time. About 1.98 million people, or 94 per cent of the population, require proper shelter urgently in the enclave, a report led by the Norwegian Refugee Council and conducted through the Palestine Shelter Cluster shows. The staggering figure was released days after Israel and the Board of Peace had agreed to establish two working groups on Gaza, one on disarmament and demilitarisation, and the second on sanitation, clean water and other public health issues. However, Israel has insisted that the disarmament of militant groups must be completed before reconstruction, which is forecast to cost about $71 billion, begins in the Palestinian territory. Meanwhile, the report found that residents and families are living amid flooding, pests , and unsafe buildings, while Israeli restrictions on materials hamper repairs. Palestinian Akram Abu Humeideh, 42, begins his day before sunrise because of the heat in the tent he lives in. The displaced former teacher now lives in Al Mawasi in Khan Younis, in the south of the Gaza Strip, with his wife and four children. He starts by queuing for water, then for food at a community kitchen before finding somewhere to charge mobile phones and batteries. After that, Mr Abu Humeideh cleans around the tent and eventually tries to sleep despite insects and rodents. “Living in a tent means losing all privacy and comfort; every day becomes an exhausting struggle just to secure the basic necessities of life," he told The National . His experience is shared by hundreds of thousands of Palestinians almost three years into the Gaza war, according to the report that paints a picture of a shelter emergency that goes far beyond the destruction of homes. About 84 per cent of households were classified as living in “critical” or “catastrophic” conditions when researchers assessed their ability to perform basic domestic activities, including sleeping, cooking, washing, storing water , accessing lighting and coping with extreme temperatures. All four governorates included in the assessment, North Gaza, Gaza, Deir Al Balah and Khan Younis, were classified in Phase 4, or Critical, under the Shelter Severity Classification system; Rafah and other areas deemed inaccessible or unsafe were excluded from the study. The assessment was based on 1,951 household interviews conducted between June 14 and 28 and used a five-phase scale ranging from minimal to catastrophic. Mr Abu Humeideh's youngest daughter Leen, 6, has grown up knowing war and life in a tent. “It breaks my heart when I see her going to fill water containers or carrying a pot to the community kitchen to collect food," he said. The conditions described by Mr Abu Humeideh are reflected across the Shelter Cluster assessment. About 65 per cent of assessed households are living in tents or makeshift shelters. Tents alone accommodate 54 per cent of households, while another 11 per cent are in makeshift structures. For families who have managed to return to their homes, the alternative is not necessarily safer. Basel Abu Madi, 50, knows both realities. His family lived in a tent during the early stages of the war. When they returned to northern Gaza in January 2025, they found their three-storey home on Al Jalaa street still standing. Windows, doors, and some walls were damaged, but the structure remained largely intact. “Our happiness was indescribable,” Mr Abu Madi told The National. “We moved back in and spent a period there that felt wonderful compared with life in a tent." They stayed for about eight months. When Israel launched its Gaza city offensive in August 2025, the family was displaced to the south and returned to tents. Two months later, after the October ceasefire agreement came into effect, they went home again. But this time, their house was almost gone. Only the first floor and part of the second floor of the three-storey building remained. Over the following months, the family repaired what it could and moved back into the ruins. Mr Abu Madi now lives there with his family of eight, alongside his married son and his family of three. “Living in the remnants of your home is extremely difficult,” he said. “There is the heartbreak you feel every time you remember what your house once looked like, how you used to live there, and then see what it has become.”

title: Former Mufti of Syria sentenced to life in prison
description: Ahmad Hassoun guilty of supporting officers implicated in war crimes, among other charges
content: Syria 's highest Islamic official under the deposed Assad regime, Ahmad Badr Al Din Hassoun, has been sentenced to life in prison after being tried on charges of “incitement to violence, justification of killing and abuse of office”, the state news agency Sana said on Monday. The court also ordered the confiscation of his moveable assets. The mufti went on trial in the Fourth Criminal Court in Damascus in June. He was accused of using his position to encourage members of the former regime to crack down on anti-government protesters and supporting Russia and Iran 's intervention in the Syrian civil war. He was also charged with “publicly supporting officers implicated in war crimes”, including the former head of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force, Qassem Suleimani. Hassoun, who is in his 70s, appeared in court three times in July and for a fifth hearing this month, where his testimony was heard, video evidence against him was presented and verified, and witness statements were taken, Sana reported. “One witness said he and his family had been repeatedly extorted following his sister’s detention and had paid money and provided goods in exchange for Hassoun’s intervention,” the report said. Prosecutors had demanded the death penalty for Hassoun. The current Syrian authorities under President Ahmad Al Shara have been carrying out trials of Assad-era officials, most of whom have been sentenced to death. Most recently, former warlord Waseem Al Assad , a second cousin of the deposed dictator, received the death penalty for murder and torture committed during the civil war. He is the fourth member of the Al Assad family to be sentenced to death since the court in Damascus began issuing verdicts this month in cases related to the 2011-2024 war. The same court earlier sentenced Bashar Al Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia, along with their first cousin Atif Najib, for their role in the crackdown on public protests in Deraa, the cradle of the Syrian revolt, in 2011. The former dictator and his brother are in Russia after fleeing Syria when rebels seized power in December 2024. Last week, Lebanon handed over an Assad-era general, Adel Issa , to Syria after he was arrested in the country. He once commanded Syria’s 17th Division before being transferred in 2015 to lead ground forces in Deir Ezzor until he retired the following year. He faces charges of torture and murder.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo back with a bang and more to come from Summerville: Saudi Pro League talking points
description: Darwin Nunez spearheads new-look Diriyah attack after sealing loan move from Al Hilal
content: Matchday 3 of the Saudi Pro League gets a shift forward this week, with games on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Five teams look to maintain their perfect start to the season, with Neom joining Al Nassr, Al Hilal, Al Ahli Saudi and Al Ettifaq on six points. Cristiano Ronaldo is officially off the mark for the 2026–27 season after registering a goal in Al Nassr's 4–0 win at Al Riyadh. Ronaldo's race to 1,000 goals dominated much of the pre-season talk, but fans were made to wait to see the Al Nassr captain in action after he was given an extended break following his World Cup exploits with Portugal and his recent marriage to longtime partner Georgina Rodriguez. He watched the opening-day win over Al Fateh from the stands , and was again left out as Nassr clinched a place in the last 16 of the King's Cup, courtesy of a 4-1 victory over Diriyah. On Friday, he was introduced as a substitute in the 62nd minute, sporting a new haircut. Nassr already held a commanding 3-0 lead when Ronaldo received an Ayman Yahya pass, rolled past his marker and swept the ball past Milan Borjan in the Riyadh goal . The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is now only 23 goals away from reaching the 1,000-goal milestone. It was his first run out under new Nassr coach Ange Postecoglou. Some had questioned whether Ronaldo was a good fit for the 'Angeball' approach, but the Australian was full of praise for his 41-year-old talisman after the match. “His mentality is he always wants to play, but he made sure he did all the right things – at training he worked hard – and it was fantastic for him to get 30 minutes today," Postecoglou said. “And he scores a goal, which just shows you the measure of the man.” From there, Ronaldo flew to Paris to join world leaders Emmanuel Macron, the French president, and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as the Esports World Cup , of which he is a global ambassador, drew to a close. The jet-setter is expected back in Saudi Arabia for Nassr's next match: an away assignment to Al Ettifaq on Tuesday. Darwin Nunez's loan move from Al Hilal to Diriyah has been confirmed. The Uruguayan striker, 27, had been linked with a move to Turkish club Trabzonspor to reunite with his former Liverpool teammate Mohamed Salah , but Diriyah's persistence paid off, and he is now in line to make his debut in Wednesday's clash against Al Kholood. Joining Nunez in a new-look attack is Enzo Millot, the 24-year-old German midfielder, who joins on loan from Asian champions and Pro League rivals Al Ahli Saudi. The third addition is Adil Boulbina, who joins from Al Duhail after a season in which the winger registered 20 goal contributions in 32 Qatar Stars League games, including 13 goals. Boulbina, 23, was part of Algeria’s squad at the summer World Cup. One new arrival who got some minutes under his belt was Tijjani Reijnders. The Dutch midfielder sealed a £52-million move to Al Qadsiah last week. The former Manchester City player was introduced as a second-half substitute by coach Brendan Rodgers, but he was powerless to prevent a 1-0 defeat to Al Ittihad. "I came here to try and win trophies with my teammates – we're playing for four trophies, if I'm right," Reijnders told the SPL website. "We want to win as many as possible, and we are all very eager to do that. And, personally, I hope I can help the team as much as possible with goals and assists.” No club has spent more this summer than the £60m (£55m plus £5m in add-ons) that Al Hilal paid to purchase Crysensio Summerville from West Ham United. On his debut on August 14, Summerville won the second of Hilal's three penalties in the match against promoted Al Faisaly. Ruben Neves converted, and despite a second-half fightback, Hilal ran out 4-2 winners . His second SPL match, against Al Fayha on Thursday, was equally impressive. The Netherlands international had a hand in the first of Hilal's three goals, firing a fizzing shot that Fayha goalkeeper Orlando Mosquera could only parry into the path of Sergej Milinkovic-Savic, who scored. After Sultan Mandash doubled Hilal's lead, Summerville was given penalty duties when Theo Hernandez was bundled over in the Fayha box. Summerville, 24, opted for a Panenka penalty but fluffed his lines. It had no bearing on the outcome, with Nasser Al Dawsari adding a third to maintain Hilal's perfect start to the new campaign . “We’ve started very strong in the league; very important away game as well,” he said. “So I'm happy with the three points today.” “Obviously, the three points away from home, very important for us. We had some good attacks, but we need to finish them.” On his penalty miss, Summerville added: “Oh yeah, I should have put it away, to [seal] the game as well.” With Malcom having joined UAE club Al Jazira after his contract was terminated, coach Simone Inzaghi will look to Summerville to ignite Hilal's attack. An electric winger who shone at this summer’s World Cup, playing in all four of the Netherlands' games, Summerville said he still had plenty more to offer. “I know what I'm capable of,” Summerville said. “For me, it was a good game, like OK for me. But I know what I'm capable of; I know what I can do. So there's a lot to improve in my game, and I will go in the training ground and work on this.” All kick-offs are UAE time. Monday Neom v Al Qadsiah, 8.40pm Al Ittihad vs Al Hazem, 10pm Tuesday Abha vs Al Khaleej, 8.05pm Al Taawoun v Al Fayha, 8.10pm Al Ettifaq vs Al Nassr, 10pm Al Shabab v Al Riyadh, 10pm Wednesday Al Faisaly vs Al Fateh, 8pm Diriyah v Al Kholood, 10pm Al Hilal vs Al Ahli Saudi has been moved to September 1.

title: UK launches home inspections to determine 'mansion tax' wealth surcharge
description: Properties worth more than £2m will fall into new tax band
content: The tax authorities in the UK are to send inspectors to high-value properties to determine whether owners will pay a new wealth levy on their value. HMRC will send valuation agents with the ability to demand entry to assess whether homes are worth more than £2 million ($2.7 million) and so come under the high-value council tax surcharge, commonly known as the mansion tax . The levy was introduced by former chancellor Rachel Reeves in last year’s budget and is due to take effect in April 2028, after a consultation ended in July. Owners would be expected to pay £2,500 a year for properties worth £2 million to £2.5 million, and £3,500 for properties worth up to £3.5 million. Properties between £3.5 million and £5 million would incur a charge of £5,000 annually, while those worth more than £5 million would face a £7,500 levy. The surcharge is separate from the council tax and would rise annually with inflation. The Valuation Office, which is part of HMRC and is responsible for assessing council tax bands for homes in England and Wales, says inspections will be required where “attributes can only be confirmed internally or a re-measurement is required”. It is believed the unit is in line for additional resources to help it take on the new drive to raise extra revenue. The opposition Conservative Party pointed out that the Valuation Office has hired an extra 493 staff over the past year, which they say is in preparation for a campaign to enforce the new tax. Inspectors will carry out assessments, including the size and architectural style of homes. They will also look at the number of bedrooms, bathrooms and storeys. Anyone who “intentionally delays or obstructs” a valuation officer carrying out their duties faces a £200 fine, ministers have confirmed. Failing to provide information without a “reasonable excuse” could result in a fine of up to £500. “Hard-working families and pensioners face the prospect of HMRC tax inspectors snooping around their gardens and inside their homes, to justify hiking taxes on them,” said James Cleverly, the Conservative's shadow housing secretary. “Even homes which are below the new tax thresholds face these intrusive checks, with the threat of criminal prosecutions and fines if people refuse.” Campaigners for the surcharge argue that house prices in expensive parts of London, such as Mayfair and Knightsbridge , have become even more inflated due to the number of second homes or investment properties. Some have highlighted properties where the owners rarely visit to make an argument for freeing up housing stock for local buyers. Against this is a softening of the UK's prime property prices in face of the rising taxes. Advocates for overseas-based property interests point out a proportion of the absent owners are UK-tied individuals who have retained property in the UK despite setting up lives abroad. Even if the properties are rented out, owners are liable for the new tax. A government spokesman said visits would take place by prior agreement with the property owner and in line with official guidelines. “The public understands that we are addressing a long-standing unfairness, where a Band D home in Darlington pays more in council tax than a £10 million mansion in Mayfair. The Valuation Office has extensive experience valuing domestic property, and will use a wide range of evidence to determine bandings.”

title: Iran's currency hits record low as US prepares to hit Tehran with economic offensive
description: Rial trading at about two million to the dollar on Monday
content: Iran’s currency, which has recently been in freefall, hit an all-time low against the dollar, as the US prepares to announce crushing economic measures against Tehran on Monday. The Iranian rial was trading at about 2.02 million to the US dollar on the parallel market on Monday, according to Bonbast.com, which monitors unofficial exchange rates. That compares with 1.53 million rials to a dollar in early March, shortly after the war broke out. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has threatened Iran with an “economic D-Day”, saying Washington is entering the end game in the conflict. The US is planning “the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary”, he wrote in an article published on Monday in the Financial Times . He is due to hold a press conference at 9pm UAE time. US President Donald Trump warned last week that countries aiding Iran would face economic implications. He did not name any specific nations. Iran's rial has been under pressure since the war broke out on February 28, as the country struggles under the weight of existing sanctions and dropping exports. Last week, the country's central bank chief said Iran was exporting no oil, warning that access to foreign exchange reserves has become more difficult after being blocked by the US. “There is no doubt that we have restrictions on oil exports,” Abdolnaser Hemmati said on state television. The Central Bank of Iran governor said he had spoken to counterparts overseas and was told revenue from oil sales had “fallen to zero”. He added: “The same thing has happened to us and it is a reality that we are not exporting oil.” Iran is under growing economic pressure, with the war compounding inflation, currency weakness, energy shortages and sanctions, while damaging infrastructure and disrupting trade. The country's economy is expected to contract by 5.4 per cent this year, according to the July outlook from the International Monetary Fund. Inflation is projected at about 70 per cent for 2026.

title: Unstoppable Arsenal, Sangare's dazzling debut, Villa already in crisis? Five Premier League takeaways
description: Opening weekend brought drama and surprises as England's top-flight returned for 2026/27 season
content: The Premier League is back, and the nine games across the weekend provided shock results, plenty of goals and several talking points. If Arsenal started the season as strong favourites to retain their crown, then that feeling only grew as the weekend progressed. The Gunners swept aside promoted Coventry City 3-0 on Friday night and then sat back and watched as their rivals struggled. Manchester City eventually beat Bournemouth 2-1 thanks to some magic from substitute Rayan Cherki, but for the most part looked like a team with plenty of issues to resolve. The same goes for Liverpool, while Manchester United were even worse in their Saturday lunchtime 2-0 defeat at Hull City. Arsenal's stability and patient squad building paid off last season, and now looks even more valuable with so many of the Premier League's other leading clubs looking undercooked. The presence of Unai Emery and the optimal levels of performance he consistently draws from his players meant there was not much talk of Villa struggling this term. However, being walloped 4-0 at Brighton on the opening day really highlighted the chaos of their off-season. Villa have banked around £220 million selling Morgan Rogers , Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, but are now deprived of their talents and could yet lose Ollie Watkins (to Al Hilal) and wantaway keeper Emi Martinez before the window shuts. New faces have and will continue to arrive at the club, but it already looks a tall order to replicate the success of recent seasons. City eventually got the job done against Bournemouth, but Enzo Maresca's first teamsheet was an eye-opener. The Italian's decision to use Marc Guehi in midfield was particularly curious, and he was certainly missed in defence as Abdukodir Khusanov and Ruben Dias endured a panicky first half. Recognised central midfielders Mateo Kovacic, Nico Gonzalez and Matheus Nunes were all sat on the bench. The first two have been linked with moves away this summer, while Nunes is likely to come back into the side at right back. But, was Maresca sending a message that he is unhappy with his options? Ayyoub Bouaddi is on the way in, while it is well documented that Maresca would like to bring in Enzo Fernandez from his former club Chelsea. That will be one to watch in the final week of the transfer window. In the end, Liverpool will have been delighted to escape St James' Park with a 2-2 draw on Sunday in a game that highlighted many of the issues facing Andoni Iraola. Forward-thinking full-backs Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong create an imbalance in the team, and Newcastle ruthlessly exploited the space behind them. Liverpool's midfield was ragged and unable to cope with counter-attacks. It's easy to see why former player Jamie Carragher has been imploring them to sign a specialist holding midfielder who can plug the gaps when others are ahead of the ball. But perhaps even more concerning were the performances of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Isak continues to struggle for form and fitness since his acrimonious move from Newcastle , while Wirtz picked up where he left off last season – and not in a good way. For all his technical ability, the pace and intensity of the Premier League continues to unnerve the German international. Nine of the 20 Premier League clubs begin the season with new managers, but that won't stop more from making changes if results dictate. Eddie Howe will be waiting for a prime Premier League job, having left Newcastle in the summer. Could he end up at Manchester United if Michael Carrick struggles in his second season? Saturday's opening defeat at Hull was definitely concerning. David Moyes is in his final 12 months at Everton. What about Spurs? They were as bad as ever at Brentford, leaving Roberto De Zerbi unable to explain what was a disastrous opener for a big-spending club where failure is becoming ingrained. It's a fair bet Howe will be back in football before the season is through. The new season always means fresh imports, and the weekend was the first chance to have a look at some of them. Christos Tzolis continued his fine start to life at Arsenal with another strong display against Coventry.
