He also defended the earlier negotiations with Washington, describing the resulting memorandum as a major agreement reached with Iran’s “dignity” and “strength”. The sanctions could test Washington’s relationship with Beijing as much as its pressure on Tehran. China is Iran’s dominant oil customer, meaning measures targeting buyers, shipping companies or financial intermediaries could directly affect Chinese trade. Washington has urged Beijing to co-operate, while China has called for diplomacy and opposed unilateral pressure. For Iran, sanctions combined with restricted oil exports threaten deeper economic damage after months of conflict. For Gulf states, the continuing disruption of the Strait of Hormuz is exposing the risks of relying on a single maritime chokepoint for energy exports.

title: Ivan Toney hits hat-trick, Cristiano Ronaldo earns praise from Ange Postecoglou
description: Second round of Saudi Pro League fixtures sees familiar names among the goals
content: England striker Ivan Toney scored a hat-trick as Al Ahli thrashed Abha 4-0 to make it two wins from two at the start of the new Saudi Pro League season. It took Toney just five minutes to break the deadlock as he capitalised on some great work by new Armenian midfielder Eduard Spertsyan to sweep home. It was 2-0 in under 10 minutes as Galeno was chopped down in the box and Toney dispatched the spot-kick. The third arrived in spectacular fashion as Francisco Trincao scored his first goal in Saudi football. The Portugal winger picked up the ball 30 yards from goal and let fly with an unstoppable left-footed strike. Trincao then set up Toney for his third, with the Ahli striker powering home a shot after being fed inside the box. It was his sixth SPL hat-trick, and he now has 58 goals in 64 games since his move from Brentford. Elsewhere, Al Kholood scored three first-half goals and then held on to beat Al Taawoun 3-2. Scottish defender Jack Hendry scored the only goal as Al Ettifaq won 1-0 on the road at Al Fateh. On Friday, Cristiano Ronaldo got his season up and running with his 977th career goal as he came off the bench to help Al Nassr to a 4-0 win over Al Riyadh. Ronaldo was back in the match day squad for the first time since the World Cup and his recent wedding, but was named on the bench by new boss Ange Postecoglou . The 41-year-old came on in the 62nd minute with his side already cruising at 3-0 up, thanks to goals from Abdulelah Al Amri, Angelo Gabriel and Joao Felix. Ronaldo then scored a terrific goal as he collected a low cross and lost his man in one movement before sweeping the ball home. The effort moved him closer to the 1,000-goal milestone and was his 130th goal for Al Nassr in all competitions. “I said after last game that it was important for Cris to take his time to come back, because he was very, very busy obviously in the off-season,” Postecoglou said. “His mentality is he always wants to play, but he made sure he did all the right things – at training he worked hard – and it was fantastic for him to get 30 minutes today. “And he scores a goal, which just shows you the measure of the man.”

title: Tadej ⁠Pogacar makes winning start to Vuelta a Espana: 'Red is a nice colour'
description: UAE Team Emirates-XRG star dons leader's jersey after opening stage
content: Tadej ⁠Pogacar dazzled in ⁠Monaco by winning ​the first stage of the ⁠81st Vuelta a Espana on Saturday. The Slovenian, bidding to win the only Grand Tour to elude him, broke the heart of Britain's Ethan Hayter to win the 9.4km individual time trial by 0.09 seconds. Rolling down the start ramp out of Monte Carlo's glitzy ​casino, UAE Team Emirates star Pogacar tore ‌around the ⁠narrow and twisty ​course and made ​up ‌time late on to snatch ⁠the victory. Britain's Josh Tarling finished ⁠an emotional third fastest having decided to race eight days after the death of ​his brother Fin at the Volta a Portugal. For the 27-year-old Pogacar, it was his 36th Grand Tour stage victory, adding to the six Giro d’Italia and 26 Tour de France stage wins in his illustrious palmares. Returning to the Vuelta for the first time since his third-place finish as a Grand Tour rookie in 2019, he tops the general classification after the first day of racing. Pogacar said: “It’s a weird feeling to win the opening time trial by such a small margin. I was not expecting it. And this red is a really nice colour. For sure, I think I gained that 0.09 seconds when we passed in front of my apartment, because that was the most technical part of the course. I walk and cycle there every day. Even though it’s completely different in a race, knowing these roads super well helped me a lot today. “When I was going to the start line, I saw that Josh [Tarling] had the best time. I really wanted him to win today, I was rooting for him. Then I came to the intermediate, and I heard a different name, it was Ethan Hayter in front of me by three seconds. I gave it all, without taking risks. And I would really like to see Josh perform well in this Vuelta. “[Keeping the Red Jersey for three weeks] is going to be tough. Already tomorrow, some guys can break away or take it with bonus seconds. It’s going to be tight for the Red Jersey, and we can see some shuffling in the GC.” Elsewhere, UAE Team Emirates-XRG made a strong showing across the board in Monaco, with Jay Vine, Ivo Oliveira, and Joao Almeida all finishing inside the top 20. 1. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) 10:57 2. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) +0.09″ 3. Joshua Tarling (Netcompany INEOS) +4″

title: UAE-Russia trade and investment agreement comes into effect
description: Treaty expected to reduce barriers to market entry and enable movement of professionals
content: A trade and investment agreement between the UAE and Russia has officially come into force a year after it was signed, in a move aimed at boosting bilateral economic ties . It aims to increase collaboration across high-growth services sectors by establishing clear rules and protections for services trade and cross-border investment, the Ministry of Foreign Trade said. The trade in services and investment agreement (Tisia) will "reduce barriers to market entry, facilitate the movement of professionals and create a more predictable environment for businesses operating across both markets", the ministry said. It will focus on sectors including FinTech, healthcare, transport, logistics and professional services. The Tisia was signed on August 8 last year in Moscow during President Sheikh Mohamed's visit to Russia. "The entry into force of the UAE-Russia Tisia, alongside the economic partnership agreement with the EAEU [Eurasian Economic Union], represents the full activation of a comprehensive trade and investment framework that will unlock significant opportunities for businesses and investors in both nations," said Dr Thani Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister of Foreign Trade. The EAEU comprises five member states: Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia and Kyrgyzstan with a combined GDP of nearly $5 trillion. The UAE signed an economic partnership agreement with the EAEU in 2025 covering trade in goods at the regional level. Russia is a major economic partner for the UAE, with bilateral non-oil trade reaching $20.4 billion last year, a 77.7 per cent increase compared with 2024, the ministry said. The deal with Russia is part of the UAE's broader foreign trade agenda, which aims to increase non-oil trade to $1.1 trillion by 2031. The country is investing heavily in trade and logistics infrastructure, including modern seaports and airports to attract foreign investors. The UAE’s non-oil foreign trade surged 26 per cent annually to exceed $1 trillion for the first time in 2025. Non-oil exports during the year rose 45 per cent to $221 billion. To support its trade ambitions, the UAE has concluded 38 Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (Cepas) with countries around the world since the programme was launched in September 2021. The programme aims to reduce tariffs and remove trade bottlenecks through simplified customs procedures and rules. The Emirates has Cepas in place with India, Turkey, Jordan, Serbia and Vietnam, with 18 such deals currently in force. The latest to enter into force, on July 1, was the Cepa with Ukraine. Under the agreement, 99 per cent of Ukrainian imports of UAE goods and 97 per cent of Ukrainian exports to the Emirates will be exempt from customs duties with immediate effect. The deal is estimated to contribute $369 million to the UAE’s GDP and $874 million to Ukraine’s by 2031. Last month, the UAE also finalised a Cepa with Canada. The country also expects to conclude Cepas this year with Bangladesh, the EU, Peru, Ghana, Rwanda and Zambia.

title: Andres Iniesta excited by Gulf United project as Spanish great takes first steps into coaching
description: Former Barcelona star has taken charge at UAE second-tier side and wants to instill winning mentality at ambitious Dubai club
content: Andres Iniesta spent the defining years of his playing career at the very highest level of football. He was at the heart of one of Barcelona’s greatest sides, won nine La Liga titles and four Uefa Champions Leagues and scored the extra-time goal against the Netherlands to help Spain win their first World Cup in 2010. Now, at the age of 42, one of the greatest midfielders of his generation has chosen to step into coaching with Gulf United FC. The Dubai club is competing in the UAE First Division, one tier below the Pro League. Rather than begin at an established European club or wait for a more glamorous appointment, Iniesta has chosen a young club founded in 2019 whose project is built around developing players and giving them a pathway into professional football. At his unveiling on Saturday, Iniesta explained why the UAE had become the setting for his first foray into coaching and why he had chosen Gulf United. “It’s easy for me, for us as a family. We have been living here for three years. My last year I played here in the UAE,” Iniesta said, pointing to his time playing for Emirates Club. “When I got to know the people around the club, around the team, it was easy to decide that this is a very good place to start. The programme, the project is amazing. I love to work with young players, with talented players, and to help them improve.” There is also an awareness that this is the beginning of his education as much as theirs. Few players enter coaching with a playing CV as decorated as Iniesta’s, but he spoke repeatedly about the need to learn rather than assume his success on the pitch automatically translates to the dugout. “For me, as an individual challenge, it is amazing,” he said. “I also have to learn, I have to improve with my staff, with my players. It’s an amazing challenge for me.” The surroundings may be more modest than the stages Iniesta occupied for most of his career, but his ambitions are not. Asked what he expects from his first season, the Spaniard is keen to transmit the mentality he possessed as a player. “Expectations are always high. All my life I worked or I played for the best position, the highest position. This has to be our mentality,” he said. “Of course, it’s not easy. We have to work a lot because it’s the only way to be better, to improve. But I believe in our players. I believe in the mentality they have, the quality they have.” For Iniesta, though, the pursuit of results is as essential as the development of young players. Gulf United have placed youth at the centre of their ethos, and Iniesta believes veteran experience and emerging talent can complement one another. “Our mentality is to win, but I believe you are closer to winning when you are doing good things, the right things,” he said. “It’s not about luck. When teams win, it’s because they do many things well. Football is always about the mix. We are lucky because, speaking about the first team, we have a very good mix.” Iniesta was equally clear about the need for UAE clubs to place greater faith in Emirati players. Having plied his craft in Spain, Japan and the UAE, Iniesta resisted making direct comparisons between the different footballing cultures and instead argued that clubs need clear projects that allow local talent to develop. “The quality is good,” he said when asked about Emirati players. “The coaches, the teams, everyone has to trust in the players. Of course they have quality, but it is about what we want to do with our players. “I know professional football is always about winning, but each team or each club has to have a project about the local players because also it’s nice to see our players in our national team.” His message to the young players within Gulf United’s academy was similarly simple. Talent matters, but Iniesta believes opportunity is only useful when a player is capable of exploiting it. “Every day you have to dream,” he said. “You want to be a professional player, you have to dream about the best thing you can do and every day is very important. Not every team believes in the same thing as Gulf United believes in. This is one thing that is very important for you to know.” When one parent asked what single piece of advice he would give the club’s youngsters, Iniesta spoke of enjoyment of the game. “Enjoy and be ready to learn,” he said. “To be a professional player is very difficult. It’s very, very, very difficult. The only way is learn, improve and enjoy.” For Gulf United, there is obvious prestige in having Iniesta on the touchline. For Iniesta, the appeal lies in learning a new profession while attempting to create opportunities for players striving to develop. “Football one day can change your life,” he said. “But if you are not ready, it’s impossible for your life to change.”

title: Crew missing after cargo ship sinks off India
description: Vessel departed Paradip port on India’s east coast on Thursday carrying iron ore bound for Singapore
content: A Panama-flagged cargo ship sank off the eastern coast of India, leaving 22 of its 24 crew members missing and prompting a major search-and-rescue operation. The MV Ocean Winner was carrying 72,100 tonnes of iron ore fines when it sank about 445km from Paradip port in Odisha, the Indian Coast Guard said. The crew comprised 20 Chinese, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi. Two Chinese crew members were rescued from lifeboats, while a search for the remaining 22 was under way. The vessel had departed Paradip, a major port on India’s east coast, on Friday, carrying iron ore bound for China, according to an initial report prepared by India’s Maritime Administration. The ship lost contact with maritime rescue authorities on Saturday before sinking in the Bay of Bengal. The Coast Guard sent the ships Anmol, Varad and Vijay to the area, alongside Indian Navy vessels and aircraft, to assist with the search. The two survivors were recovered from lifeboats by the commercial vessel MT Isopos, according to Indian media reports. The pair said the vessel began listing on Friday and sank within eight minutes, forcing the crew to abandon ship, Shyam Jagannathan, director general of India’s Maritime Administration, told Reuters. Mr Jagannathan said the chances of finding survivors generally fall sharply after 12 hours, but rescuers were continuing the search. The Indian Navy said it was closely co-ordinating with the Coast Guard to locate the remaining crew. The Coast Guard sent two vessels from Sri Vijaya Puram, formerly known as Port Blair, a representative said. Government sources said the vessel sank about 445km from Paradip port. The cause of the sinking was not immediately known. Indian authorities have not said whether the vessel encountered severe weather, mechanical problems or other difficulty before it went down. Capt Alekha Charan Sahoo, deputy conservator of the Paradip Port Authority, said he was praying for the safety of the crew and hoping for the best. The vessel’s operator, Victory Star Group, contacted Indian authorities after communication with the ship was lost, according to Indian media reports. The ship’s ownership could not immediately be independently established.

title: E-invoicing is more than a compliance exercise for UAE companies
description: Initiative can alter how organisations generate, exchange and leverage transaction data
content: The UAE's e-invoicing programme is one of the most significant changes to the country’s tax and finance system. While many organisations view it primarily as a compliance requirement , that perspective significantly understates its importance. E-invoicing is not simply about digitising invoices or meeting a regulatory obligation. It is a business transformation initiative that will alter how organisations generate, exchange, manage and leverage transaction data. Businesses that approach it strategically will not only meet regulatory requirements, but also unlock greater operational efficiency, stronger governance and more informed decision-making. The Ministry of Finance has extended the deadline for appointing an accredited service provider (ASP) to October 30 for the businesses under phase 1 of the programme. However, the businesses that start preparing today will be in a far stronger position than those that wait until the final weeks before implementation. There are four key actions that UAE businesses should prioritise before the October deadline. The starting point for every organisation should be a comprehensive review of its existing technology environment. Many businesses operate multiple ERP (enterprise resource planning) platforms, billing systems and finance applications, often developed over several years or through acquisitions. E-invoicing requires these systems to work together seamlessly while delivering a significantly broader set of invoice data than many organisations currently maintain. Businesses should ask themselves several key questions: Conducting a detailed gap analysis now will help organisations identify potential issues before they become implementation challenges. The earlier these issues are identified, the easier and more cost-effective they are to resolve. One of the biggest mistakes organisations can make is assuming e-invoicing is solely a tax or finance project. In reality, e-invoicing touches almost every aspect of the organisation. Finance and tax teams may lead compliance efforts, but successful implementation also requires involvement from technology, procurement, legal, sales, operations and customer-facing functions. The impact extends well beyond reporting obligations. It affects how invoices are generated, how data is captured, how customer and supplier information is maintained, and how transactions flow across the organisation. For this reason, UAE businesses should establish executive sponsorship and a clear governance structure as early as possible. A transformation programme requires defined ownership, cross-functional collaboration and accountability. Organisations that take a business-wide approach will be better positioned to implement e-invoicing efficiently and maximise the long-term value it can create. Selecting an ASP should not be viewed purely as a technology or a procurement exercise. The right provider can become a long-term strategic partner, supporting not only implementation but also continuing compliance, future regulatory changes and the broader evolution of digital tax administration. Businesses should evaluate providers against several criteria: Organisations should also remember that every ASP may have slightly different functionalities regarding how invoice data is transformed, validated, and submitted. Making the right choice now can significantly reduce complexity throughout the implementation journey. One of the most overlooked aspects of e-invoicing is the value of the data it generates. Every invoice becomes a structured source of information. With the right approach, organisations can gain deeper insight into transactions, customer behaviour, operational performance and financial trends. However, the value of that insight depends entirely on the quality of the underlying data. Poor-quality information leads to poor-quality outcomes. Inaccurate, incomplete or inconsistent data creates compliance risks while limiting the organisation’s ability to generate meaningful information. Greater transparency, improved data quality, and more efficient invoice processing will ultimately benefit businesses, regulators and the wider economy. Organisations that embrace the change early will benefit. The upcoming mandate should therefore be viewed not as an obligatory checkpoint, but as the start of a broader transformation journey. Aamer Bhatti is indirect tax partner at EY Mena

title: Landmark Toyota building has been a home for thousands and a witness to Dubai's rapid expansion
description: The National's Daniel Bardsley reflects on his years living in tower set for demolition in 2027
content: Dubai’s Toyota building has earned its landmark status. This 15-storey block, which dates back to 1974, stands proudly in photographs of early Dubai, with Sheikh Zayed Road cutting its way through the almost empty desert. It was one of the city’s first towers, a starting point for a frenetic pace of development that would turn this stretch of road into one of the most dramatically built-up locations in the world. Soon it will be no more; the building’s owner, the Nasser Rashid Lootah Group, has confirmed that it will be demolished next year. But for me and for thousands of others over the decades, the Toyota building is much more than a milestone in the history of Dubai: it has been a home. It was my home for about three years after I moved to Dubai in late 2004. By then, the building had already been emphatically eclipsed in height, glamour and comfort by the dazzling skyscrapers of Sheikh Zayed Road, but its relative modesty was a factor in my living there. The room, rented from a friendly Egyptian man called Hossam, who lived in the flat with his Filipina wife, was inexpensive and included all bills. The location was another reason as the building, standing next to Interchange One on Sheikh Zayed Road, was a short taxi ride from the offices where I worked at the time. With its tiled flooring, basic furniture and threadbare curtains, the room (like everything else in the Toyota building) was decidedly no-frills, but it was spacious and I was conscious that I was living in relative luxury compared to many Dubai residents who could afford only a bed space. Although my landlord and his wife were the only people in the building I tended to chat to, the diversity of the Toyota building’s residents (and the fact that very few other westerners lived there) was part of the appeal. This city within a city was a microcosm of Dubai, with Indian, Pakistani, Arab and Russian residents who all called it home. In the three years that I spent in the building, I don’t think I ever saw another westerner. My room had air conditioning, but it was courtesy of an extremely noisy wall-mounted unit that I don’t think I ever kept on overnight, preferring to use the large ceiling-mounted fan instead. On weekdays, I typically restricted use of the air-con to the final few minutes before I left the building to go to work. Taxis were always prowling the area, and I would have to wait only a minute or two before a cream-coloured Toyota Camry or Nissan Altima would swing by to take me the short distance to the office. On the ground floor of the building, there was a small shop selling food, stationery and sundry items, run by an elderly man. I used to visit regularly to buy fruit and biscuits. Inside, the lobby was as unpretentious and functional — even shabby — as the rest of the building, but thankfully, the lifts were almost always working. Aside from all the practical benefits, one of the key pluses of my home was the setting: my room opened on to its own small balcony with a stunning view down Sheikh Zayed Road, looking towards the Dusit Thani Dubai and the other shiny high-rises. Sheikh Zayed Road never slept, although in the early hours of the morning, the daytime hordes of traffic mercifully faded to a trickle. Lacking a car when I lived in Dubai, during summer weekends I would sometimes spend the day in my room reading, venturing outside only in the relative cool of the evening, perhaps to take a bus to Satwa and its Indian restaurants, or to walk down to Jumeirah and the Mercato Shopping Mall. The service roads beside Sheikh Zayed Road were also good to wander along after dark, always buzzing with people and having plenty of cafes and inexpensive restaurants within walking distance. Even if I stayed at home, there was always something to see from my balcony. It might simply be the traffic heading for Jumeirah, or it might be one of the cream-coloured minibuses trundling along to collect Emirates cabin crew from one of the five medium-rise buildings on the opposite side of Sheikh Zayed Road. Like the Toyota building, these residential blocks appear in early photographs of the area. At the time I moved into the Toyota building, the area of Sheikh Zayed Road immediately south of interchange one was, by Dubai standards, relatively undeveloped, but that was to change. Emerging from the desert was what was to become the world’s tallest building, the Burj Khalifa, and I had a grandstand view of its construction from my flat’s bathroom window. I rather regretted not taking a photo of progress every week or fortnight, as it would have created an impressive time-lapse set of images of the building work. From late 2007, having taken a job with The National before its April 2008 launch, I commuted to Abu Dhabi in a rental car before moving to the capital. This almost caused my time in the Toyota building to have a nasty sting in the tail, because once extreme rainfall flooded both the car park and my rental car (a Toyota, of course). Had the vehicle been ruined, I would have been financially liable, but fortunately the hire car company, after I explained what had happened, charged me just a few hundred dirhams for cleaning. As I upped sticks for Abu Dhabi, it was not without regret that I moved out of the building: It had provided a fine vantage point from which to view Dubai and its endless activity and growth. So, when the wrecking ball does its work next year, I am sure I will not be the only past or present resident of Dubai to feel a pang of sadness at the loss of this much-loved building.

title: My Dubai Rent: Nurse-turned-consultant pays Dh690,000 a year for five-bedroom Al Barsha villa
description: Australian Dubai resident has modified her rental property
content: My Dubai Rent takes you inside a reader’s home to have a look at what they get for their money, how much they pay in rent and asks them what they like and don’t like. Click here if you would like to take part in the series and show us why your home is so special. Sarah Donaldson – known professionally as Nurse Sarah Louise – pays Dh690,000 a year for a five-bedroom villa in Al Barsha. Ms Donaldson, an Australian former nurse who now runs her own consultancy for aesthetic clinics called The Business Injection, lives in the main house with husband and two children, while her team operates out of a detached majlis alongside a four-car, air-conditioned garage that the couple had built. The National takes a look around. The situation pushed us into moving. I was looking to either get a separate office building and keep the house that we had, or put the budget together and get a bigger house with an office that was detached from the house. We've converted the majlis – it's a traditional outer building – in to a registered business address, with room for staff, a kitchen and, eventually, we're going to knock two rooms through to make it more of an open workspace. We've gone from Dh350,000 to Dh400,000 to Dh690,000. We lived at The Villa – that's quite an expat community, mixed with locals, more modern houses, bigger properties – five-bedroom, private pool. We lived out there for a year, but the location is too far – we do a lot of work in the city. So we moved to Al Barsha 1, right behind a park. We have a two-year-old. She was only one at the time so it was nice just to have a park next to us. And then, this third year [in the UAE], we've come into this one. We like Al Barsha, we like the location, and we like the privacy of having a full villa. We have quite a small family, but for people that want to visit when they're overseas, you've got the extra bedroom space. And we spend a lot of time in our home. I know a lot of people say: “Oh, you move to Dubai to be in the warmer weather and be outdoors,” which is true – it's almost like the UK in the winter. In the summer, we stay in the UAE, where generally we don't leave because our work doesn't stop. We work internationally so Christmas time, realistically, is the only time that we get off. You get your private pool [and] the biggest thing is the plot size. The house is five bedrooms plus two lounge rooms, a separate dining, another separate small sitting room, en suites in every bedroom, which is normal, but they're double the size. And you have the size to be able to do modifications. We've done all the media walls, all the built-ins. The baby's room has been wallpapered. The curtain bill was ginormous with floor-to-ceiling windows throughout. The garage was our biggest modification. We built that from scratch. It's a four-car garage with aircon. We will modify the pool and put a pergola outside. We will also put in a carport, because it's boiling hot for cars that don't have cover. My husband's quite friendly with the owner, and we were allowed to make all the changes we want to the house. We're here for three years minimum. We put up cameras. We built a garage. We're a dream tenant. And that's why he said: “Go for it – do whatever you want.” We've made it more “us” just by putting in the furniture that we like, colour co-ordinating things. We have animals, so the animals obviously have their little bits in here. And just making it warm: lots of rugs, lots of colours. We're just getting our artworks put up now. There's a little park they've just built for the kids – AstroTurf, an air-conditioned room. We're six minutes from Dubai Hills Mall, nine minutes from the Palm, four minutes to JVC Circle Mall. All the schools are here – we're just at the back of all the main ones. My 16-year-old is in online school, so it doesn't matter, and the two-year-old is at a nursery back in Al Barsha 1. We buy investment properties – smaller ones that you can rent out and get a bigger yield from. In these types of homes, we don't believe in buying to live. We invest our money in businesses and things that give us rental return quite quickly. But if we could buy this property tomorrow, we would – because we love the area. And especially if you've paid off three years of rent, that would go towards the cost. But when you're looking to rent somewhere stable and make it home, it's just about finding a landlord that will give you the longevity.

title: Premier League: Hull and Ipswich grab opening weekend headlines as Everton ease to win
description: Promoted duo seal superb wins over Manchester United and Sunderland on Saturday
content: Hull City and Ipswich Town, both newly promoted from the English second tier, both secured headline-grabbing victories on the opening weekend of the Premier League season. In Saturday's early game, Hull powered to an impressive win over Manchester United who were looking to start the new campaign with a bang after last season's third-place finish and Uefa Champions League qualification. But Michael Carrick's side looked well off the pace from the start against Hull – who won the Championship play-off final against Middlesbrough in May to seal promotion – with the home side sealing all three points thanks to first-half goals from defensive duo Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy at MKM Stadium. “It's just one game, we're disappointed we haven't won,” Carrick insisted. “It's not more than that, it's not less than that. We've got to soak it up and come back stronger.” The Tigers 2-0 victory was their first ever top-flight win against United in their first Premier League game since 2017. “It means a lot, we were organised, and it was very good for us,” said manager Sergej Jakirovic. “The players stick to a tactical plan. We suffer because we play against Manchester United but we punished the opponent.” Ipswich Town, who finished runners-up in the Championship last season to seal their place back in the top-flight, were also savouring victory on Saturday night after beating Sunderland 2-1. Substitute Jack Clarke scored an 90th-minute winner against his former club to earn the Tractor Boys all three points at Portman Road against a team that finished seventh last time out and qualified for the Europa League. Ipswich had taken a first-half lead when Julio Enciso superbly set-up fellow summer signing Emersonn for a simple tap in only for Sunderland to level when a curling Nilson Angulo free-kick went in via the crossbar. But it was to be Clarke's day as the player who left Sunderland two years ago in a deal worth £20 million curled home the winner from just inside the penalty area. "You can see how hard it is to win Premier League games, we need to find a way to win enough of them to make it a successful season," said Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil after his first match in charge. Sunderland manager Regis Le Bris admitted his team might have been suffering from a spot of early-season rustiness. “It is often the case. It is not unusual,” he said. “Today it was massive because of the consequence but this is the Premier League, it is ruthless.” Everton won their Premier League opener for the first time in five years after beating Crystal Palace 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Goals from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry either side of half-time secured the points as Palace manager Pierre Sage suffered defeat in his first match in charge. “Finish as high a possible,” said Everton midfielder Hayden Hackney when asked about the team's aims this season. “In the European spots hopefully, it's a long season and it will be difficult but that's the aim.” The Eagles – who have won the FA Cup , Community Shield and Europa Conference League in the last two seasons – were missing last season's top-scorer Ismaila Sarr with the Senegalese attacker linked with a move to Turkish side Galatasaray, having already lost manager Oliver Glasner and defender Maxence Lacroix during the summer. “Different tactics, same formation but a different way of playing,” said Palace defender Chris Richards when asked about the team's differences under Sage compared to Glasner. “Pre-season we saw a lot of different things, new players coming in. Today was a good line in the sand regardless of the result.” Glasner, meanwhile, saw his reign as Nottingham Forest manager start with a defeat as Anton Stach's free-kick earned Leeds United victory two minutes from time at the City Ground. Forest have turned to Glasner after sacking four managers in less than 12 months with Nuno Espirito Santo, Ange Postecoglou, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira all heading for the exit after being dismissed by owner Evangelos Marinakis. Glanser will know there is plenty of work ahead to improve a team that finished 16th last season and sold key midfielder Elliot Anderson to Manchester City during the summer. "Well, it was the game I expected," said Glasner. "The one situation that will decide and one set-piece will decide. It was a game with very rare chances. Really disappointed, but this is what we have to expect today." It was a welcome win for Leeds manager Daniel Farke who has been well backed in the summer transfer window with the Yorkshiremen spending more than £80m on new players. “I always back my players and Anton Stach always has those moments, I expected a difficult game away at Forest,” said Farke, whose team face Forest again in the League Cup on Tuesday. “I'm very happy to come away with a clean sheet and compliments to the players.” On his new signings, the German coach added: “Very happy because they have big boots to fill.”

title: US imposes 50 per cent tariffs on Canada
description: Canada announces retaliatory duties after trade talks fall apart
content: The US imposed 50 per cent tariffs on $20 billion (Dh73.4 billion) worth of Canadian products, in the latest escalation of the trade rift between the historic allies. The import taxes that came into effect on Saturday will apply to hundreds of products from Canada , such as plywood, liquor, electrical equipment and hockey gear. Canada said it would retaliate "dollar for dollar", with Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing that new duties on US goods would take effect from September 8. "In the coming days, we will release details of these new tariff ​measures, ‌measures, which ⁠will ​come into ​force ‌the Tuesday after ⁠Labour Day," Mr Carney said. US President Donald Trump announced the 50 per cent levy on Canadian goods in July, with a deadline of August 19, but he paused the tariffs hours before they were set to take effect. The three-day pause led to last-ditch negotiations for what would have been a salve to the strained trade relations between the two countries. In a statement, Mr Carney blamed Washington for the breakdown, saying “last-minute changes in the US proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal”. He said he suspended talks and directed Canada’s negotiating team to return to Ottawa. US trade representative Jamieson Greer blamed Canadian negotiators and said the team made last-minute demands that overturned the terms of a draft deal worked out over days of negotiations. “Despite the US offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk-backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days,” Mr Greer said. The new tariffs are being imposed under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, a provision that has never been used. The law gives the President the power to impose duties on countries considered to be discriminating against US commerce. The two sides had been discussing a deal that included lowering tariffs on certain Canadian steel and aluminium to 25 per cent, cutting duties on Canadian cars to 15 per cent and eliminating a 10 per cent lumber tariff. But the new levies won’t apply to the most important natural resources the US imports from Canada, such as oil, potash and critical minerals. Canada is the US’s most important foreign supplier of crude oil and petroleum products — more than 4 million barrels per day. If these tariffs remain in place, Canada could lose almost 90,000 jobs, University of Calgary economist Trevor Tombe told Bloomberg . The impact is most sharply felt in machinery and electronics, plastics and rubber, furniture, wood, paper, and chemicals and cosmetics, he added. BC, Ontario and Quebec would be the worst-hit provinces, he said. While the ​new measures affect a relatively small share of Canadian ​exports, about 5 per cent, ‌they add to existing US tariffs on steel, lumber and autos. ⁠ The combined pressure could slow Canada's fragile economic recovery and affect broader negotiations for a free-trade pact between the neighbours. Mr Carney said on Saturday that retaliatory duties could be placed on US goods in industries including steel and dairy. Further details have yet to be announced. The recent escalation has affected negotiations to renew the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Mr Trump declined to renew the treaty earlier this year. The new duties apply regardless of whether Canadian goods qualify for preferential treatment under the ​trade agreement, which has shielded much of Canadian industry from earlier US tariffs. Mr Carney said, "The retaliation escalates the trade conflict and calls into question the future of a North American trade pact between the United States, Canada and Mexico that is crucial to industry in all three countries."

title: Lando Norris produces 'best lap of my life' to seal Dutch GP pole with title-race leader Kimi Antonelli third
description: Defending F1 champion will start from front of grid at Zandvoort after as McLaren driver looks to build on Hungary triumph last time out
content: Lando Norris secured pole position for Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix after producing what he called “the best lap of my life” during qualifying at Zandvoort. The teenage McLaren driver, who triumphed last time out in Hungary before the Formula One summer break for his first win of the season , will start at the front of the grid alongside George Russell with his Mercedes teammate and title-race leader Kimi Antonelli third. Norris pipped Russell by 0.102 seconds just as rain started to fall at the seaside track as the Briton also secured his second successive pole after doing the same at the Hungaroring a month ago . “Well done, best lap of my life,” he said on the team radio after claiming first place in the Netherlands. Earlier, Russell had won the sprint race after leading from start to finish leaving him third in the drivers' championship, three points behind Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and 56 shy of Antonelli. “I'm a little surprised honestly,” said Norris following the end of qualifying. “A decent lap, I was pushing because you've seen how close it is, one hundredth, two hundredths can make a big difference in the end. “A good turn around from earlier today when I felt like we struggled a bit. We certainly felt very strong. The team did a good job so credit to them on trying to get a little bit more out the car and it certainly helped me today. “I'm looking forward to the race tomorrow. This is always one of the best events. Hopefully we can put on a good show.” Antonelli, meanwhile, admitted it had been “a difficult session” as the 19-year-old Italian – who turns 20 on Tuesday – had to settle for second row on the grid, alongside Norris's McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri. “Overall, always found myself on the back foot,” he said. “Last lap did a mistake in turn one, lost a couple of tenths, it was my mistake. Shame for that, we had a real shot for pole. “In Q3 I thought we had a shot, we had a chance. When I started the last lap in Q3, I was too tense down in sector one. I thought this is going to be difficult. I was able to make it up the rest of the lap. It's a shame for that but it's all to play for tomorrow.” For Russell, it had been a good day after following up his sprint win with a front-row spot on Sunday. “Lando did a great job so congrats to him and McLaren, said the Briton. “It was a strong session. I thought we had it in there just to fight for pole but P2 I'm pretty satisfied with, especially after coming back after such a tough last few races before the break. I'm sort of getting in my groove again and I'll try to fight with them again tomorrow. “I feel in a good place and I just sort of feel myself again, which is really important. It was really nice to drive around here and these cooler temperatures made the track feel really fast, so it was a real joy for us all to drive and I'm looking forward to the race.” Seven-time champion Hamilton will start in fifth alongside Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc, with the Red bull pair Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson seventh and eighth, respectively. “We changed quite a bit [since the sprint] and it didn't make a difference, pretty much the same pace that we've had all weekend,” said a frustrated Verstappen, who signed a new contract with Red Bull this week. “It didn't allow me to push or feel comfortable with the car.”

title: Hull City v Man United ratings: Mendy 7, McBurnie 9; Santos 4, Mbeumo 6
description: Tigers stun Red Devils by winning Premier League opener 2-0 at MKM Stadium
content: Newly-promoted Hull City produced a shock on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign by defeating Manchester United 2-0 at MKM Stadium. First-half goals from defenders Nobel Mendy and Semi-Ajayi earned Hull, who were promoted via the Championship play-offs last season, a thoroughly deserved victory in what was their first English top-flight match since 2017. Hull's Bosnian manager Sergej Jakirovic set his team up with a back five that completely nullified United's attack, even with the second-half introduction of Marcus Rashford who was making his first appearance for the Red Devils since December 2024 following loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona. Jakirovic had vowed ahead of the game to silence his team's critics who have dismissed the Tigers as relegation cannon fodder and he did that in style by brushing aside a team who finished in third place last season. On Friday night, Championship title winners Coventry City had been well beaten by Arsenal, with the defending champions winning 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium. But there would be no such result for Hull, who finished sixth in the second tier but defeated Middlesbrough in the play-off final to earn promotion. Next up for Hull is a League Cup second round match away to to Stoke City on Tuesday followed by a Premier League trip to Coventry next Saturday. Michael Carrick's United side will look to pick themselves up when they face Everton on Merseyside in the league next Sunday. Hull City captain Louis Coyle: “The noise speaks for itself. Before we went to bed last night we couldn’t have dreamt it any better. It'll be a shock to people, I’m not saying it’s how I thought it would go, but this team’s got something special in terms of character, resilience, and we know what we’re doing. “We know we’re going to get chances on the break. You’re against a fantastic side and we know that’s the minimum it’s going to take. So, so proud of the boys for what we achieved last year. We’re not just here to make the numbers up – we’re here to stay in this division. What an incredible start for the boys.” Man United captain Bruno Fernandes: “Same mistakes as we did last season every away game. We give too much of the ball to them, in the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball, too much time. We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays – we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals. “We understand the frustration [of supporters], every season at the start we want to compete and win every game but we need the fans on our side, and to believe in ourselves.” Konstantinos Tzolakis – 8/10: Greek international goalkeeper called into action with regulation early saves from Mbeumo and Cunha. Next big stop didn't arrive until 77th minute when he denied Mbeumo again. Very assured on debut. Nobel Mendy – 7/10: Club-record signing looked shaky early on, bizarrely allowing one cross to bounce in box gifting chance to Mbuemo. Headed home Hull's second goal in style. Limped off injured in second half. John Egan – 8/10: Experienced defender was last man standing when both his central-defensive partners – Mendy and Ajayi – were forced off in second half. Stood firm against everything United's array of attackers threw at him. Semi Ajayi – 8/10: Big defender thumped Hull into lead with close range finish after Lemmens kept out McBurnie effort. Was Tigers' first Premier League goal since May 21, 2017. Also came off due to injury. Lewis Coyle – 8/10: Hull's captain sent over superb early cross from right that almost saw McBurnie open scoring. Became third Hull player to come off injured, earning a thoroughly-deserved standing ovation from home fans after usual committed display. Matt Crooks – 7/10: Midfielder picked up first-half booking for foul not long after Hull went 2-0 up. Almost clean through on goal after superb Belloumi ball over top but denied by Lammens coming out of goal to sweep up. Regan Slater – 8/10: Superb whipped-in free-kick earned assist for Mendy's goal. Relentless in his pressing of opposition. Impressive shift. Ryan Giles – 8/10: Produced two crosses in matter of minutes in first half that almost led to goals, one ending in McBurnie header being saved, the other almost flying straight into net. Crossing was constant threat. Elliot Stroud – 7/10: Making his debut on the left, Sweden international looked comfortable on the ball from start. A solid first game for 24-year-old summer signing from Swedish top-flight side Mjallby. Mohamed Belloumi – 7/10: Tricky Algerian winger was tripped on edge of box by Tielemens with resulting free-kick resulting in goal. Curled long-range effort over bar. Some flashes of real quality and quick feet who could be an exciting player this season for Hull. Ollie McBurnie – 9/10: Hull's play-off final goal hero saw header saved before goalkeeper Lemmens then somehow kept out his close-range shot that saw Mendy score from rebound. All-action performance from Scottish striker that included skipping past three United challenges in one second-half surge forward. Lucas Herrington (On for Mendy, 63') – 7/10: Teenage defender, who played in World Cup for Australia, came on for debut after moving from MLS in summer. Didn't put foot wrong. Paddy McNair (On for Ajayi, 64') – 7/10: Former Man United defender brought on as Hull lost both goalscorers to injury and slotted straight into what was an impressive Hull defensive performance. Liam Miller (On for Stroud, 70') – 7/10: Canadian winger tarted career at United's fierce rivals Liverpool and helped Hull seal all three points. Booked for late dive. Cody Drameh (On for Coyle, 70') – 7/10: Inches from making it 3-0 minutes after coming on as he drilled low effort just wide of post. Matt Targett (On for Giles, 85') – N/A . Senne Lammens – 6/10: Diving save from McBurnie just before 15-minute mark, then tipped over a shot from Adam two minutes later. Then again from McBurnie before the Tigers opening goal from one of the many crosses slung in. Noussair Mazraoui – 5/10: Top defending at the back post after four minutes to head a ball away from Hull’s first attack, yet United were twice undone with goals from set plays and the Moroccan twice gave the ball away. Harry Maguire – 6 /10: Great cross just before half-hour but Dorgu couldn’t quite get on to it. Ran behind defenders against his former club and was the team’s main attacking threat. Ayden heaven – 5/10: Chastening first half when two Hull central defenders both scored. McBurnie had the better of him in the build-up to the opening goal. Inexperience was exploited. Luke Shaw – 5/10: High ball into Hull’s box which Mbeumo met after 12. Vital defending stopping Belloumi down right and tried to get wide to give United width. Booked. Andrey Santos – 4/10: Ineffective United Premier League debut for the Brazilian, who gave up possession and fouls too easily. United had 72 per cent of possession but most of that came after the team were 2-0 down. Youri Tielemans – 5/10: Too many poor touches in a first half where Hull won more tackles and duals. Nutmegged in first half and gave away a foul which led to a free-kick and the second goal. Disappointing debut. Patrick Dorgu – 4/10: Squezed a ball through Egan’s legs towards goal, had a tussle with the goalkeeper and almost got on to a Maguire cross. All within the first 30 minutes. Booked for a yellow card challenge on Crooks. Often the most advanced player, yet limited influence on the game. Bruno Fernandes – 5/10: Little space to create and his team simply couldn’t generate proper chances. Desperate shot on target just before hour. Crosses to nothing. Usually inspires. Not today. Bryan Mbeumo – 6/10: Had first proper effort on target and he was United’s main threat in the first half. Saw bicycle-kick towards goal blocked but United were poor up front and created little. Leaned back and curled a shot well over on 75, then ran and had strike saved two minutes later. Matheus Cunha – 5/10: Quiet and of little threat. Played centre-forward and had one shot on target. Dropped deeper in a congested forward area where United struggled to create proper chances. Marcus Rashford (On for Dorgu, 46') – 6/10: First minutes in red since 2024. Positive, direct start and linked better with Shaw than Dorgu had done. Good ball to Sesko with 10 minutes left. Kobbie Mainoo (On for Tielemans, 67') – 5/10: Played one poor, square pass which led to a Hull attack. Lacking match fitness. Benjamin Sesko (On for Santos, 67') – 4/10: He scored 10 in 15 final games last season and gave United a belated focal point, but did little with it. United had 39 crosses. And most were easily dealt with. Diogo Dalot (On for Mazraoui, 81') – N/A. Shea Lacey (On for Cunha, 81') – N/A.

title: Iran gives permission for Iraqi oil tankers to pass through Strait of Hormuz
description: Agreement reached during Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf's visit, Iranian media says
content: Iraqi President Nizar Amidi on Saturday said Iran had granted permission for several Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, after repeated requests from Baghdad as the waterway remained disrupted by the regional conflict. He spoke during the eighth Baghdad Dialogue conference , saying Iraq was among the countries most exposed to the impact of the conflict because of its dependence on oil exports and economic links with Iran. “There is facilitation for some tankers carrying Iraqi oil in the Strait of Hormuz,” Mr Amidi said, without providing further details. Iran's state news agency, IRNA, reported separately that Tehran had given permission for several Iraqi oil tankers to cross the waterway after repeated requests from Baghdad through various channels. The special permission was one of Baghdad's main requests during Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's recent visit to Iraq, IRNA said. Iraq has faced difficulties transporting its oil because it does not have its own tankers, Mr Amidi said. “We have a problem transporting oil due to the absence of a national tanker,” he said, adding that developments in the Strait of Hormuz had consequences for the entire world, not only Iraq. Mr Amidi added that Iraq would seek to stay out of the war between Iran and the US, warning that Baghdad would be among the countries hardest-hit if the conflict escalated. “We will be among the countries most affected after Iran if the escalation continues, given the economic interdependence and our complete reliance on oil,” he said. On internal security , Mr Amidi said Baghdad would not allow Iraqi territory to be used to launch attacks against other countries. He said attacks from inside Iraq against countries in the region “have no justification”, as Baghdad seeks to prevent the country from being drawn further into the conflict. Mr Amidi repeated Baghdad's vow to bring all weapons under state control , saying armed groups must ultimately hand over their weapons through an Iraqi-led process. The government has set September 30 as a deadline for bringing weapons under state authority, although some Iran-backed factions continue to resist the move.

title: Malcom seals surprise move to Al Jazira after Al Hilal contract terminated
description: Winger switches Riyadh for Abu Dhabi after three seasons in the kingdom
content: Brazilian winger Malcom has completed a surprise move from Al Hilal to UAE Pro League side Al Jazira. The 29-year-old revealed his switch on social media on Friday before any official announcement had been made by the 21-time Saudi Pro League champions. Hours later, Al Hilal's official statement confirmed they had agreed to terminate Malcom's contract bringing an end to his successful three-year spell in Riyadh. His arrival represents a major coup for the Abu Dhabi club who started their new campaign with a 2-0 win at Hatta last Sunday having finished last season in fourth place, 24 points shy of champions and double winners Al Ain . Jazira are now managed by former Al Ain, Shabab Al Ahli and Sharjah coach Cosmin Olaroiu after the Romanian's brutal exit from the UAE national team job in May. Malcom joined Al Hilal from Russian outfit Zenit St Petersburg in 2023 and would go on to make 139 appearances for the capital club, scoring 47 goals and assisting a further 41. He helped Hilal win the SPL title in his first season – scoring 15 goals along the way – and would also lift the King's Cup twice as well as the Saudi Super Cup on two occasions. Sao Paulo-born Malcom started his career at Brazilian side Corinthians before moving to Bordeaux in France where he would establish himself as a firm fan favourite, with his stunning long-range finish against Dijon earning him the Ligue 1 goal of the season award in 2017/18. He spent three seasons with Bordeaux – scoring 23 and assisting 24 in 96 appearances – before his form caught the eye of Spanish giants Barcelona, then managed by Ernesto Valverde and whose squad included the attacking talents of Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez and Ousmane Dembele. The Catalan club forked out €41 million for the right-winger who joined on a five-year deal but would spend just one season in Spain which would see him make 24 appearances across all competitions, as Barca claimed the La Liga title and reached the Uefa Champions League semi-finals. Malcom would also score his first Champions League goal – against Inter Milan in the group stage – and came off the bench at half-time in Barca's Copa del Rey final defeat against Valencia. In the semi-final win over Real Madrid, Malcom scored his debut Clasico goal as Barca drew the first leg 1-1 at Camp Nou on the way to a 4-1 aggregate victory. He would soon be on his travels again, this time heading to colder climbs in the Russian Premier League for €40m. It would be a trophy-laden spell with Zenit – when Malcom scored 42, supplying a further 24 in 109 games – that saw them win three league titles, one Russian cup and four Russian Super Cups before moving to the kingdom in a €60m deal. Malcom had become the latest high-profile SPL arrival, joining Senegal defender Kalidou Koulibaly, Serbia midfielder Sergej Milinkovic-Savic and Portuguese midfielder Ruben Neves at Hilal. He would later be joined by countryman Neymar but his fellow forward endured a miserable, injury-ravaged spell in Riyadh. Malcom's SPL career would end with a goal as he scored Hilal's second as they started the new season with a 4-2 win at home to Al Faisaly. His two Brazil caps came in 2023, having first been called-up into the squad for the 2018 friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Argentina without playing in either. Malcom secured an Olympic gold medal in 2020 after scoring a brilliant extra-time winner for Brazil in the final against Spain in Tokyo. Malcom made his senior debut coming off the bench to replace Rodrygo for the final eight minutes in the 4-1 friendly win over Guinea – Vinicius Junior scored the final goal from the spot after Malcom had been fouled in the box – before earning his only national team start as Brazil lost to 4-2 Senegal three days later.

title: Saudi Crown Prince visits France to sign deals and discuss Strait of Hormuz
description: Prince Mohammed will meet French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday
content: Saudi Arabia and France are expected to sign deals and discuss alternative routes to the Strait of Hormuz during Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s visit to Paris. The Saudi Crown Prince left the Kingdom on Friday evening for a trip to France to enhance transport, health and security ties. He was to meet French President Emmanuel Macron . The leaders were expected to discuss ways to diversify transport routes for energy and logistics, including maritime routes, as well as alternative pipeline and regional rail projects, the French leader's office told reporters. The visit “reflects the vitality of the dialogue between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and France and will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the strategic partnership between our two countries,” the Elysee Palace said. Mr Macron and the Saudi Crown Prince would, for the first time, convene a meeting of the Franco-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council, according to the statement. They were also set to oversee the signing of agreements covering technology, transport, energy and health. The Saudi delegation comprises seven ministers. The leaders were also expected to discuss conflicts in the Middle East involving Israel, Palestine, Lebanon and Syria, where France is working to help develop energy and logistics projects, according to the officials. Prince Mohammed's visit comes at a time when tension is high in the Middle East as the war between the US and Iran continues. On Monday, Prince Mohammed is expected to meet French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu. “The high-level meeting provides an opportunity to address key bilateral and international issues, whether economic, security-related or diplomatic,” the Prime Minister's office said. The leaders will also attend the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup on Sunday, the first time the event is being held in Paris. The event was created and hosted in Riyadh in 2023 as part of the country's Vision 2030 project. On his last visit to France in 2023, the Crown Prince met Mr Macron and attended a reception as part of Riyadh’s successful bid to host the 2030 Expo. Mr Macron's last visit to the Kingdom was in 2024. Relations between Saudi Arabia and France are strong, with cultural ties deepened by Paris's involvement in the development of the kingdom's historic AlUla region.

title: UAE three-day weekend: Why families are skipping travel as couples and friends head out
description: Back from their summer break, families to stay at home for long weekend ahead of the return to school
content: While the coming holiday to mark the Prophet Mohammed's birthday gives UAE residents a long weekend, travel agents say not everyone is rushing to the airport, with back-to-school preparations limiting family trips. There is, however, increasing demand for travel among couples and friend groups. The Prophet Mohammed's birthday is on the 12th day of Rabi Al Awal, which this year falls on August 25 of the Gregorian calendar. However, the public holiday has been set for Friday, August 28, resulting in a three-day weekend for both the public and private sectors. According to Hasa Al Harthi, head of corporate and leisure at DW Travel, travel demand from families is "limited". "We are seeing a slightly different travel pattern for the upcoming August long weekend, as it falls just before the return to school," she said. "Family demand has been relatively limited, with more bookings coming from couples and groups of friends who have deliberately avoided the peak summer period." Raja Mir Wasim, manager at International Travel Services (ITS), has also observed the same trend for the coming holiday, with an increasing number of couples and groups of friends taking trips. "Although demand for travel hasn't been affected, it has been priority-driven since families have taken their holidays earlier and it is now people without children who are travelling," Mr Wasim said. As travellers search for convenient breaks that maximise the extra day off, destinations offering easy access, competitive pricing and minimal travel hassle are proving especially popular. DW Travel's data showed that, for shorter trips, there was growing interest in Phuket, the Maldives, Istanbul and Montenegro, with visa access playing an increasingly important role in last-minute travel decisions. "Montenegro recently introduced visa-free access for eligible UAE residents, making it particularly attractive for a spontaneous European break," said Ms Al Harthi. She added that some residents were planning to use the extra day to extend their European holidays into September, taking advantage of better shoulder-season pricing and weather. Mr Wasim said that tourists were also booking trips to Thailand, China, London, Trabzon and South Africa. "People are now extending their three-day holidays and making them into five- to seven-day trips," he said. ITS is still receiving inquiries concerning last-minute travel bookings. "However, most people booked packages two weeks ago when the holiday was announced," Mr Wasim said. Ms Al Harthi said it was not too late to find a good deal, but that being flexible around destinations, airports, and flight times was key because return flights on the popular Thursday evenings and Sundays would naturally carry a premium. She added that domestic holiday options continued to appeal to residents seeking convenient, cost-effective breaks during long weekends. “UAE staycations remain a great option for travellers who want to make the most of the long weekend without the cost or travel time of flying overseas, making the most of the great summer staycation offers available in the market,” Ms Al Harthi said. More and more people in the UAE are turning to destinations beyond Europe for their holidays, as visa issues, rising costs , and the desire for new experiences change how people travel. The travel experts agree that easy access to visas plays a big role when people decide on a destination. Visa-free entry, visas on arrival, or simplified visas on arrival are available at many destinations for UAE residents, regardless of their passports.

title: Turkey seeks Interpol red notice against Netanyahu over Gaza aid flotilla case
description: Move is part of a case against 35 people over a violent Israeli raid on activists of the Global Sumud Flotilla
content: Turkey has requested Interpol red notices against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and another suspect, as part of a domestic criminal case related to a violent raid against activists on board the Global Sumud Flotilla. Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said arrest warrants had been issued for Mr Netanyahu and another person on charges including genocide, crimes against humanity, torture, property damage and hijacking of means of transport. The move is part of a case against 35 people over the Israeli offensive in international waters. Interpol has not indicated whether it has accepted the request. Mr Netanyahu is already wanted under an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court in November 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza. An Interpol Red Notice is a request to law enforcement authorities worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender, or similar legal action. It is not an international arrest warrant. Istanbul's 11th High Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Mr Netanyahu and the other suspect on July 14. Reports said Afek Moskovitch, an Israeli army lieutenant alleged to have been involved in the destruction of the Turkish-Palestinian Friendship Hospital in Gaza, was the other suspect. Mr Gurlek said judicial proceedings were continuing over the alleged armed intervention against civilians delivering humanitarian aid to Gaza in international waters and the detention of activists. He said the arrest warrants had prompted the Justice Ministry to ask the Interior Ministry to seek Interpol Red Notices for the two suspects. The documents were also forwarded to the Foreign Ministry. “We will not allow the crimes committed in Gaza to be covered up or those responsible to be protected by a shield of impunity,” Mr Gurlek added. “We will resolutely use all means available under national and international law." The Global Sumud Flotilla, also called the Gaza Flotilla , is a civilian mission seeking to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza. It set sail from the Turkish port of Marmaris on May 14 with dozens of boats carrying more than 400 activists from about 40 countries. Israeli forces intercepted the vessels in international waters on May 18-19, about 460 kilometres from Gaza, and detained all 429 people on board, according to organisers. Most were deported to Istanbul on May 21. It was the sixth flotilla to set sail for Gaza since the start of the war in the enclave, which was sparked by the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023. After returning home, several participants alleged they had been beaten or otherwise mistreated in Israeli custody. An Australian activist, Juliet Lamont, said she was dragged, beaten and sexually assaulted, and described the four-day detention as “absolute hell”. Another, Sam Woripa Watson, said he suffered a fractured rib and saw activists being tasered and hit with rubber bullets. These claims were denied by Israeli authorities.

title: From 1997's Grand Theft Auto to GTA 6: The evolution of gaming’s biggest crime series
description: A look at the games that drove the franchise from cult hit to global phenomenon
content: When the first Grand Theft Auto arrived in 1997, there was little indication that the top-down driving game would evolve into one of the defining series in entertainment. Developed in Dundee by DMA Design, the studio that would later become Rockstar North, the game offered something unusually permissive. Players could steal cars, work for criminals and abandon their objectives to simply cause havoc around the city. That freedom became the foundation of GTA. Grand Theft Auto 3 transformed it into a three-dimensional open world; Vice City and San Andreas demonstrated how distinctive those worlds could become; GTA 4 pursued greater realism; and GTA 5 , supported by more than a decade of GTA Online , grew into one of the most successful games ever made. Ahead of GTA 6 , here is how the series reached that point. Before GTA became the gaming behemoth it is today, it was a project called Race 'n’ Chase . DMA Design initially imagined a game in which players could take the role of criminals or police officers, before discovering that playing the criminals was considerably more entertaining. The finished game contained three locations that would become central to the series: Liberty City, San Andreas and Vice City. Missions were collected from ringing telephone boxes and the action was viewed from above, but GTA's essential formula was already there: provide players with a city, vehicles and objectives, then give them considerable freedom in how they approached them. The controversy surrounding its violence also established another recurring part of GTA 's history. Criticism from politicians before its release helped draw attention to a game whose provocative premise was already part of its identity. GTA briefly left America with London 1969 , an expansion that transplanted the original game's top-down formula to a caricature of 1960s Britain, complete with period cars, music and local slang. A smaller follow-up, London 1961 , was released as a free PC download later that year. Together, they remain anomalies in GTA history. No subsequent instalment has been set primarily outside the US, while their period detail anticipated the way games such as Vice City would later use music and culture to define an era. Grand Theft Auto 2 refined, rather than reinvented, its predecessor. It retained the overhead viewpoint but introduced a more developed gang system, with completing jobs for one faction potentially damaging the player's standing with another. Its industrial setting, Anywhere City, also stood apart from GTA 's later reliance on fictional versions of recognisable American locations. It was the final main instalment built around the original top-down format. This was the game that changed everything. Released for PlayStation 2 in October 2001, Grand Theft Auto 3 transformed the series into a fully three-dimensional open world. Players controlled the largely silent Claude as he moved through Liberty City's criminal underworld, but the plot was almost secondary to the novelty of inhabiting the city. Cars could be stolen almost anywhere; police responses escalated with the player's wanted level, and missions could be interrupted simply because something more interesting was happening nearby. Radio became equally important. Licensed songs sat alongside talk shows, fictional advertisements and satire, helping turn time spent driving between missions into part of the experience. Its influence reached far beyond GTA . Large 3D worlds built around missions, exploration and emergent chaos became one of the dominant structures of 21st-century gaming, with GTA 3 providing an early blueprint. Only a year later, Rockstar showed that an open world could have a personality as distinctive as its characters. Set in 1986 and influenced by Miami Vice , Scarface and the excesses associated with Florida in the 1980s, Vice City replaced Liberty City's greys with neon, beaches and an expansive licensed soundtrack. That soundtrack became one of the game's defining features. Songs from artists including Michael Jackson, Iron Maiden, Blondie and A Flock of Seagulls played across its radio stations, helping reinforce the period setting and making simply driving around Vice City feel more immersive. It also introduced GTA 's first fully voiced protagonist, Tommy Vercetti, played by Ray Liotta. His rise from recently released prisoner to criminal kingpin gave the story a more cinematic structure. Motorcycles, purchasable properties and revenue-generating businesses expanded the formula further. The results were enormous. Vice City sold 1.4 million copies within two days and became the best-selling game in the US in 2002. It ultimately sold more than 17 million copies across platforms. If Vice City gave GTA personality, San Andreas gave it scale. Carl “CJ” Johnson returns to Los Santos in the early 1990s after his mother's murder, but the game soon expands far beyond one city. Rockstar created an entire fictional state encompassing Los Santos, San Fierro and Las Venturas, inspired by Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las Vegas. Its ambition grew with the map. CJ could eat, exercise, gain or lose weight, improve weapon skills and customise his appearance. Players could gamble, modify cars, take over gang territory and explore the countryside between cities. San Andreas also became one of the defining games of the PlayStation 2 era. Its size, freedom and sheer range of activities encapsulated what made the console's library feel so ambitious at the time, helping cement the PS2 as a must-own system. The console would eventually sell more than 160 million units worldwide, making it the best-selling games console of all time. Liberty City Stories was an ambitious attempt at a portable GTA . Released initially for the PSP , it returned to the three-dimensional Liberty City of GTA III and followed Leone crime family member Toni Cipriani in 1998. Rather than substantially redesigning GTA for hand-held play, Rockstar attempted to reproduce much of the console experience on a portable device. A PlayStation 2 version followed the next year. Rockstar repeated the idea with Vice City Stories , a prequel set in 1984. Protagonist Victor Vance begins as a soldier before becoming drawn into the city's criminal economy, while an empire-building system allows players to establish and manage illegal businesses. It was the final original GTA built around the technology and design foundations established by GTA 3 , closing a remarkably prolific period for the series. Seven years after GTA 3 , Rockstar reinvented Liberty City again. GTA 4 launched in April 2008 for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, beginning GTA's HD era. Liberty City was denser and more closely modelled on New York, while new physics and animation gave vehicles and characters considerably more weight. The story also became more grounded. Niko Bellic, an Eastern European immigrant arriving in the US looking for opportunity and answers about his past, gave Rockstar a way to examine immigration, capitalism and the gap between the American dream and reality. About 3.6 million copies were sold on its first day, generating approximately $310 million. Within a week, sales had reached about six million copies and more than $500 million. Rockstar then used the same city for two substantial expansions. The Lost and Damned followed biker Johnny Klebitz, while The Ballad of Gay Tony centred on Luis Lopez and nightclub owner Tony Prince. GTA 5 's defining structural change was to divide its story among three playable protagonists. Michael De Santa is a retired career criminal living unhappily in luxury; Franklin Clinton is a younger hustler looking for greater opportunities; Trevor Philips is a volatile criminal living outside Los Santos. Players can switch between them, sometimes during missions, giving the game a variety of perspectives, personalities and styles of play that previous GTA stories could not offer. That structure also helped to keep the experience feeling fresh long after release. Moving between Michael's family problems, Franklin's ambitions and Trevor's unpredictable criminal life allowed Rockstar to tell different kinds of stories within the same world, while character-specific missions and abilities gave each protagonist a distinct feel. Los Santos also returned on a far larger scale, surrounded by mountains, desert, small towns and coastline. Released on September 17, 2013, GTA 5 generated about $800 million on its first day and passed $1 billion after only three days, making it the fastest any entertainment product had reached that figure. Its extraordinary longevity owes much to Grand Theft Auto Online . What began as its multiplayer mode grew into a vast live-service game built around property, businesses, vehicles and co-operative heists. Rockstar continued expanding it for more than a decade, carrying Los Santos across three console generations and adding new missions, businesses, locations and storylines. By August 2026, GTA 5 had sold more than 230 million copies worldwide. The continued success of the game and GTA Online helped to create a 13-year gap between numbered instalments, by far the longest in the series' history.

title: Meloni and Aoun hold talks amid race to prevent security vacuum in southern Lebanon
description: Italy is planning to help replace UN peacekeepers in the country when deadline expires in December
content: Growing concern over the possibility of a security vacuum in southern Lebanon was at the centre of discussions between Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in Rome on Friday. The UN's peacekeeping force in Lebanon, Unifil, is set to withdraw from the country by December 31, 2026. Mr Aoun and Ms Meloni spoke about “Italy’s role in consolidating security and stability in the south” of Lebanon, the Lebanese leader's office said on social media, and “the period following the end of the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon”. Italy – which has the biggest contingent of EU soldiers in the peacekeeping mission – and France are planning to establish another force along with several European countries , backed by Nato, to take over Unifil's role. The US and Israel, which is fighting the Hezbollah militant group in southern Lebanon, have opposed the plan and proposed instead a US-led force. Mr Aoun wishes to press on with the EU-backed force, working alongside the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF). Mr Aoun thanked Ms Meloni “for the support Italy provides to Lebanon at various levels”. “They also discussed the general situation in Lebanon, particularly in the south, in light of the continuing Israeli attacks and the need to pressure Israel to comply with the implementation of the framework agreement reached during the Lebanese-American-Israeli negotiations in Washington,” his office said.
