Meanwhile, senior officials from the Makkah pact countries, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, are to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional co-ordination. Saudi Arabia is represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman , and Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir. The Turkish head of intelligence Ibrahim Kalin will also join the talks. Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Rayed Krimly, said on X the visit was aimed at de-escalation and finding diplomatic solutions to the crises in the region. The planned discussions will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia came under escalating attacks from the Houthis. يرأس صاحب السمو الملكي الأمير خالد بن سلمان بن عبدالعزيز آل سعود، وزير الدفاع، وفد المملكة للاجتماعات التي تستضيفها العاصمة الإيرانية طهران اليوم بين دول اتفاقية مكة للدفاع المشترك مع المسؤولين من الجمهورية الإسلامية الإيرانية. وذلك بمشاركة المشير/ عاصم منير، رئيس أركان الجيش… — AMB Dr. Rayed Krimly (@Rayedkrimly) October 26, 2026 Qatari media reported that a delegation from the country was in Tehran on Sunday. Greek PM visits Riyadh Saudi Arabia and Greece have pledged to strengthen security and defence co-operation and expressed concern over attacks on energy infrastructure, according to a joint statement issued after Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis visited Riyadh. Earlier, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman received Mr Mitsotakis at the Royal Court in Al Yamamah Palace, where they held talks. The two sides highlighted the importance of their strategic partnership and the implementation of joint initiatives. Bilateral trade reached about $1.7 billion in 2025, up from 2021 levels, said the statement, which was carried by the state-run Saudi Press Agency. Riyadh and Athens pledged to accelerate co-operation on a planned electricity interconnection project linking Saudi Arabia to Europe through Greece, as well as explore clean hydrogen exports from the kingdom to European markets, the statement added. The leaders stressed the need to protect international maritime routes and ensure uninterrupted energy supplies, expressing concern over attacks on energy infrastructure. The countries also committed to strengthening co-operation in defence, cyber security, counter-terrorism and the sharing of intelligence, as well as in artificial intelligence, transport, tourism, education and health.

title: Asian Cup 2027 to go ahead as planned in Saudi Arabia
description: AFC release schedule for tournament that will run from January 7 to February 5 in kingdom
content: The 2027 Asian Cup will go ahead as planned in Saudi Arabia, with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) confirming the tournament ⁠schedule and venues on Monday. The tournament will kick-off on January 7 with Saudi Arabia taking on Palestine at Riyadh's ‌King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The 24-team continental championship will run until February 5, ⁠with the opening match and final both ​scheduled ⁠to take place at the King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The tournament will take place across eight venues in three cities – Riyadh (five), Jeddah (two) and Al Khobar (one). The UAE are in Group E and begin their Asian Cup campaign against Vietnam on January 11 at the Imam Mohammed Bin Saud University Stadium in Riyadh. Their next group game is against Yemen on January 15 at Riyadh's ‌King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The UAE conclude their group phase against South Korea on January 20 at the Imam Mohammed Bin Saud University Stadium. Defending champions Qatar will begin their title defence against Thailand on ​January 11, while Japan ‌open their campaign ⁠against Indonesia the ​same day. title: Abu Dhabi esports team Red Dunes takes top prize in prestigious Street Fighter tournament
description: Four-player team defeats GTW in London to secure $60,000 and a place at next year's world championship in Japan
content: Abu Dhabi esports team Red Dunes has won the Street Fighter League championship for the Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia region, defeating some of the world's leading players to secure a place at next year's international finals in Japan. The team claimed the title on Saturday at the MCM Comic Con London, held at the Excel centre in the British capital. Red Dunes beat GTW 70-30 in the grand final of the Street Fighter 6 competition. The victory earned the Abu Dhabi team $60,000 from the tournament's $100,000 prize pool and a place in the Street Fighter League World Championship in Tokyo next March. For Abu Dhabi-raised player Adel Anouche , better known as Big Bird, the result was particularly significant as it was the team's first championship under the Red Dunes name. "This win means a lot to me because it's our first win with our organisation, Red Dunes esports, and SFL is known to be a tournament to crown the best team!" he tells The National . "It's definitely ranked high for me. Truly best way to showcase our Abu Dhabi, UAE home team." Street Fighter League differs from traditional fighting game tournaments by placing competitors in four-player teams, with victories contributing towards an overall score. This year's EMEAA competition brought together 24 players across six teams representing Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Red Dunes entered the playoffs as the second seed after finishing the regular season behind GTW. Its roster comprised Anouche; Jordanian Amjad Al Shalabi , known as AngryBird; Norwegian veteran Arman Hanjani, known as Phenom; and Swede Joel Sundell, who competes as Juicy Joe. Hanjani has been competing internationally for more than a decade, finishing third at Capcom Cup in 2019. Sundell reached the semi-finals of Capcom Cup 11 last year, defeating Al Shalabi along the way. Red Dunes defeated YESports 60-20 in the semi-finals before overcoming GTW in the championship match. Anouche led the comeback after an early deficit, securing two important victories using the character C Viper. Sundell contributed a win against Bravery, while Al Shalabi sealed the championship by defeating Zhen with Akuma. Anouche admits the competition initially left him uncertain about his team's chances. "I even thought we had a low chance of winning after seeing all the teams, but I guess I was wrong and underestimated our team," he says. The championship adds to the achievements of Anouche and Al Shalabi, childhood friends who grew up in Abu Dhabi and are known collectively as The Birds. Al Shalabi won the Street Fighter 6 championship at Evo in Las Vegas in 2023, while Algerian-born Anouche has finished as runner-up twice at the prestigious fighting game tournament. The pair's international reputation was apparent at Tokyo Game Show last month, where they drew crowds of Japanese fans during a meet-and-greet. Anouche believes their success reflects the strength of the Middle East's fighting game community, which developed partly through the region's arcade culture. "Even though the quantity is not there, the quality is definitely present in our players," he says. "With enough dedication and discipline, I'm sure we'll see a lot more champions coming out of Middle East." Saturday's result marks the roster's third consecutive regional Street Fighter League title. At the world championship, taking place at Tokyo's Ryogoku Kokugikan from March 10 to 14, they hope to improve on two previous unsuccessful attempts. "Our next goal is to win SFL world finals. We were able to get a shot at it twice but never made it happen, hopefully 3rd time is the charm now," Al Shalabi says. The team has adopted the slogan "Third Impact" for its latest attempt at the world title.

title: Burnham’s first budget is caught between debt, defence and an ageing Britain
description: The Prime Minister knows his government cannot tax and spend its way out of what is a national predicament
content: That the UK has run out of money for its needs must be the grim realisation that underpins the national budget this week. There are signs that the new Chancellor of the Exchequer, John Healey , is indeed ingesting this message – yet Mr Healey must go further to level with the country. The national debt hit £3 trillion ($4 trillion) last week. The budget is expected to lay out the need to borrow more than £330 million in the year from April. Meanwhile, the government is spending more than £100 million repaying debt every year. These grim statistics come at time of already increased taxation. In the coming months, previously announced new taxation is already expected to bite on both wealth and profits. After a number of years when income was targeted, the latest measures tap out the money people own, on top of earnings. The result so far is an exodus of high earners and increasing signs that certain types of jobs are no longer being created because the cost of paying taxes on labour is deterring businesses from adding to the workforce. For example, consider the coincidence of two pressures on the bank sector revealed last week. The speculation about a higher bank tax, to capture the proceeds of higher interest rates, is rife. Barclays, one of the country’s largest banks, said it will reduce its headcount by 5,000 to reflect the changing needs of embedding AI in its system. Another straw in the wind: there were an estimated 645,000 people aged 90 years and over in the UK last year, an increase of 55 per cent since 2005. The tax changes already set to come in before Wednesday’s budget also target this portion of the population. Any unused pensions of those who die over 75 will be heavily taxed from now on. The diagnosis for the UK is complicated by just where the tax proceeds are going. The country is spending heavily on those in need of the sick and others needing welfare. By contrast, other government services such as education are being slimmed down by necessity. The big elephant in the room is that the government must spend more on defence. This is largely because wars are seen as encroaching fast on the UK’s global space. Mr Healey knows this because he resigned as the defence secretary in the previous government, under Keir Starmer, over its failure to fund defence. The crimp on how to contain spending has not been resolved. Instead, a tax drive that doesn’t seem to fit with the British way anymore – such as inspecting private property to assess if it is worth £2 million, and therefore, eligible for extra taxes – is gaining momentum. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has framed his challenge as a 10-year programme to transform the country. The approach he wants to take is having the state mobilise its assets for the public good. To make a break with tax and spend, as he does this, would entail leading a radical government. No wonder Mr Burnham sees the need for stealth in these early days. He is barely three months into the job. There is a danger in not tackling spending or addressing how to accommodate an ageing population and a workforce shaped by changing technology. Those are the strategic needs that are not being addressed right now. Having a first budget is a moment of asserting its authority for a new government. It is true that the Labour party, under its previous leadership, was dedicated to balancing its books at a time when economic growth was faltering. As Mr Healey reduces his headroom between forecast-borrowing and revenues, he will know how difficult that literal balancing act has become. For Mr Burnham, the lessons are clear. There will need to be a dedicated defence build-up in the years to come. Alongside this, he has a legacy priority of ensuring state-provided long-term care for the elderly, such as those swelling numbers of nonagenarians. The only way to fund that is to return directly to raise taxes on earnings. To secure a mandate for those measures, he will need his message of hope to generate faster growth and – more importantly – win an election with a commitment to do so. Until that point, he will remain caught in a political trap where he can’t address the big questions. And the country’s strategic traps will remain glaringly exposed.

title: Alpha Dhabi commits $1bn for global AI investments
description: Investments through Alpha Wave III fund to target high-growth AI companies
content: Alpha Dhabi Holding , a subsidiary of the Abu Dhabi-listed International Holding Company, has signed an agreement to commit $1 billion for investments in artificial intelligence companies around the globe. Investment Holding Company is to invest through the Alpha Wave Global-managed fund Alpha Wave III, which also seeks to target high-growth companies, it said in a statement on Monday. Alpha Dhabi will deploy the committed capital over time, in line with “capital calls and the fund’s investment programme”, the company said in a filing to the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, where its shares trade. Returns from the Alpha Wave III fund will be dictated by the performance and valuation of the underlying investments, with value expected to be realised through distributions and exits over the life of the fund. The investment commitment is in line with the company’s growth strategy and “broadens Alpha Dhabi’s access to artificial intelligence and innovation-led opportunities”, said Hamad Al Ameri, managing director and group chief executive of Alpha Dhabi. “This investment supports our portfolio diversification objectives and our focus on long-term value creation.” Building on commitment The latest commitment builds on Alpha Dhabi’s 2022 investment of Dh9.2 billion ($2.5 billion) in Alpha Wave Ventures II. The fund, launched by Chimera Capital and Alpha Wave, received a capital contribution of Dh2.6 billion and undrawn capital commitment of Dh6.6 billion to be drawn down over time for investments in growth-stage companies globally, the company said at the time . Through the venture fund, Alpha Dhabi has gained indirect exposure to companies including SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic. Alpha Dhabi intends to fund the investment in Alpha Wave III from the recycling of its cash distributions from Alpha Wave Ventures II and existing resources. “The financial impact will be recognised over time, reflecting the timing of capital deployment and the performance,” Alpha Dhabi said on Monday. Established in 2013, Alpha Dhabi manages a portfolio of more than 250 public and private investments, spanning 45 countries. It invests in companies in high-growth sectors, including AI and technology, real estate, industry, construction, health care, energy and hospitality. In August, Alpha Dhabi doubled its shareholding and capital commitment in its private credit joint venture with the emirate’s sovereign wealth fund, Mubadala Investment Company. Under the revised partnership agreement, the company boosted its capital commitment in Micad Credit JV to $1 billion. It also raised shareholding from 20 per cent to 40 per cent in Micad, which manages about $1.7 billion in assets across 45 portfolio companies, Alpha Dhabi said at the time. In May, Abu Dhabi's Ta'ziz signed a deal with Alpha Dhabi, targeting $10 billion in capital investment in its new industrial chemicals ecosystem in the emirate. The two companies said at the time that they were conducting a joint feasibility and market study, and the move remained subject to final investment decisions and regulatory approvals.

title: Which airlines are flying to Riyadh? Latest schedules and cancellations
description: Some flights resume, as Saudia and Riyadh Air use alternative airports and several UAE airlines maintain suspensions
content: Travel to Riyadh remains disrupted after Yemen’s Houthis claimed they launched another strike on King Khalid International Airport on October 25, hours after Saudi authorities announced flights had resumed. Flightradar24 showed a small number of flights departing the airport on Monday, although most scheduled departures were cancelled. The kingdom's national carrier Saudia is operating some of its Riyadh-linked services through Dammam and Al Qassim, about 400km north-west of the capital. Riyadh Air has shifted several international routes to Al Qassim. UAE airlines Etihad Airways, Emirates, flydubai and Air Arabia have maintained flight suspensions or cancellations on routes to the Saudi capital. For passengers planning to travel to the Saudi capital, here’s what to know. Which UAE airlines have suspended flights to Riyadh? Etihad has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until November 5. Emirates airline services from Dubai to Riyadh are currently scheduled to resume on November 8. But the planned return dates are subject to change. Meanwhile, flydubai has cancelled services to Riyadh through October 29. Air Arabia’s services from Sharjah to Riyadh also remain suspended, with no date announced to resume those flights in the airline's latest update. Where are Saudia flights operating? Saudia says some of its Riyadh flights are operating through Al Qassim and Dammam airports. Tickets include a bus transfer arranged by the airline between the airport and the Saudi capital. Passengers should check their booking and the airline’s instructions to confirm which airport they will use and the arrangements for their bus transfer. Which routes is Riyadh Air operating? Riyadh Air says that until further notice it is operating only to and from Cairo, Dhaka, Jeddah, London Heathrow, Lahore and Islamabad, all through Al Qassim airport. Passengers departing from Riyadh can check in at the InterContinental Durrat Al Riyadh hotel and take a complimentary bus to Al Qassim airport. The airline says the journey takes about four and a half hours. Hotel check-in opens eight hours and 15 minutes before the flight is set to depart and closes six hours and 30 minutes before it takes off. Passengers can also make their own way to Al Qassim airport, where the airline advises arriving at least three hours before departure. Does Riyadh airport reopening mean normal flights have resumed? No. King Khalid International Airport announced the reopening of two terminals from October 25, with Terminal 1 designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international services operated by Saudi airlines. Passengers with confirmed bookings have been asked to contact their airline before heading to the airport. Some flights have taken off, but cancellations continue and airline arrangements vary. Passengers should confirm whether their flight will operate and which airport will be used, rather than relying solely on a published schedule. What should passengers do before travelling? People should check their flight directly with their airline, confirm their departure and arrival airports, and monitor messages about changes to their booking. Anyone using an airline-arranged bus transfer should confirm the meeting point and departure time, allowing time for the journey. Those with onward connections should ask their airline about arrangements if travel disruption affects their itinerary. Passengers whose services have been cancelled should contact their airline or booking agent to discuss rebooking or refund options.

title: Dubai announces lane closures on Emirates Road from Monday to clear the way for self-driving taxi tests
description: Three lanes opposite Al Maktoum International Airport will be closed to traffic during peak hours for six days
content: Dubai will partially close a stretch on one of the emirate's main motorways during peak hours this week, to enable tests of self-driving taxis to be carried out. Vehicles will be barred from using three lanes on Emirates Road, also known as E611, opposite Al Maktoum International Airport, the Roads and Transport Authority said. The rules will apply between 9am and 4pm daily from Monday, October 26, until Saturday, October 31. Al Maktoum International Airport Tunnel will be fully closed during this period to allow the autonomous vehicle trials to take place. Authorities called on motorists to plan their journeys in advance and follow road signs to ensure smooth travel. Autonomous strategy takes shape The road closures further highlight Dubai's commitment to integrating rapidly evolving autonomous technology into its road infrastructure. In September, the emirate's government launched a cutting-edge testing centre where future fleets of autonomous vehicles will be geared up for the demands of the emirate's busy road network. The Dubai Mobility Labs – based at Dubai Silicon Oasis – features a vast multipurpose area including testing tracks where self-driving technology can be safely put through the paces before being approved for public use. The high-tech centre has been established by the RTA in partnership with the Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority and is a key step in the emirate's drive to make 25 per cent of all journeys autonomous by 2030. Dubai Mobility Labs provides a controlled environment to simulate a wide variety of traffic scenarios, alongside real-world testing on public roads extending from Dubai Silicon Oasis to Al Qudra. Self-driving vehicles will be assessed under diverse operating conditions to examine their ability to respond to challenging traffic and weather across 248 test scenarios. The testing ground is critical to check sensing and decision-making systems, to assess the capacity to adapt to evolving road situations, and to ensure vehicle readiness before modes of transport progress to trials on public roads and move to full operations. The Dubai Mobility Labs has already held successful trials of autonomous driving technology and vehicles developed by global companies, including WeRide, Pony.ai and Tesla. Driving progress Meanwhile, new research has shown that the vast majority of UAE motorists are ready to embrace autonomous transport - even as other parts of the world remain more reluctant. The study by Bain & Company, a global consultant company, found 90 percent of people in the UAE would consider purchasing a self-driving vehicle. The survey of more than 12,000 people placed the UAE just behind Indonesia (93 per cent) and India (91 per cent) but ahead of China (84 per cent), Europe (47 per cent) and the US (40 per cent). Hitting the road Uber Technologies started operating Baidu's Apollo Go driverless service in its Dubai network in August, with plans to introduce thousands of the autonomous vehicles in the emirate. The service, which will use Baidu's sixth-generation RT6 robotaxi , will initially be available in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, with plans to expand. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed , Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, launched a self-driving taxi network in the city in February. Sheikh Hamdan inaugurated the commercial operations of the Chinese-made Baidu Apollo Go self-driving cars and took a trip in one of the vehicles to attend the World Governments Summit. In September last year, Dubai announced that a 15 square kilometre testing zone for self-driving taxis, delivery and other service vehicles would be established in Festival City and Dubai Creek Harbour to evaluate how autonomous transport can work on a larger scale.

title: Israel's opposition in final show of force before elections as tens of thousands rally in Tel Aviv
description: Demonstrators call for Benjamin Netanyahu to be voted out of power – amid reports of stand-off between government and military
content: Supporters of Israel's opposition took to the streets of Tel Aviv at the weekend in a final show of force before polls open on Tuesday, in what many observers are calling the most important elections in the country's history. Tens of thousands of demonstrators flocked to the upmarket neighbourhoods of the city as opposition figures made the case that the country’s future was at risk if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won yet another term in office. Four years of his ultranationalist government has plunged the country into wars across the Middle East, deepened internal divisions and fractured Israel's reputation abroad. Mainstream polls have predicted for months that the opposition will gain more seats than Mr Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc, which relies heavily on the most extreme wings of Israel’s settler movement and the ultra-Orthodox community. But neither side is predicted to have a majority, raising the prospect of weeks of complicated negotiations to form a coalition. Mr Netanyahu would remain as a caretaker prime minister during that time. There are fears that the Israeli leader might use such a deadlock to his advantage. There is also the prospect of renewed fighting with Iran before the elections take place, as Mr Netanyahu escalates his rhetoric on social media. On Sunday, there were reports in Israeli media of a stand-off between Mr Netanyahu and the military's leader described as an "unprecedented confrontation" at the top of the Israeli state. Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir resisted carrying out Mr Netanyahu's instructions for unspecified military action in recent days, fearing it would provoke Iran to launch an attack on Israel before polls open, broadcaster Channel 12 reported. “If Benjamin Netanyahu wins again, I’m genuinely scared for this country. I don’t think I have a future here,” Romy Schlegel-Cohen, 17, told The National in Hostage Square on Saturday evening, as she handed out campaign flags to passers-by. Organisers of the rally, who are calling for a state commission of inquiry into the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023, said 100,000 people attended. Some had dressed up, one as Mr Netanyahu with a Pinocchio nose, others as repairmen with tools, symbolising the need to fix Israel. “I can’t vote yet, but I want to be able to show people who can vote that what they’re doing is important – they’re voting for me,” Ms Schlegel-Cohen said. “Change is needed right now. It was needed long ago. If I can convince even one person, it’s enough.” Hostage Square, next to the Tel Aviv Museum of Art and the headquarters of the Israeli military, is a fortress for the anti-Netanyahu protest movement. Soon after Hamas attacked southern Israel in 2023, the area hosted regular protests calling on the government to secure the release of those taken hostage. Since the last Gaza ceasefire was announced last year, that movement has grown to call for a state commission of inquiry, the highest level of investigation in Israel, into how the catastrophic security failure came about. Mr Netanyahu’s far-right government has consistently opposed such an investigation. Ofri Bibas, the sister-in-law of Shiri Bibas, who was killed along with her two young children in Gaza after being taken hostage during the October 7 attacks, told The National that she wanted the elections to be about the day her family members were abducted. “No one who was in a position of power on October 7 should still be in their job. The Prime Minister and the government should have resigned on the day,” she said. “The thing that’s most difficult for me to understand is the hypocrisy. If any other prime minister had been in position on October 7, they would never have considered staying in their job. Just because it’s Netanyahu doesn’t mean he can’t be replaced, or that Israel can’t continue without him. After 20 years, we have to look for something new, for a change and for a better life.” On Sunday evening, the man most likely to realise such hopes for new leadership, Gadi Eisenkot , drew hundreds of people to a large hall in the north of the city. Supporters of his Yashar party say that only an opposition victory can rehabilitate Israel’s position in the world. Support has plummeted since the outbreak of the Gaza war and escalating settler and military violence in the occupied West Bank. Mr Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, is not opposed to Israeli settlements and has condemned what he described as a “handful of thugs” when talking about the violence in recent months. He lost close relatives in the Gaza war and has vowed to end it if he wins, without setting out a detailed plan. “These are the most dramatic, important and historic elections of all time in Israel,” Lianne Pollak-David, a candidate on Yashar’s electoral list, told The National. “Gadi Eisenkot is not only a top-notch strategist, not only a very brave leader, but simply the kind of person who can unify the country, who can bring us back to where we should be: a model nation among the family of nations. “My message to the Arab world is clear: we’re here for regional integration and we’re here to expand the Abraham Accords. We’re here to drive Israel and the region to be a much more secure, stable and prosperous place. We need to be working together − all the moderate forces. Israel should be at the forefront of that effort. “If we continue with Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership, it will lead us to being a pariah state.”

title: Saudi coalition strikes Sanaa, Jordan arrests church attack suspects and iPhone Duo buyers complain

content: In today’s episode of Trending Middle East , the Saudi-led coalition carries out strikes on Yemen’s capital Sanaa, saying it destroyed Houthi ballistic missile launch sites used to attack Riyadh.
